stages.title: Stage 1
stages.task: Talk to Darnes in the villager camp.
hints: Darnes: This is no place for Wynn natives. This is a Villager-Troll war.
Darnes: Oh, well. Actually, we do need a human to assist us. It would help us avoid conflict at all.
Darnes: The filthy but thick-skinned Orcs and their troll brothers have been long standing enemies of the Villagers.
Darnes: Villagers are not of physical might, we prefer the use of magic. However the Orc's skins are immune to all but the strongest spells.
Darnes: So, if we can settle our differences peacefully, we will... But Orcs are not the most intelligent creatures, in fact I don't think they even know how to spell Orc.
Darnes: Nevertheless, they do respect loss and victory. If we are able to get the leader, Gorgu, to sign a peace treaty they will have no choice but to stay peaceful, for now.
Darnes: Now you see our problem. We are not able to get to Gorgu, he lives deep in the caves of the fortress, protected.
Darnes: Our best bet is to send someone disguised as an Orc, however our body type and smell will give us away instantly. We need you to go in our stead, Orcs won't know a human's scent too well.

Darnes: A convincing mask should fool them. So, please bring me [3 Orc Skin] by killing some orcs in the Camps just south of here. We will reward you handsomely if you are able to convince Gorgu to sign the treaty.

stages.title: Stage 2
stages.task: Bring back 3 Orc Skin to Darnes by killing Orcs near the camp.
hints: Darnes: Oh! Perfect! Let me craft it...
Darnes: ...
Darnes: ...
Darnes: Ha! A work of art if I say so myself! Alright! You will certainly fool those stupid orcs, and that's for sure! You're going to look like a real orc with this mask!
Darnes: Remember to grunt and shout about how much you love pig for dinner! This will bring us one step further to ending the Orc war one way or another.
Darnes: Now, go to Leadin, the Orc fortress, by following the path out of the war camp and past the Orcs.
Darnes: Then put on the mask, search for the cave and make your way to Gorgu and make him sign the peace treaty. But be careful, Orcs are bad enough, but Gorgu's something else!
Darnes: Oh, and bring me back the Orc Mask when you're done too, I would like to keep it!

Darnes: Well, I guess this hand print on the treaty counts.. I guess they don't use pens.
Darnes: We will stay stationed here to make sure the Orcs don't start any trouble, but the men will be so relieved we don't have to fight.
Darnes: As promised, here is the reward. It was part of the war fund, but since there is no war, you may have some!
Darnes: I know I said I wanted to keep this mask... But it smells hideous, you can take it. I even upgraded it for you! Who knows, you might need it again someday.

hints: Alem: I have warned you...
A strong spiritual force pulls you towards the graveyard, making it impossible to leave the area any other way than walking.

There are four locations in the graveyard in which you must complete a puzzle of sorts to trigger a line of dialogue. You can go through the locations in any order you want, and the dialogues will still trigger in the same order.

One of the locations is the church at [272, 82, -329]. Go down the stairs across from the entrance and into the lava room at [272, 67, -320]. This will trigger a line of fire particles that open the doors across from the lava room (if the second door does not open, try walking away, using /class, and walking back up to it). At the end of the passage, you will find a room with a strange creature surrounded by a few cultists. One of the four dialogues will trigger soon after you enter.

Another of the locations is the house at [288, 84, -409]. Entering the room to the left at [301, 82, -412] will cause a dead body to fall on the floor, with an Abandoned Key item right next to it. You can use the key to open the door right next to the entrance, by throwing it into the hopper at [290, 83, -411]. Then, go up the newly opened stairs, pick up an Attic Key in the room to the right at [290, 90, -414], and go back up the ladder to the left of the stairs to open another door by throwing the key into the hopper at [299, 94, -417]. Entering the attic will trigger a short cutscene with a ghost and one of the four dialogues.

Another of the locations is the house at [281, 78, -472]. Going up the stairs to the left, at [293, 78, -482], and into the bedroom, will trigger a short cutscene with some floating books and papers. Walking towards the door opposite the stairs will cause you to fall through the floor and into a stone tunnel. Continue through the tunnel to trigger two cutscenes with skeletons walking towards you - one in the middle, with one skeleton, and one at the end, with eight skeletons on all sides. After the one at the end finishes, one of the four dialogues will trigger.

Another of the locations is the house at [251, 75, -489]. Go up the stairs to the right, and pick up the Severed Arm in the bedroom at [236, 88, -489]. Take the Arm all the way down the stairs, and around to the hallway at [242, 75, -478] to cause the hanging skeleton to fall and open another set of stairs with the following dialogue:
XXXXXXX: Oh, my arm.. It's ba...
Approaching the skeleton without the Arm will instead trigger this dialogue:
XXXXXXX: Where di.. my arm.? I need my a... I had it somewh... upstairs?
Once the stairs fall down, go up them and towards the altar at [250, 81, -477] to trigger one of the four dialogues.
Once you have triggered all four dialogues, you will be taken to a newly opened door at the north end of the graveyard. Enter it to progress.
Once, there was a man,
who helped the spirits pass on,
however he was still
mortal.

After completing the sentence, Head to the door at [283, 74, -576] Once you pass through the door you will enter a large dark hallway. In order to pass through the door on the far end, you will need to pick up an Old Crypt Key from the room at [131, 9, 755] and throw it into the hopper at the end of the hallway, at [194, 10, 749].
This door appears to be locked. Perhaps a key could be used...
After you open the door at the end, enter it to reach a room with a tomb saying "R.I.P Mael Twain A guide and a friend.". Entering the room will trigger a few lines of dialogue and a cutscene.
???: You were warned not to enter this forsaken place.
???: But since you made it thusfar, I suppose I shall show you the truth...

The cutscene shows a series of clips of the graveyard. First, it shows it in good condition, with Mael Twain helping spirits, however, after Mael dies, it shows the graveyard in its current rotten condition, and the spirits becoming restless.
Mael: Do you understand now?
Mael: Now leave, and forget the horrors you have witnessed here today...
Mael: They are safer here.
You can finally take a breath again. Maybe Alem can expain what happened...

She had the power and the opportunity to kill it ten times over, but clung to her morals. She could not recognize necessity, and refused to heed my offers and warnings.
And so, my dark agony began. The light began to siphon away from me. I found myself paranoid and addled, fearful that my disfigurement would be seen.

stages.title: Stage 11

You must parkour to the end of the room while escaping the explosions behind you.

Enter the painting in the next room. Another cutscene will play, this one starting in Lari's camp at 820 AP.
The people of Gelibord saw my cursed visage... They saw me near the dark scars. They assumed without thought, and turned me into a perfect scapegoat.
Not even death saw the end of my misfortunes. Not even a final release such as this could save me from Lari's stubbornness and endless mistakes.
Return through the door you entered in, back to the dining room. The door opposite the one you entered will open, go through it.
[!] This parkour relies heavily on particles to guide the player. It is highly recommended that you turn on all particles for this segment of the quest.
You must parkour across the room to advance. Jump across the purple particle platforms, use the light blue particle waves to push you up, and avoid the dark cloud particles.
Once you enter the next room, go to the painting across from the entrance. Another cutscene will play, taking place soon after the previous one, in the Lazarus Pit.
She brought me back...but the dark infection had eroded away my mind, my soul, my magic, and it continued to ravage my body. Every part of me, the dark touched.
Her soft light burned in me, as the darkness quashed it and filled in the emptiness that it had created. I was there...but you could not say I was the same person.
I could feel nothing. She still made me feel...but only annoyance. Rage. Sorrow. I could not bear to be with her a moment longer.
Go up either staircase on the sides of the painting, and enter the door at the end of the walkway.

stages.title: Stage 13
stages.task: Investigate the dark door at the end of the castle.
hints: There is no fixing this. Her actions are doomed to failure, just as I saw. She has not returned since this time... And so she did not realize that her actions have done little.
The very powers she bestowed me with, knowingly or not...allow me to command spirits as I wish. To have those who doomed me to this purgatory feel the same aches as I have.
To have their minds, bodies, and souls wracked. To have their magic outlawed and wither in disuse.
Each soul I consume fills me with new strength. And none can reach me- Lari herself saw to that. Would she have taken action, had she known?
There is truly, finally, nothing more for you here. The spell can not be broken, as of now. You have seen my life laid bare in front of you. There is nothing more for you to see.
Leave. And do not return.

▸ Tips
Bring emeralds (or you will have to kill mobs for some) for the Olux stage. A full stack should be sufficient.
It is recommended that you bring teleport scrolls for Ragni, Almuj, Nesaak, Troms, Olux, Rodoroc, Corkus, and Detlas in order to save travel time.
You'll be teleported back to the quest NPC after every sequence, so you don't need to bring Lutho scrolls.
In the event that an NPC won't spawn during any point of the stage, use /class, /hub, and/or relog.
It is recommended that you bring consumable buffs to the Corkus and Detlas parts, as the bosses are difficult.
To access the iron golem factory in scenario 5, you must first complete until stage 4 of An Iron Heart Part II.
To access the Rodoroc Slums for scenario 6, you must first complete until stage 8 of Dwarves and Doguns Part II.

In scenario 8, Aledar does more damage, and Tasim has more health and elemental defence. If you kill Tasim first, Aledar becomes much stronger, and if you kill Aledar first, Tasim becomes much healthier. Therefore: If your build is a DPS build, kill Aledar first. But if your build is a tank build, kill Tasim first.

Lieutenant Tolv: If you think you can do a job better than an expert, go ahead and talk with them, but I'm pretty sure you'll have to cancel whatever plans you had.

Yes

Paxon: So we need to use the TNT Placer to daisy-chain blasts from the detonator, without blasting any tents, crates, or walls.

No

Swapping Hands while holding the TNT Placer cycles between small, medium, and large TNT. Small TNT has a blast radius of 3 blocks, medium is 4, and large is 5. There are 10 of each TNT. Right-click the TNT Placer to place a TNT. Placed TNT can be picked up by left-clicking it. Interact with the detonator to start the TNT chain. If the TNT chain destroys a structure or is abruptly stopped, all placed TNT will remain where they are. The destroyed block(s) will be highlighted red.
Start with medium or large TNT until the open area is reached
Use large TNT in the open area to curve to the left
Switch to medium TNT in between the white tent and crates. Switch to small if necessary.
Use medium or large TNT to curve to the right
Use medium TNT until the area between the blue tent and the walls
Use small and/or medium TNT for the rest of the path
A specific solution that works is:
Once the blue rock is blasted through, move into the opening.

stages.title: Stage 7
stages.task: Continue through the cave.
hints: Near the end of this side path, five spots in the ground will start emanating particles. Five Weak Zombies pop out of the ground.
All five Weak Zombies must be killed to continue.
...you were scared of those, once upon a time. What a difference time makes.
The blue rock at the end blasts open.

stages.title: Stage 8
stages.task: Talk to the Guard at [-9756, 56, -1219].
hints: Guard: Halt! Where did you come from? There was a cave-in past here, wasn't there?
Guard: A new path, huh? I didn't think you'd have things to be doing back here, though I won't say I'm ungrateful.
Guard: It even crushed the grook's nest there. I've been working off field rations for a few days. So where are you headed?
Guard: The border? I suppose if you're headed there, it must be important, official business. Although, it might have to wait.
Guard: The bridge repair was something of a hackjob. It may not bear up your weight. Now that the cave-in's clear, we might be able to get it fixed proper...
Guard: But that'll take time. I'd just as soon turn back whatever business you have isn't worth your life, after all.

stages.title: Stage 9
stages.task: Cross the repaired bridge at [-9715, 56, -1263].
hints: Optional dialogue on the way to the bridge:
Guard: Say, I think I recognize you, actually. That's a rarity for this line of work.
Guard: Are you sure that what you have to do is worth it? That bridge is awful rickety. Wouldn't want to lose you.

Walking onto the bridge freezes the Player in place. The bridge starts to collapse again, and the Player only has five seconds to run across. Failing to cross the bridge in time brings the Player back to the start of the bridge.

stages.title: Stage 10
stages.task: Continue back down the path to Fruma.
hints: Soldier: Hey, you there! Come talk to me before you pass through.

Soldier: Well, let me take a look and see if this stuff is up to regulation.
Soldier: Hmm... Ah, yep, signs of wear all over... Armor not polished... Weapon looks liable to fall apart any second...
Soldier: I'm surprised you made it ten feet out here with those rusty trinkets! This is no way to protect yourself!
Soldier: Look, there's a loot chest in the cave just there, so you need to head in and get yourself some proper equipment.
But I'm level 1XX
Soldier: ...that so, huh? Well, I think you should take a second look up ahead.
The Soldier walks over to the cave and constructs a "dungeon" called the "Gate of Unfathomable Difficulty", being extreme and the Player's current level.
Soldier: See? Now no more guff about levels you either gear up properly, or you don't pass! I won't have you risking your life.
Soldier: You can find good stuff in caves, like the one just next to me, so hop to it.
I'm going the other way.
Soldier: Like I said, coming or going. No matter what, you should gear up by looting the cave here before heading onwards.
Understood.
Soldier: Good stuff. There's a loot chest in that cave there, so you should find everything you need. Get to it!

stages.title: Stage 11
stages.task: Explore the cave to find some loot.
hints: Optional dialogue:
Soldier: Enter the cave and open the loot chest.

The cave is a near-exact replica of the loot cave in the old King's Recruit, the only difference being the stone is already broken. After doing some parkour, an old Tier 1 Loot Chest can be opened, revealing 8 Emeralds, a level 1-5 Unique unidentified helmet, and a Ruined Oak Weapon that breaks after using it.

stages.title: Stage 12
stages.task: Continue back down the path to Fruma.
hints: Soldier: That looks like the stuff. You can take that armor to an Item Identifier right there, and then you can wear it once identified.
Soldier: Though... since you seem to be heading back to the border... I have to ask why. It's pretty unusual. Probably best you head back to Ragni.
Soldier: If other recruits see you coming the other way, they might get confused, or discouraged. Wouldn't want to risk that, right?
Optional dialogue on the path back to Fruma:
Soldier: Are you sure whatever you're doing is worth it? Maybe you should just head back to town.

Once the Player arrives at the gate between the Wynn and Fruma provinces, a line of dialogue will appear.
This gate markes the Fruman Border you must make sure you aren't spotted from this point onwards.

hints: Fruman Recruit: ...been recruiting Fruman soldiers for the war effort. Apparently things are really bad over there. Makes me nervous...

They're gone. Hurry down the path!

The second recruits can be avoided by going into the tree to the right.

They're gone. Hurry down the path!

The third recruits can be avoided by hiding behind the boulder to the right.
Fruman Recruit: I'm thinking about meals more than wheels. I feel like I haven't eaten in days. Hope the walk's short...
Fruman Recruit: Well, if he was a more competent driver you wouldn't have to walk so far on an empty stomach! Let's hurry so we can get you a feast, huh?
They're gone. Hurry down the path!
Fruman Recruit: Wait, who's that? Why are they coming from the border??

stages.title: Stage 14
stages.task: Hide from the Caravan Driver.
hints: The Caravan Driver can be avoided by going behind the large boulder to the left.
Caravan Driver: ...and that's the last of them for today.

The Caravan Driver walks to the wheel and looks at it.
Caravan Driver: Same darn boulder... Same darn line, too. Wonder if they'll let me shake it up one day. This is always a pain...
The Caravan Driver uses magic to attach the wheel back onto the caravan.

The Caravan Driver opens the large door.
This is your chance, the gate's open! Follow the Caravan Driver!

stages.task: Explore past the Fruma Gate.
hints: Beyond the gate is an area unlike the Ragni Outskirts. Rather than being rural, the unseen part of the outskirts is a heavily industrialized complex.
What is this place? Such technology, you can hardly imagine how it was made.

He's dead asleep. You could probably ring a church bell an inch above his head and he'd stay unconscious.
...something's prickling at the back of your mind. Weren't you asleep like this when you first arrived, too?
Exit the cart to progress.

Caravan Driver: Bet you think you're slick. Didn't even notice me hang back to watch, huh? I wasn't born yesterday.

Caravan Driver: It's not wise to be here After all, you weren't the one out of your group of three that got permission to stay. Yeah, I heard about the tournament results.
Caravan Driver: So...you got two choices, buddy. We can let this slide between us. We can. You can go marching back to Ragni and my lips will be sealed.

No

4 Torann Reinforcements
Wave 2:
4 Torann Reinforcements

Wave 3:
4 Constable Guards

stages.task: Leave Fort Torann.
hints: You have emptied Fort Torann of soldiers. You must escape before someone discovers what has happened here. The only way out is forward.

A strong spell should get through this wood without a problem.
Maybe another spell?
Again?
Again.

stages.title: Stage 3
stages.task: Escape the illusion.
hints: To get out of the orange room, there will be a fake wall at the eastern end. Your objective is to find three crystals. The first challenge in the magenta room has you doing parkour on white blocks. Right-clicking the gray blocks will temporarily change the configuration of the white blocks. After getting to a pink room, there will be a crystal at the end of the parkour, which must be right-clicked to be destroyed.
After destroying the first crystal, you will then be in a lime room.
A shard of the crystal seems to have remained behind. Maybe you can use this to escape!
Right Click with the shard to change what is real and what is fake.

The Crystal Shard is used so when right-clicked will change the state of yellow and purple blocks. When a block is an illusion, it will be there visually but does not exist physically, and when a block is real, you can use it physically. Eventually, after completing the parkour in another orange room, the second crystal must be destroyed.

You will then be sent to another lime room where there will be pink blocks that travel in a snake-like manner. After completing the parkour, you will then be sent to a blue room, where all of the previous mechanics come into play to reach the third and final crystal.

stages.title: Stage 4
stages.task: Run away and confront the wizard.
hints: A large purple mass will appear behind you, and you must run away from it. Once you have ran away from it, climb up the tower where the wizard is.
Jump into the hole right below Dramele's tower. You will end up in a strange dimension after you get in the hole.

stages.title: Stage 5
stages.task: Find a way out of the strange dimension.
hints: There's the strange gem Dramele threw away... You should take it with you, he said it would save Norsten.
Right-click on the Strange Gem to pick it up. A nauseating aura will be applied to you, and then several Magical Disturbances will spawn.
After you have defeated all of the Magical Disturbances, a puzzle will appear.
Although the strange beings are now gone, some parts of them were left behind. They look very unstable.
Perhaps if you combine them in the right way you can cause an explosion and escape.
Goal: Get 100 Explosive Power by combining the 6 different cores in the grid made of green particles.
Right Click a core to select it, the Right Click one of the 6 green spots in the grid to place it there.
Each core gains and loses explosive power based on its position in the grid, and what cores it's touching. Each core touches the cores that are above, below, and next to it.
Remember, you need to get 100 Explosive Power! If you need a hint, click on Hints and Rules and select "I want a hint."

stages.title: Stage 6
stages.task: Find a way out of the strange dimension.
hints: There will be a 2 by 3 grid with green particles where you can place the cores. To the left is a confirm button to submit your answer, and to the left is a clear mode button which can be used to remove cores from their position. On the opposite side of the area is the Hints & Rules NPC. Each Core has the following attributes:
Purple Core: +10 Explosive Power, x2 Power when touching blue
Orange Core: +5 Explosive Power, -5 Power when touching blue, +5 Power when touching purple, x2 Power when on the left
Blue Core: +10 Explosive Power, +5 Power when touching purple, x2 Power when on the right
Gray Core: +0 Explosive Power, -20 Power per core it touches that isn't rainbow
Green Core: +25 Explosive Power, -10 Power when touching orange, -5 Power when touching blue, -5 Power when touching purple
Rainbow Core: +0 Explosive Power, +20 Power when touching blue, +10 Power when touching orange, +10 Power when touching purple, +5 Power when touching green
If you fail the puzzle, you will be given a tip, such as how the total power is calculated from top to bottom for each core.

stages.title: Stage 7
stages.task: Escape the strange dimension.
hints: After getting the Unstable Core Amalgamation, place it in the center of the floor to the strange dimension. It will explode, allowing you to access the portal out of the dimension. You will land in front of the gate to Thesead where Peli and Norsten will be.

stages.title: Stage 8
stages.task: Talk to the woman in the cave.
hints: In the large, open cave are some maple trees and an unnamed woman in the center.
???: Well, well. If it isn't a fresh breeze dancing in the leaves...
???: You must be the Cursed One who caused such a stir at Torann, yes? News has spread quickly of your actions.
???: I'm impressed you found your way to me.
???: So let's get to the business at hand. I'll start with this you're from the Wynn Province, aren't you?
???: I thought so... You're certainly not from around here. Though, I would recommend you keep that information close to your chest.
???: Very few people have knowledge of the outside world, and those that do... they're the ones who will be looking for you. Best to avoid drawing their attention.
Syndra: But I should introduce myself. My name is Syndra, leader of the Leaves in the Wind resistance group.
You trust me?
Player: You trust me enough to tell me that?
Syndra: Call it something of a gamble. Given your... shall we say, explosive entrance into the province, I find it unlikely you're with the crown.
Syndra: Even if you chose to reveal my secrets and if anyone even believed you you'd have no guarantee of your own safety.
Resistance group?
Player: A resistance group?
Syndra: Yes. You haven’t been here long, but you’ve felt it, haven’t you? The crown has its roots buried deep in this province, and it certainly isn’t kind to all.
Syndra: Those it sees as disposable… they don’t often make it far. That is why I have taken my role. I’d like to see a day where none are left behind.
Syndra: But that's enough about me. On to you. Why are you here, cursed one? For what purpose have you come to Fruma?
Something strange is happening.
Player: Something strange is happening here. I can feel it.
Syndra: Interesting. A sense that something isn't right...
Syndra: To tell you the truth, it's one I've had myself for quite some time. Though, likely for a different reason to you.
I'm looking for a friend.
Player: I'm looking for a friend.
Syndra: A noble cause… It is one I can wholeheartedly support.
Syndra: In a world like this, the most we can do sometimes is hold on to those we care for. Take care not to lose that drive.
Syndra: Then, I would ask of you one more thing. A test, in a way...
Syndra: The power you carry the curse you bear. I have seen such things before, yet always at a distance. Never up close.
Syndra: I would ask for a duel. Nothing dangerous, or lethal... I have safeguards in place for myself, so do not test my limits. When I call it, we stop.
Syndra: I would simply like to see the strength of a cursed one in battle firsthand. So, then. Let us begin!

stages.title: Stage 9
stages.task: Complete Syndra's challenge.
hints: A boss fight with Syndra will ensue.
Syndra: Enough! Come speak to me.
Syndra: Impressive. Very impressive. I have never seen a cursed one with such control and technique...
Syndra: If I did not know better, I would believe you to have been blessed by the crown itself.
Player: You keep calling me cursed. What does it mean?
Syndra: Your power, your spells. The ability to bend the world to your whim, to wield the elements for your own gain.
Syndra: Eons ago, so the stories say, the world was pure and balanced. Our people lived with the land, content with what we had.
Syndra: And yet, an evil force lurked within us, a malice which despised our peace and happiness. One day, it burst forth, granting unimaginable power to those it deemed worthy...
Syndra: Its power could not be controlled. Those cursed by its touch went on to tear apart the land, destroying cities and towns... fear overtook the land, none were safe.
Syndra: Until she arrived, a force of good to counter the evil. She granted her own blessings to the people of Fruma, power which could be controlled and wielded to banish the cursed.
Syndra: She saved our province, and became our immortal Queen. Always looking out for the people, always alert for the presence of evil... for it could not be killed, only staved off.
Syndra: The cursed ones never left. They only grew smarter, more capable of hiding from the crown's watchful eye.
Syndra: And so, it tells the people, always be aware. Always be looking for the cursed ones. It is only a matter of time before they hurt you.
Syndra: ...I have a different perspective on this story, you might imagine. The crown has wronged me, and many others. Yet, the stories hold truths to them, to an extent.
Syndra: That is why your control over your power has interested me. It bears more traits of the crown's blessings than of the evil's curses, and yet...
Player: I've only ever known it as magic. Where I'm from, most people can wield it.
Syndra: Magic... yes, that term has been used in higher studies at the University.
Syndra: But a land filled with cursed ones... and it isn't destroyed? I suppose I have had no reason to believe the crown's reports about it, but...
Syndra: I need time to process this information. But I would like to discuss it with you further, at a later date, if you would be willing.
Syndra: Then that leads me to my final request. Would you join our cause, and offer your help to our resistance group? Your knowledge and strength would be greatly appreciated.
I will.
Player: I'll join your resistance group.
Syndra: Thank you. I will take you to meet with the others, then. Our home is directly to the south-west, it should be hard to miss. I'll meet you there.
Syndra will walk out of the cave.

stages.title: Stage 10
hints: Syndra: There you are, Player. I see you found your way here alright.
Syndra: If you're going to be joining us, I should introduce you to the others.
Syndra: Ahem... Children, come on out! We have a new member I'd like you to meet.
Rex, Zeph, and two other new characters (Mora and Sui) walk out of the house.
Zeph: We m-meet again! I knew you'd be a g-good fit!
Rex: Yeah, Zeph, we know. You've been saying so for hours...
Mora: Ah, lighten up Rex. Welcome to the Leaves, friend! No matter your origin, if Syndra believes you to be trustworthy, it must be so.
Syndra: On that subject, Player here is from outside of our province. They'll be joining our resistance against the crown...
Syndra: ...and, hopefully, they'll be able to help me resolve some theories I have on the nature of curses and blessings.
Sui: Oh... they're cursed...?
Syndra: Yes. But they're no threat to us. We share the same enemies. And, having that power on our side could make a huge difference for our efforts.
Mora: Hm... are you certain, miss? I do trust your judgment, but perhaps it would be best to err on the side of caution when dealing with the cursed.
Rex: The curse is the least of our problems! Are we really blindly trusting someone who says they're from Wynn? People don't just... just... come back from there!
Syndra: That's enough, Rex. I understand your misgivings, but I have reasons for my trust. I would ask you to have faith in me.
Rex: ...fine. Whatever.
Syndra: Now. I still need to acquire the proper papers for Player to be able to access Espren. In the meantime, why don't you all get to know each other properly?
Syndra: I'll be back shortly.
Syndra will walk out of the resistance base.

hints: Zeph will walk the path into the Frog Tavern, starting by following a path of crates and then going on top of the roof.

Go through the curtained area and then go down the stairs. At the bar is a Bartender, Syndra, and Sovereign Zhiraok.
Zeph: Th-there she is! I w-wonder what she's

Syndra: You seem... stressed.
Sovereign Zhiraok: Oh, thank you for noticing! It's because of the stress. Look, I know you're aware of the attack on Torann by now. You've always kept up with the details.
Sovereign Zhiraok: But how about we accelerate this. You know how little time I have and you didn't bring me here just for drinks.
Syndra: Skipping the small talk, I see. Are my intentions really that transparent?
Sovereign Zhiraok: Predictable, more like, after all this time. You've always got an angle you're working towards when you call me here.
Syndra: Maybe I just like the ambience.
Syndra: ...I need another passport. Same as the rest.
Sovereign Zhiraok: Naturally. You and your trend for collecting strays... Really you should just start a family by this point.
Syndra: You of all people should know that I can't just stand by and leave them to fend for themselves.
Sovereign Zhiraok: Yes... A toddler could calculate that by watching you. I'll solve that problem for you. Keep them out of trouble, and we won't have any issues as usual.
Syndra: Of course. As I always do.
Sovereign Zhiraok: Ha! "Always." If I were a gambling man I'd never bet on your odds.
Sovereign Zhiraok: I need to get moving. There's always something that needs me to crunch the numbers... and today's events have only added to the pile.
Syndra: I certainly wouldn't want to delay you, Sovereign. I hope you manage to sort out all these problems.
Sovereign Zhiraok gets out of his seat.
Sovereign Zhiraok: Oh, we will. It's only a matter of time. Take care, Syndra. Keep it constant.

Syndra: ...
Syndra: Sigh. You may as well come down now. Zeph, Player.

Syndra: I had hoped to keep this a secret for a reason... but what's done is done. Just... don't do anything rash, would you?

Kaio: Hm... I guess not, thinking on it now. A few years ago, had you asked, I'd've probably said yes. But I don't got the strength in me for it anymore.

Kaio: I've got no such delusions, unfortunately. I reckon this path only ends in tragedy. But it's not my place to say so, so I don't.
Kaio: Would be good to be proven wrong... but I don't think I will be. I've seen this sorta thing before.
Talking to Kaio again without interacting with the gravestone:
Kaio: ...what? I got nothin' else to say.
The gravestone next to Kaio can be interacted with.
Interacting with the gravestone:
It's a headstone. Carved into the stone, you see a name and a year.
"Aledar, 119 IA"
Kaio: Interesting that you're drawn to that grave in particular. S'our latest loss, that'n there.
Kaio: It's a damn shame. A tragedy each 'n every time, yet still happens often enough to feel routine. But that's life, I reckon.
Aledar... I knew him.
Kaio: ...did you now? Funny thing to say about a dead man, considering I ain't ever seen you 'round these parts before.
Kaio: Now, spill. 'Fore I go and tell Synny you ain't no good after all.
He got sent to Wynn. We... met there.
Kaio: Ah... caught Rex muttering something 'bout that once or twice before. Poor girl... it'd do her well to set it aside, for a time.
Kaio: Didn't think much of it, but I suppose you're livin' proof, aren'tcha? Strange as can be...
Kaio: Say, is the memory wipin' a real thing? Got no damn clue where that theory started, but... well, if one thing's true, why not the rest?
It is.
Kaio: Damn. Damn. That's rough. That real rough, ain't it. And you're tellin' me that's where he ended up?
Kaio: Hrm... y'know, it's funny. Big guy like him, you wouldn't take him for a thief. Hard to keep hidden, eh? And yet...
Kaio: He'd manage to turn blending into a crowd into an art. No matter where he was, who he spoke to, how he was actin', he'd always seem like he fit right in.
Kaio: ...t'was a right stupid risk that did him in, in the end. I told him, I did it ain't worth breaking into the Sovereign's place, especially not during festival times...
Kaio: But he was the kinda sort to dig in his heels. Said he'd be fine, said it'd be worth it, nabbin' all those documents. Something to help the cause... I hardly even remember now.
Kaio: Can't save 'em all. Especially not from themselves. I've learned that many times over, over my years.
Kaio: So he got caught. Heard a cursed one got involved... was a whole damn mess. Sovereign really wasn't happy with Synny when he heard, let me tell you. Ain't seen her that shellshocked in years.
Kaio: ...but you're sayin' he lived? How's that all work out?
He's... gone, now.
Kaio: Ah. I see. I... see.
Kaio: Well... tell me this, then. Was he happy, you think? Out there in the wider world? Did he live a good life?
...yes. He did.
Kaio: ...alright. Alrighty. Good. That that's good, y'hear. I... I'm glad for that much.
Kaio: Thank you for... for tellin' me all that. S'not a tale that ends in happiness, but I reckon so long as he made the most of it... that's all you can really hope for.
Kaio: Y'may as well leave me be a while, now. Got some thinkin' to get through.
Talking with Kaio again:
Kaio: ...

hints: First area:
Interact with the red and green crystal in any order.
Second area:
No crystals have to be interacted with. Instead walk past the blue crystal to the exit.
Third area:
Interact with the crystals in the following order: green, red, yellow.

An earthquake will happen and then will cause several walls with colored veins to rise out of the ground. The state of a wall will be reversed when you interact with a crystal of a color corresponding to the wall. As an example, if a red wall can appear in two places, and a Red Wall is already there while there is a gate for a red wall that does not have that wall, the crystal will change it so the wall will now be on the one that did not already have a wall. There will be three rooms of increasing difficulty.

hints: To heal Ressinter, you must put 1 Chamomile, 1 Pyrola, and 2 Yarrows into the brewing pot to receive a [Herbal Balm], or either fail the combination 3 times and then help will arrive.|healing Ressinter}}
This is the medicine book Zuett talked about... but almost all of the words are in Orcish! There are pictures of each plant, and readable names, but...
[1] Look up Sweetgale.
The book depicts a tall, vine-like plant with red buds.
The illustration shows a body with splotchy red patches, and seems to depict pulped buds being applied to them.
There's a picture of fire on the skin...? Is it trying to say that sweetgale helps heal inflammation?
Another diagram shows grubs on the body, and seems to show that applying the pulped buds kills the bugs? That's what the big red X over the grub implies...
[2] Look up Yarrow.
The book depicts large groups of flowers in various colors, but primarily yellow.
Seems like yarrow can do a lot- there's a lot of disparate illustrations. One points at a sneezing orc with two yarrow plants pointing at it, and the sneezing stopping.
A similar illustration shows an orc that appears to be having stomach cramps, if its hands are crossed over its stomach is any indication, with two yarrow plants being pointing at it.
The third one seemingly shows an orc seemingly cut up, with red droplets coming off it. Again, two yarrow plants are pointed at it, and the next picture shows the cuts and droplets gone.
[3] Look up Chamomile.
The book depicts small, dainty flowers with white petals.
There's a detailed picture of the plant, and with arrows pointing to multiple different illustrated orcs each showing different things.

One orc is shown to be agitated, and then subsequently sleeping. Another is...shown with red patches on the skin, and fire next to it, which is depicted with water droplets in the next drawing. The red patches are gone.
The last one shows various cuts and gashes on a third orc that's emitting red droplets, and then smaller cuts without any red drops on the next depiction...
...but the next page is showing an orc with X's over its eyes, and arrows from multiple chamomile plants pointing to it. Does that mean too much chamomile is bad?
[4] Look up Feverfew.
The book depicts a shrub-like plant with white petals and buds.

It looks like it's good for healing a lot of things. The pictures show a sweating, feverish orc, one is clutching its stomach, a female one clutching her stomach, and what can be assumed to be an orc with...a toothache?
Seems to imply that feverfew is good for dealing with all those kinds of maladies.
[5] Look up Gingko Leaf.
The book depicts broad, yellow-green leaves.
There's an image of an orc with red droplets coming off it, and an arrow with a picture of a gingko leaf pointing at it- the arrow is crossed out. That could mean multiple things.
The next page shows a gingko leaf pointed at an illustration of a brain, and a similar arrow points from a frowning orc to a smiling one.
So that means it's good for mood and mental health...and that it does something with bleeding, but you can't tell whether that would be good or bad for it.
[6] Look up Pyrola.
The book depicts red-orange flowering stalks, almost like cattails.
There's a large illustration of an orc with big purple blotches all over it, and next to it there's a similar illustration with orange splotches instead.
That implies that ground-up pyrola goes on there...probably depicting bruises.
Similar orange splotches are applied to what is clearly a cut, and the next illustration over shows the same cut having become smaller.
Then there's illustrations of what look like...veins? There's a lot of orcish script next to it, so you can't make heads or tails of what that much could mean.
[7] Look up Elderberry.
The book depicts a short shrub covered in vibrant red berries on small stalks.
There are multiple illustrations of what look like sick orcs- sneezing and coughing shown in pictures.
One illustration shows what looks to be an orc in great pain, and arrows pointing from the elderberries to those figures.
Your best guess is that elderberries are good for healing mild illnesses, and maybe for dulling pain.
[8] Close the book.
First fail:
The bleeding seems to have slowed down a little bit, but the medicine orc is still badly injured. The balm must not have been effective. You'll have to make another one.
Second fail:
The balm doesn't seem to have worked this time either. He's still bleeding badly. Maybe you can just...cover up all the cuts and hope for the best? Or maybe that's not a good idea.
Third fail:
Still no significant effect. The orc's breathing is getting shallower...

stages.title: Stage 2
stages.task: Find Javier's map, hidden in the skull tomb at the entrance of the island
hints: The entrance to the skull Javier mentions is at [-672, 44, -3195]. Once you reach it, head inside, and follow the path until you reach a four-way intersection. Go straight across the intersection, then turn left and continue to follow the path. You will reach a large open treasure room, and the following dialogue will play:
As the buccaneer says, walk to the tomb at [-682, 19, -3205]. This will open a new tunnel out of the treasure room and trigger more dialogue:
You go on as you can hear laughter spreading through the walls...

Go into the newly opened tunnel, and follow it through. It will connect back to the main path, but another new tunnel will open across from it; follow this one as well. You will be stopped at one point and a figure will fall from the ceiling, spawning a level 60 Deceased Trespasser which you can either kill or simply avoid.

Very shortly afterwards, a hole in the floor will appear beneath you - if you fall through, you will have to go through the tunnels again. You will then pass through a "minefield" in which stepping on any of the pressure plates damages you, and can progress by going to the right. Avoiding the constantly firing cannonballs in the next hallway will allow you to progress to a tunnel that leads straight to the map. Once you have the map, you can exit and return to Javier.

▸ Tips
Have the 5 Emerald Blocks with you before visiting Dalben, to avoid making two trips.
Bring an Emerald Block before entering the cave, as it is required to open up the passage to the map.
If you stay in the staircase after giving 1 Emerald Block, the doors will close and you will become trapped.
After talking to Dalben at Stage 5, it is faster to buy a Selchar boat pass (or use a teleport scroll) and swim/boat to Sarnfic, instead of starting from Mage Island.

The Treasure Guardian will attempt to shoot Arrow Storms at you and push you into the lava on the edges of the arena. You can utilize the four pillars in the arena to counter these attacks, either to block an Arrow Storm by getting behind one, or to stop a Push from throwing you into the lava by standing in front of one.

hints: Irlok: Welcome to the Bantisu Temple, traveler. We guide lost souls onwards, be they wandering men to town or spirits unable to exit the canyon.
Irlok: However, recently, our job has become much more difficult. The canyon shakes, and changes. Often, long-buried creatures are released as the walls shift.
Irlok: And unfortunately, the worst has come to pass, that one of these creatures is hostile. The Bantisu monks of old collapsed the entrance to its cave to seal it away...
Irlok: ...but the rubble has shifted, and the cave is open once more. We were not strong enough to defeat it then, and we are not strong enough to defeat it now.
Irlok: Even trying to collapse the cave again has ended in failure, for the beast, Krolton, slays our mages and demolitionists in but an instant.
Irlok: However, the word on the wind tells tales of humans doing the impossible as a matter of rote. Krolton must be dealt with before it leaves the cave- I beg your assistance!
Irlok: We've no time to spare. I will prepare a short spell to bring you to the cave- Please, wait outside, and prepare yourself.

Strangers from the West.
Strangers: Strangers from the West 188 BP

Strangers: The most curious people have come in the shadows of the mountains. They wear a strange garb, of varied and colorful fabrics, yet speak in an unintelligible tongue harsher than even our Jungle cousins' speech.
Strangers: When their voices drop to but a grating whisper, their scribes produce such wondrous and awful magic, one that matches the legends of Hashr the Betrayer no less.

Strangers: They appear to call themselves the Edhlashez (or perhaps Etlawshess), and hail from the land west past the mountains, calling it Evroemath and Efrovmath at once, as well as simply Taashelh.
Strangers: Three of our most learned priests have already set about learning this tongue, for it seems entwined with the secrets of their magic.

Strangers: While their maths are recognizable, and have been a boon to our communication as yet, they are formidable too, perhaps more advanced than our own. There is much to learn of their timekeeping however, and we admit to some confusion.
Strangers: They have marked today as the 18th of Uth in some 6th Sifkelh (or Zivgel), but gave the same date ereyesterday, and yet the same a fortnight after their arrival some two moons previous.

Strangers: Contrary to their magic, their weapons seem almost rudimentary, clearly suited towards hunting rather than warfare. We welcome them in peace, and they seem to expect the same, to our relief.

Strangers: The townsfolk remain curious, though an undercurrent of nervousness remains upon experiencing their eerily familiar magic. It appears the memories of our ancestors are as yet too strong to forget.
The text ends here...
The Language of the Edlashez.
Language: The Language of the Edlashes 187 BP

Language: It has been some ten months since the arrival of the Edlashes, and much has been learned of their customs and tongue. They are free in the teaching of their language, but guard their writing somewhat warily.
Language: The Priest Ognus has called on me to record his studies of their speech and, with permission, a description of their script.
Language: The speech of the Edlashes, which they call Taa-gashtelh (or Etl-kashtelh) is mostly smooth in rhythm yet often harsh in timbre.
Language: They too split their sentences into words, and then again into letters, each of which is ascribed a simple glyph written left to right.
Language: On occasion, their scribes appear to combine a number of glyphs into one, and write in intricate shapes or boustrophedon, though as to why they are unwilling to disclose.

Language: Of the vowels, they have five, which are used somewhat sparingly. The first, a slant from high to low, is a high, pinched sound. It is somewhat reminiscent of a sheared sheep or leaf, always truncated, never at length.

Language: Next, the mountain trail is open and relaxed, like a calm spa, long and short alike. The loop is assuredly the most bizarre; as its shape suggests it is tight and rounded, with the tongue pushed frontwards as well.
Language: It is a distinctly muddy sound, to us even one of disgust, yet the Edlashes find it as harmonious as the rest.

Language: Fourth is the downwards hook, a rounded sound, long or short, high yet deep, as a cool soothing true alto. The last is the slant from low to high, always short, and commonplace as a red dress.
Language: The consonants are several in number, and plentiful. Of the lips there are four (or perhaps six), of which most are familiar.
Language: The rarest, a stripe with a joint to the left, is a murky midnight moor; the thin dagger tip belongs to a knight of nine knives; the right-facing hook a brown bird or its precarious perch.
Language: Lastly, the swan, though foreign to our speech, is as one would do to cool a scalding-hot stew; it is a loose, relaxed breath through lips rounded but ajar, with air or with voice.
Language: At the teeth is the handle, like three thrown thistles.
Language: Behind the teeth sit four more glyphs: the crescent, in tenebrous twilight or darkened dusk; the arrow, similar, but with a yet lighter touch.
Language: There sits the elbow too, a wide, breathy sound that splits the mouth like a river; and the straw, bent left, stem sprouting straight with zeal despite roots askew.
Language: Further back sits the fork, at which our opinions diverge. To my ears it is on the tip of my tongue, a sure sign showing the way. To Ognus, it is deeper, and full-bellied instead.
Language: Further back still is the right-jointed stripe, cut clean on glossy granite. And finally, the leg climbs uphill, at times a heavy, harried huff, at others a silence, out of breath.
The text ends here...
Nothing for now.
Exits the dialogue.

stages.task: Escape The Pit
hints: Th̵̲͚͐͒e Pi̴̧̹̚͝tYour spells have been restored.
The Pit is structured a bit like a standard Dungeon. You can use your spells again, although you still cannot jump.
▸ Room 1

The first room of the Pit is a simple segment where you walk through the room. There will be some gaps that will need maneuvers that do not make you jump. At the end of room one, you need to kill the Experimental Sludge, a miniboss, and use its drop to open a door that will drop down a rope that you must climb to get to the second room.
... So apparently you can climb ropes but not jump. Being a cow is weird.
▸ Room 2

In the second room of The Pit, it is a maze through the vent system. Some fans will only produce light breezes that only move you towards a wall, while others are harder to get through, having winds strong enough that you can't go forward. At some areas, there will be a device that will deactivate certain fans be behind bars. To destroy the bars, cast a spell in front of them, and then right-click the device.

▸ Room 4
The fourth room serves as a passage from the third room to the fifth room. At the start, two Cowbominations will ambush you, although you are not required to kill them.

Drale: Oh, this is- Oh! You're alive! I, ah- heh. Sorry about... all that. I really, really need to label these levers properly...
Drale: Right! Right. You'se seen... all that down there, then. I just hope you won't think less of me for it.
Drale: I can... I can tell you more about it later. I hope it wasn't too bad? Down there? You seen to have gotten out in one piece, so...
[1] Moo mooooo moo moo! (The workers in the pit want better positions!)
Drale: ...Oh. Right. Gosh, how long has it been since I-...
Drale: Okay. Alright, yes, I'll give them better positions. And I'll- I don't know. Apologize. Give them a bonus.
Drale: It's been... hard, recently. We've been working to get back home, and I guess I just... Put too much of myself into that. It's fine! Don't- Don't worry about me.
[1] Moo... Moo moo moooo? (So... How do I get back to normal?)
Drale: Oh. Right, your body! I can fix that! We just need to get back to the machine, and... Poof. You'll be back to normal!
Drale: ...I hope. Hey, being a cow isn't so bad! If- If it doesn't work, we can make you a home here...?
Drale: Uh... It'll work. It's always- always worked in the past! Heh...
Drale: Anyway! Let's get going!
[2] Moo. (Moo.)
[2] Moo moo moooo... (How do I get back to normal?)
[3] Moo. (Moo.)
Drale: Uh... Hm. Maybe- Maybe being a cow is affecting your brain somehow... That can't be good.
Drale: We should get you back to human as quickly as possible. Come on, follow me.
Gave Drale attitude:
Drale: ...This doesn't even mean anything! What am I supposed to do with-
Drale: Oh! It's- It's you! Didn't I just...
Drale: ...Um. This is... really awkward, haha. I'm... sorry?
Drale: You're... the one who pretended to be a cow, right? I, uh... in my defense, I was very stressed. So I dropped you into the Pit.
Drale: ...Anyway! What's- What's going on with your life? Anything interesting?
[1] Moo moo moooo. (How do I get back to normal?)
Drale: Oh! Right. Getting back to normal.
Drale: You said you stepped into my machine, right? We could try putting you in there a second time. What's the worst that could happen?
Drale: ...Uh. You stay as a cow. That's what. That's... fine. Let's just go and try it out.
[2] Moo. (Moo.)
Said you are a cow:
Drale: ...This doesn't even mean anything! What am I supposed to do with-
Drale: Oh! It's- It's you! Didn't I just...
Drale: ...Um. This is... really awkward, haha. I'm... sorry?
Drale: I am talking to a cow. Again. Why is this where my life has taken me.
Drale: So! What's... going on, little buddy? Any- any souvenirs? From the Pit...?
[1] Moo moo Moooo! (I'm not a cow! I'm a human that was turned into a cow!)
Drale: Oh, you- Oh. Right! Okay. I don't- I don't quite understand why you would pretend to be a cow. But alright!
Drale: So, uh... Human turned into a cow. Okay. How did you manage to get yourself stuck as a cow, anyway? I didn't think we had anything that could do that...
[1] Moo moo moooo. (I walked into your stupid machine!)
Drale: My machine. It's- It's not even supposed to do that! I designed it to turn exiles back into Wocs, how would it have...
Drale: Great. Of course it'd have that issue, and just when I thought I...
Drale: Right. Right. Alright. We can work with this! Let's just take you back to that machine, put you in it, and see if it turns you back to normal!
Drale: It'll work. Probably. I mean, I haven't ever tried it, so I can't really say for sure... Oh, yep, you're still here. Let's get moving.
[2] Moo. (Moo.)
Drale: Uh... Hm. Maybe- Maybe being a cow is affecting your brain somehow... That can't be good.
Drale: We should get you back to human as quickly as possible. Come on, follow me.
[2] Moo. (Moo.)
Drale: Yep. Just a cow...
Drale: Well, alright. Let's just- get you in my machine, I guess. It worked for the exiles, so maybe it will work for you...?
Drale: ...Don't look at me like that. Come on, let's get going.
Drale will then walk to the machine that turned you into a cow.
Told Drale you were the one that helped him:
Drale: So... How have you been? It's been a while since our adventure at Katoa Ranch, hasn't it?
Drale: Well, you've been turned into a cow... Obviously... But besides that!
Drale: Me? Well... heh. I've been doing pretty well, all thing considered. We've been gathering exiles from all over the province! Set up a city for us all while we work towards...
Drale: It's a long story. I can't tell you everything- not yet. But... All of us here, we don't belong here. We just want to go home.
Drale: And- and maybe if we can find our ship again, we'll be able to prove that we're not irredeemable. That whatever we went through- that it won't define us.
Drale: ...Heh. Don't- don't worry about it too much. For now, this place is enough of a safe haven for us. It'll have to be enough until we succeed.
Drale: We're so close. I can feel it. Just... Just a little while left to go.
Drale: Anyway, uh... Here's the elevator! Just step on in, and we can head on up to the laboratory.
[1] Moooo moo moo moo? (What's that big door next to us for?)
Drale: The- oh. Uh... It's nothing. Nothing to worry about.
Drale: It just leads to... maintenance. Yep! Just- just maintenance. Nothing else.
Drale: Into the elevator now, come on! You need a key to get in anyway, and I definitely don't have one laying around!
[2] Moo. (Moo.)
Drale: ...You're worrying me, friend. Come on, let's get going. Into the elevator, let's get you back to normal.
Gave Drale attitude or pretended you were a cow first and then said you were a human:
Drale: So... Have you done anything interesting recently? Besides- getting turned into a cow. Obviously.
Drale: You're, uh... Probably wondering what this place is. Just a big city under some random guy's farm, right?
Drale: It's... heh. We've been trying to gather as many of our people as we can. We exiles have to stick together, after all.
Drale: It's a long story. I'm not sure how much of it I really want to tell you, heh. Especially considering... Yeah.
Drale: But. This place is a safe haven for us exiles. A place for us all to live until we achieve our goals.
Drale: And- hey! You've seen our secrets now! May as well let it be a safe haven for you as well, right? Heh.
Drale: Oh- the elevator. Here we are. Uh... Just head on in, little buddy? It'll take us up.
[1] Moooo moo moo moo? (What's that big door next to us for?)
Drale: The- oh. Uh... It's nothing. Nothing to worry about.
Drale: It just leads to... maintenance. Yep! Just- just maintenance. Nothing else.
Drale: Into the elevator now, come on! You need a key to get in anyway, and I definitely don't have one laying around!
[2] Moo. (Moo.)
Drale: ...You're worrying me. Come on, let's get going. Into the elevator, let's get you back to normal.
Replied with 'Moo.'
Drale: So... Hey there, little... cow?
Drale: Uh. Do you- do you understand what I'm saying?
Drale: ...This is stupid. I'm talking to a cow. Of course you can't...
Drale: ...
Drale: Well I guess I could- talk at you. For a bit. If that's, heh, fine with you!
Drale: It's been tough, recently. Working towards a goal I know is important, but still feels... out of reach.
Drale: And it doesn't seem like anybody else can see that! That this is important! They look at me like I'm going crazy, and-
Drale: I'm not. I know I'm not. We need to find the ship. If we don't, who knows what...
Drale: Anyway! Here's the elevator! Just step on in, and we can head on up to the laboratory.
[1] Moooo moo moo moo? (What's that big door next to us for?)
Drale: Hrrgh- You're- you're not a cow?! Why would you... I just said all that, and you could...
Drale: D-Don't worry about the door. It's... It's nothing. Maintenance. That- that's what it is.
Drale: Er... come on, into the elevator! You want to get back to normal, right? Besides, you'd need a key to get in there, and I don't know where you'd find one of those, haha!
[2] Moo. (Moo.)
Drale: ...Moo. Yep. I agree. Come on, let's get going. Into the elevator.
Drale: So... here we are. The lab!
Drale: Just... follow me, for now. The machine is this way.
Drale: There it is! If you step into the machine, real quick, it should... it should work!

stages.title: Stage 1
hints: Farmer Cevalus: Ah, looks like a fresh recruit! Did you see my posting? Good, good.

Farmer Cevalus: Unfortunately, it so happens that my wedding ring might have slipped off as I was putting him to rest...
Farmer Cevalus: I need you to go back there and, well, recover the ring.
Farmer Cevalus: It's nothing I couldn't handle myself, of course, but the wife already suspects something, and with her dear father passing so recently...
Farmer Cevalus: Well, you see the situation I'm in? Help a poor fellow out, just go and grab that Muddy Shovel over there, and then come back to me.

Yes.

Why are you asking me that?

About .

Dig up the grave?
Yes. (Select this option to progress the quest)
Not yet...

There you go...
Now to see if you can find that ring Cevalus mentioned...

Farmer Cevalus: What's going on in there, soldier? Have you found the ring yet?
Farmer Cevalus: You really should hurry, before... nevermind! Just find the ring and get out of there!

+1 Golden Ring
Farmer Cevalus: You did it! Come back here now, so I can finally get my ring back.

stages.title: Stage 6
hints: Farmer Cevalus: Goodness, that was a little more exciting than I anticipated, hmph. Still, good work! I'm glad we were able to get rid of that monster...
Farmer Cevalus: I mean... poor father-in-law! I don't know how I'll explain this to the wife...
Farmer Cevalus: I'll take the ring now, it's rather precious to me...
-1 Golden Ring

▸ Post-Quest
Farmer Kelri: Hello there, stranger. Was there something you wanted to speak to me about?
Cevalus lost his ring.
Farmer Kelri: I should be angry but... I can't pretend to be surprised. He's always been such a forgetful oaf.
Farmer Kelri: But, it explains a lot... He's been acting weird lately, ever since dad passed. That must've been what happened, so thank you for telling me.
The previous dialogue options return.
Are you Cevalus' wife?
Farmer Kelri: That's right. The one and only, ha ha...
Farmer Kelri: We're just simple farmers, trying to get by. We were taking care of my dad until... well... yeah...
The previous dialogue options return.
Sorry for your loss.
Farmer Kelri: Thank you... It all happened so suddenly. On the day I left for Detlas, dad was as healthy as ever, but when I came back he was already buried. The sickness must have come so fast...
Farmer Kelri: But at his age, I'm not surprised... It's just regrettable that we couldn't get a priest out here in time, dad was such a pious man.
The previous dialogue options return.
What was your dad like?
Farmer Kelri: Dad... Above all, he was kind and always generous. He left us this entire farm. And very pious too, a true believer. Maybe that's why he lived so long...
Farmer Kelri: Oh, dear... If I don't stop, I'm gonna start crying again.
The previous dialogue options return.
Goodbye.
Exits the dialogue

stages.title: Stage 1
stages.task: Talk to Voer at [-2103, 59, -5427].
hints: Voer: Hello! Hmm, armour, weapon, look of grim despair... You must be from the Wynn province!
Voer: My name is Voer, and I'm an exotic plant merchant. I sell all kinds of, uh, perfectly legal goods to the magicians of Gavel.
Voer: Lately, this Decay has been making business rather tough. The magical plants that used to grow here are dying.
Voer: The need for magic has never been as big as it is now, and without supplies, the magicians of the swamp simply cannot operate!
Voer: I need Death Whistle in particular. It's not as deadly as it sounds, I promise- the name's just archaic, if I recall that from that- er, my book.
Voer: It is a rather rare plant with all sorts of mystical properties, so much so that it can animate objects around it!

You get the feeling that there's something hidden in this gravechamber...
Ye trespassers beware...
It's an extremely old book. The pages are torn, yellowed, and dusty.
The cover crumbles a touch at your grip when you open it up. How old is this?
"Top Secret”? The words are faded and hard to make out.
"Operation shadow"
It seems to be a report written at the start of the Dogun war.
"The natives occupy 90% of the habitable land in the heights.."
Several pages are dedicated to the Doguns personalities, traits and powers.
".. Magical powerhouses of the fire element.."
".. Live well into their thousands.."
"Near Dwarven intelligence.."
The report suggests that the two species would compete for space.
"Clearance is needed if Dwarves are going to form a colony.."
According to the report, the land was once rich with minerals and materials.
"Public opinion is firmly against removal of the natives.."
This page appears to have been ripped out and crudely reattached.
"Any war could result in rioting in Thanos and other established colonies."
"A program of public profiling of the natives is recommended.."
There are detailed instructions on producing propaganda against the Doguns.
".. recommend they are referred to as demons, as inherent fear will take hold.."
The report details propaganda at all levels of society, particularly at educational centers.
Several rumours are suggested to be propagated amongst the population.
"Once public opinion is sufficiently hostile, establishment of colonies will be achievable.."
The report goes on to detail the total dominance of Molten Heights and the importance of propaganda continuation.

Axelus: ...hell, they already rallied?! That's the army!
Axelus: That sounds like an entire battalion!! How did they know I was going after this?
Axelus: Dogun magic is slow! Keep me defended, this'll take awhile!
Axelus: Grr, this is harder than I thought!
Axelus: Ah! Don't let them get too close!
Axelus: Look, look! It's working!
The Rodoroc Power Core has been disrupted!
Axelus: I hate that you're having to fight my people, but I wouldn't be asking for help if it weren't needed.
Axelus: Hm...the slums should be behind this wall here. We'll lose them there.
Axelus: The power's down, but...that cannon should do to get us through. You know how to operate it, right?

stages.title: Stage 8
stages.task: Explore the Slum of Rodoroc.
hints: Axelus: Dwarvern society isn't as great as they make it out to be. The poorest are hidden away.
Axelus: The coalition has helped these people through some hard times, we can trust them.
Axelus: There's a reason I brought us here. The sewer system is connected to the royal palace. All the way to the kings bathroom.
Axelus: We need to find a way to ignite this explosive. Can you take a look around?

stages.title: Stage 9
stages.task: Find a way to enter the sewer system.
hints: Axelus: If we can convince the king that it’s not worth the fight, he may back down.
Axelus: I'm a little ashamed to admit I know my way round the sewers by now.
Axelus: You have to understand.. The people truly think the Doguns are evil incarnate. But the king knows better.

stages.title: Stage 10
stages.task: Enter the Royal Palace through the sewer pipe and find the king.
hints: Axelus: Don't let the guards catch you. Stay out of sight, got it?

stages.title: Stage 11
stages.task: Sneak past the guards and talk to the Dwarven King.
hints: King of Rodoroc: I can't say I'm surprised, Axelus. Guards, let them be.
Axelus: You know why I'm here, father. We haven't got any more chances to stop this.
King of Rodoroc: Axelus, you know why we have to maintain the lie. Think about the people, how they would react.
Axelus: We can not be responsible for the lies of our ancestors! This is ridiculous and you know it!
King of Rodoroc: Axelus, if the people found out, everything would descend to chaos. There would be riots, revolutions!
King of Rodoroc: If you hadn't turned traitor and gone gallivanting off with the Doguns, you would be in a better position to convince me.
King of Rodoroc: As it is now, you are too little and too late. The war has already begun.
King of Rodoroc: The armoury that a certain someone decided to sabotage won't make any difference.
Axelus: You will commit genocide so you don't have to face the consequences of your lies?
King of Rodoroc: I will be the hero of our nation, and my name will forever be remembered as the King who brought peace.

King of Rodoroc: I have nothing left to say to you. See yourselves out behind the throne. I'll let you use the trading tunnel to Thanos in the southern caves, if you just step back and let me handle things.

stages.title: Stage 12
stages.task: Exit the palace
hints: The Royal Guards escort you and Axelus out of the palace.
Axelus: I'm not giving up on this. I'm going back in, I know he can be reasoned with!
Axelus: Give this letter to Korzim in the Dogun village when you reach level 93.
Axelus: I'm going to have one last talk with my father.

stages.title: Stage 1
stages.task: Return to the Dogun Village with the letter and speak to Korzim.
hints: Korzim: We...have an issue. A dire one... Where is...Axelus at a time...like this?
Korzim: ...human... This is a brick.
Korzim: Oh... From Axelus, then...? He could not find...a stone? That...does not bode well.
Korzim reads the message on the tablet silently. His expression is inscrutable.
Korzim: He is trying to...reason with the Dwarven King? There is...no one else...then. You... You will have to...help.
Korzim: The chieftain is...desperate. He has enacted a...terrible plan. They are planning on summoning Garaheth.
Korzim: If they succeed...we all die. Dwarves... Doguns... Possibly even Villagers...and then... Humans as well.
Korzim: Garaheth is a...horrible demon. We used to worship him...thousands of years ago.
Korzim: I only overheard parts... But enough to be certain. They are preparing...to the south. At a disused...ritual site.
Korzim: Meet me there... Do not just attack. We may be able to...resolve it peacefully. I will wait...by the staircase.

stages.title: Stage 2
stages.task: Investigate the structure to the south.
hints: Korzim: ...I take back my statement. They have already begun... There cannot be reasoning.
Korzim: We shall take the east tower... Hide there...and watch.
Korzim: Interrupting...at this point will have...disastrous consequences. We must let them continue...and pray they fail.
Dogun Chieftain: Reach into the darkness...and grasp the hand of Garaheth to purge the intruders...
Korzim: This is a worst-case scenario... Meet me in Maex. We will talk more there...

stages.title: Stage 3
stages.task: Travel to Maex and meet Korzim at the entrance. [1446,35,-5280]
hints: Korzim: Hoho...! Over here...fine traveler! Join me at the gates!
Korzim: This dwarf voice is...horrible on my throat...but it is an effective disguise...is it not?
Korzim: We are headed to...a blacksmith in town. Follow me...
names: » Travel to Maex and meet Korzim at the

stages.title: Stage 4
stages.task: Talk to the blacksmith in Maex at 1508 45 -5298
hints: Edula: ...Korzim...what in the name of all that is holy is that disguise?
Edula: I'm flabbergasted you fooled anyone with that thing! How did you stop the beard from burning?
Edula: But, erm...more importantly, who's the buck in the fancy armour there?
Korzim: An ally...of the coalition. No time...Edula. Doguns... summoning... Garaheth.
Edula: So...so it's really down to that low, then. Burning your own house down to kill the rats.
Edula: Good thing we've got this prepared. One fallout will prevent the next. Soldier, I've got a list of materials we need!
Edula: You will need [10 Fire Webs]. The Heatscar Spiders under the town make them, there's a cave right by the entrance arch.
Edula: Then, [3 Magmatic Crystals] from the Maex mines. I'd get them myself, but...I'm banned from there since the rubber mallet incident.
Edula: Lastly, [1 Crystallized Lava]. The closest source is in the lava lake just outside Maex. There's a protruding crater in the lake.

stages.title: Stage 5
stages.task: Bring back [10 Fire Webs], [3 Magmatic Crystals], and [1 Crystallized lava].
hints: When getting Crystallized Lava:
Korzim: The crystal formation... It is definitely here.
Korzim: I will clear the lava... On my signal, move. And do not stop.
Korzim: Move! Move! MOVE!
Edula: Mhm, looks like everything's in order. Now, for a short explanation.
Edula: These materials go into crafting a special charm. It will allow you to resist demon fire.
Edula: We need to account for if they finish the summoning, so this'll help keep you safe if you end up having to square off with Garaheth.
Edula: You will need to craft it yourself, so its magic will bond to you. I've got a station just for it.
Edula: Right-click the crafting table in the back and put it together.

stages.title: Stage 6
stages.task: Craft the amulet in the crafting table.
hints: After right clicking the crafting table, remember the pattern that it displays, then repeat it. Taking a screenshot will help. If you forget what it is, exit with the button and right click the crafting table again.
if you don't take your items out you will lose them.
Korzim: We must... visit... Sanba... the enchanter.

stages.title: Stage 7
stages.task: Go to the enchanter and enchant the amulet.
hints: Sanba: Erm...Korzim, what on earth are you doing here? It's not safe for you!
Sanba: Wait, that amulet...oh no, really? Okay, I know what^s going on.
Sanba: We're going to need to give this a little extra kick if you're going to use this for what I think you are.
Sanba: A pinch of fire scarab tail, splash of sulphur, exactly three ounces of old brimstone...!
Sanba: Infunde hoc monile, alta intra monte. Magia!
Sanba: Meet me in the back, we can't talk out here. You never know who's listening...

stages.title: Stage 8
stages.task: Enter the storage room in the enchanter's house.
hints: Sanba: Supposing you're here to help, Soldier. Garaheth's being summoned if you're getting this...
Sanba: Axelus prepped a contingency plan for this, but having to put it in action is surreal. Let me fill you in.
Sanba: That dragon skeleton lying in the Heights belonged to an Ice Drake. Centuries ago, it was used in the Dogun wars.
Sanba: It had incredibly potent magic, particularly in its icy breath. The area it hit is still frozen to this day, and shows no signs of thaw.
Sanba: According to Axelus' stories, its breath travelled through the tunnels and coalesced someplace deep within...
Sanba: ...becoming True Ice, a potent mixture of sheer cold and magic energy. That's what we will need to combat Garaheth.'
Sanba: If you bring me [4 True Ice] I can make a staff capable of harnessing it...and we can freeze Garaheth in its tracks.
Sanba: Head north to the Freezing Heights and make your way to the top, now! We've got no time at all!

stages.title: Stage 9
stages.task: Travel to the frozen heights and find 4 True Ice.
hints: Korzim: ... This... This used to be...a Dogun town. The Dwarves rendered it barren.
Korzim: They used the Drake... They chained it up and...forced it to attack. We had to kill it...
Korzim: It... froze my town... as it died. I was there... 900 years ago.
Korzim: I know the way... into the caves.
Korzim: The True Ice...is deep inside. I will struggle to...stay warm here.
Korzim: I will try to run through...as quickly as possible. The ice is...painful.
Korzim: We must... move fast... or... we will both.... freeze.
Korzim: Maybe... I am... hotter than... I thought... do you.. Hear that?
Korzim: Oh no... I think... It's... COLLAPSING.
Korzim: My... feet are... solid... Keep... running.
Korzim: This is it... The thing that... Killed my families... [4 True Ice].
The ice still scalding your hands with cold, you make your way back to Maex.

stages.title: Stage 10
stages.task: Return to the enchanter with the True Ice.
hints: Sanba: Impressive, you two. Must've been tough to get that...doubly so for Korzim.
Sanba: Here is the staff, . Keep it safe, and don't you go dying on us.
Sanba: My husband and I will round up the coalition and get them to act now. We need to get going before-
A door slamming open is heard in the distance...
Sanba: ...that's the barracks door. That's the barracks door!!
Maex Soldier: Men! We have to meet for briefing on the surface, the war is due any hour now! Move faster!
Sanba: They're already going?! We're out of time! Korzim is waiting for you just upstairs when you reach level 94. Go train! NOW!
