stages.title: Stage 1
stages.task: Return to Korzim on the second floor of the enchanter in Maex with the Amulet of Fire Resistance and the Staff of True Ice.
hints: Korzim: ...Do you have...the staff? And the amulet...?
Korzim: The war is starting... and Axelus... He has not returned.
Korzim: We can not go... Not without him. Find him... And bring him to the... Dogun village.
Korzim: I can not leave. The guard...it is on high alert. He was last at Rodoroc...yes?

stages.title: Stage 2
stages.task: Head to Rodoroc and look for Axelus.
hints: Soldier: The first group has already started their climb, let's hurry.
Rodoroc Citizen: Hey! Everyone, the king has someone in the cage! It's been years since we used it!
Rodoroc Citizen: Wait, that's Axelus up there!! The king locked up his son?! What in the world?
Rodoroc Citizen: I heard he was consorting with demons, but that can't possibly be true, can it?
Axelus: For the last time, they are not demons!! Gods, I've been telling you this whole time! Not even my father will listen to reason!
Axelus: If I don't get freed we're doomed, you hear me?! We won't survive another war! As your prince I demand to be freed!
Axelus: Listen, the statues are climbable and there's a control panel for the lava siphons near them! Now help me so we all don't die!

stages.title: Stage 3
stages.task: Free Axelus and escape the city.
hints: To the right of the signs below where Axelus is kept prisoner, there is a red carpet that stars on the left statue legs and leads to some parkour to the button that releases Axelus.|freeing Axelus}}
Rodoroc Citizen: Wait, that human just defaced the hero's monument!! Are they working with the demons too?
Axelus: ! I didn't think you'd be back, but we need to leave, now! Meet me outside!
Axelus: ! Over here, to the right! By the cannon! I'm commandeering this thing.
Axelus: We need to get up to the Doguns before the Dwarves begin their assault, or before the Doguns take their last resort.
Axelus: Get in the cannon, now! You've got your armour, you might end up charred and covered in soot but you'll be fine!
Axelus: Don't tell anyone we shot ourselves out of a cannon, I'll never live it down. Now come on, to the Dogun village, hurry!
Axelus: If the Doguns are taking their last resort and summoning Garaheth, then we've got two sides to stop at once...basically, the odds are astronomically against us.
Axelus: That means you do what you need to do, no matter what. Understood? If we can stop this madness then the casualties won't have died for nothing! Now move!
A hole in the wall has been opened...

stages.title: Stage 4
stages.task: Reach the portal and stop Garaheth.
hints: Follow the path and kill enemies to destroy the walls. To fire the cannon right click it with the cannon ball, gotten by killing one of the enemies. It will be very obvious when you reach the portal.
Axelus: WAIT, STOP THE-
Dogun Chieftain: Quiet. Dwarven whelp...we will not go quietly. AWAKEN.
Axelus: I can't believe this... That bone was part of the ritual?! Agh, how could we have been so STUPID! You're all lucky we prepared for this!!
Axelus: You need to get inside him. He's still chained! The amulet will protect you from the heat! Freeze him from the inside out!!

stages.title: Stage 5
stages.task: Enter the body of Garaheth.

stages.title: Stage 6
stages.task: Find all 4 organs and destroy them.
hints: Right clicking the green particles with the Staff of True Ice will solidify the organ. Do this 4 times to progress. The last organ requires an item dropped by the boss of the room.|destroying the organs}}

stages.title: Stage 7
stages.task: Leave Garaheth and exit his realm.
hints: Axelus: EVERYONE, STOP THIS! RIGHT NOW!! IT'S OVER!!
Axelus: Open your eyes for once in your lives!! You see that?! Behind me! THAT was going to be the end result!
Axelus: Garaheth would have killed every one of us, damn it! Are you that short-sighted that you can't see this?!
Axelus: Everyone here is to blame, except the human who helped stop this! The Doguns were already exiled, they wouldn't have hurt anyone!
Axelus: But we couldn't just let ANYTHING be! You always need more glory, more, more, MORE! Don't you, Draani? I'm ashamed to be your lineage!
Axelus: And you, Doguns! I...I pitied you. You were wronged, but you resort to this? You'd doom the world over to spite the Dwarves? Is that it?!
Dogun Chieftain: Whelp. You do not understand. To be persecuted...and see your people tortured...hunted.
Dwarven Commander: You all deserve it! You attacked out [sic] ancestors for sport! Eye for an eye, have you heard of it? It's only fair!
Dogun Chieftain: Imbeciles...your stories are not true. We... We lived through the war. You took everything...and suffered none.
Axelus: I've been trying to tell BOTH of you that the monarchy has been spreading lies for centuries! One bad king doesn't mean the whole species is a loss!
Dogun Chieftain: Shut your mouth. Even now...you trample on the bones of our god... You have taken everything from us...
Dogun Chieftain: This earth is stained by you. We...we shall burn you...and scatter your ash to the wind.
Axelus: DON'T YOU DARE! STOP, RIGHT NOW!
Korzim: Axelus!
Korzim: ...he..
Korzim: You would... You would kill a savior...?
King of Rodoroc: No, no! No no no, this can't be happening! H-Hang on, we'll save you, I...I'll do something, I...
King of Rodoroc: Y-You DEMONS! MONSTERS! I'll avenge you, Axelus, j-just give me time-
Axelus: AGH, SHUT UP! SHUT...ack... Q-Quiet. Listen to one damn word from my mouth, Draani... For once in your miserable life
Axelus: Tell. The. TRUTH!! G-gaagh...you know that's th...the only way to stop this. Swallow your pride, you...old fool...
King of Rodoroc: I...I... Axelus... He...he called me Draani...why did...?
King of Rodoroc: Men, stand down. This... This war is over! I will not have one more life lost! Touch the Doguns and I'll personally behead you!
King of Rodoroc: Chief, I...I ask of you but an hour of your time. If you are willing to negotiate...
A few hours later...

stages.title: Stage 8
stages.task: Speak with the King of Rodoroc and the Dogun Chieftain.
hints: King of Rodoroc: Ah, you've arrived. I...actually remember you from earlier. So you and...
King of Rodoroc: A-and...
King of Rodoroc: ...you knew my son. Were helping him try to put an end to this, before everything was too far gone. Heh...apologies, for that.
King of Rodoroc: Paku and I have had a long discussion about the wisdom of youth over the old. You all were right. I needed to swallow my pride.
Dogun Chieftain: We agreed upon a peace treaty... A new city... The Dwarves will aid us in building it.
Dogun Chieftain: All hostilities...will end. My people will...be free to roam the caverns. It has been...too long.
King of Rodoroc: And the entombed Doguns at Courag will be reconstituted, as well, supposing that is a possibility.
King of Rodoroc: Every king, since my so-far-great grandfather, Draani Thunderwill, has battled with their morality over the lies told to my people.
King of Rodoroc: It ends here, with the name Draani VIII. It will take time, but the bloodshed has proven things must begin to change now.
King of Rodoroc: You and the coalition have saved the Heights, and Gavel. In Maex, you will find a stall to trade valuable minerals. You will be granted special Dwarven privileges to purchase it now.
King of Rodoroc: Though that is...almost certainly not enough a reward for everything you have done...sincerely. Thank you, Wynn soldier.
= Tips =
If you die inside Garaheth, just go through the portal to attempt the bossfight again.
If you accidentally warp back to Rodoroc after teleporting to the conference in Stage 8, just go through the portal.

stages.title: Stage 3
stages.task: Navigate the mansion to the room holding the journal
hints: The solution is:
- Walk into the room with a button on an emerald block.
- Click the button two times, so that the light gray carpet in the room directly above the button is facing north (the same direction in which the button that you have to press is positioned).
- From the room with the colored carpets, go north once, down once, east once, south once, up twice, and west once to reach a room on the third floor with another button on an emerald block.
- Press the button on the third floor once.
- From the room with the button, go east once, south once, and then west twice to the end of the hallway, until you reach a hole in the floor.
- Jump down two stories, kill and collect the book, and exit the mansion.
You can also use your movement spell (teleport on mage, escape on archer, charge on warrior, vanish on assassin, haul on shaman), to go through a ceiling hole.

Quill: Hello, everyone. Let us begin.
Quill: I trust everyone has taken the time to process last night's announcement? I will let Syndra take over shortly, but first, I would like to thank each and every one of you.
Quill: I won't mince words. This is dangerous work. What we are planning puts us at great risk. But this is what it takes to change Fruma, to put an end to the crown's oppression!
Quill: We will kill a God! And we will all be free. Now, Syndra?
Syndra gets onto the table.
Syndra: Thank you, Quill. To begin, allow me to give each group their assignment.
Syndra: Mora and Yuman, you will be infiltrating the guards' outpost in Timasca to retrieve their schedules. Get in, note down the formations, and get out.
Syndra: Mora, you're familiar with military structure, and Yuman knows his way around Timasca. I expect you two should be able to make it work.
Yuman: Yes, ma'am!
Mora: Understood. However, I have a few concerns with the overall plans... I'll speak with you later.
Syndra: Yusanu and Sui, you'll be constructing explosives that we can use as distractions during the festival to draw guards away from the main stage.
Syndra: I trust Yusanu knows what he's doing, so Sui, you'll be acting as an assistant.
Sui: Um... sure.
Yusanu: Works for me. I might already have some blueprints lying around somewhere...
Syndra: Zeph and Rex, I want you to scout the city rooftops for potential spots where Rex and Yulie can provide aerial support... in case it's necessary.
Zeph: Yeah, I c- c- can do that.
Rex: Copy that.
Syndra: Quill and Yulie, you two know your way around the city. I'll need you to scout out potential escape routes from the city... again, in case things go badly.

Yulie: ...yes. I think I have a few places in mind already.
Syndra: Finally. Player, I want you to be adaptable. Help out wherever it's needed - I'm sure your skills will come in handy.

Syndra: I was about to suggest the same thing. Then let us adjourn this meeting. Good luck, everyone.
Mora: Hum. Player and Yuman, let us go our plans then.

Yuman: Alright, guys! So, any plans? What're we cooking with here?

Rex: We've... ugh, we've all lost people. Lots of Leaves got arrested for... this or that, over the years. It sucked, but... it happened.
Rex: ...it's never been this bad before. Never anyone this close. I mean... sigh. Syndra and Mora. Gods.
Rex: I want to help her get through this, but... she's closing herself off. And... we're still not home free just yet.
Rex: ...when it's over. When it's over. Everything will be okay when it's over.
The dialogue options reappear.
Let's go.
Rex: After you!
The dialogue ends here.
Talking to Zeph in the hotel room:
Zeph: Hey Player.
Zeph: I'm r-ready to see my old friends again... I miss Kaio.
Zeph: Was there s-something on your mind?
How are you really?
Zeph: Ah... I... I don't want to lie to you.
Zeph: So... I'm not d-doing great. Everytime I... I close my eyes I s-see that... face. The S-sovereign...
Zeph: Everytime I close my e-eyes I feel all that pain. All of it! All the m-memories!
Zeph: I was... okay with it all e-ending there.
Zeph: I know that i-it's over. I know Gikyo is dead but... their ghost still h-haunts me.
The dialogue options reappear.
What do you think of the plan?
Zeph: I think it's a s-solid plan.
Zeph: I j-just wonder how many from the Leaves in the Wind are willing to a-actually come all the way here.
Zeph: Kaio for s-sure...
The dialogue options reappear.
Let's go.
Zeph: Meet you t-there.
The dialogue ends here.
Rex: Well, here we are. The dam really is something to behold, isn't it...
Zeph: I- I always d..did wonder what it'd b- b- be like to... to t...take this elevator...
Sui: Well, you'll finally get your chance. Come on, let's just fight already.
Rex: Sui. We can't just-
Sui: What? We can't rush this? The longer we wait, the more suspicious they'll get.
Rex: ...fine. Is everyone ready?
Let's do this!
Rex: Then let's do this!
The dialogue ends here.
Give me a moment...
Sui: ...don't keep us waiting, okay?
The dialogue ends without progressing the quest.
Everyone charges forward to attack the guards of the elevator.

stages.title: Stage 4
stages.task: Talk to the group again at [-1610, 124, -1051].
hints: Interacting with the group:
Sui: ...oh. It's over already.
Sui: Sigh. Whatever. Let's go... get our people.
Zeph: S- S- Sui, wait-
Rex: Guys! There's more soldiers approaching!
A cutscene plays of Sui killing the straggling group of soldiers. Rex saves Sui by shooting a guard when Sui's back is turned.
Interacting with the group:
Rex: Sui, are you INSANE?! You almost got SHOT!
Sui: I... didn't see him.
Rex: You turned your back when there were enemies still around!! What do you think would have happened if we weren't here?
Sui: ...
Rex: Shot. If you were lucky, somewhere that wouldn't have killed - but after what they saw, would they have really taken that risk?!
Sui: ...
Rex: Sui, stop being so reckless. You're... you're strong, I get that, but... that doesn't mean you're invincible.
Zeph: S...Sui, we don't w- want to l- lo- lose you too...
Sui: But if I'm not good enough, if I'm not f-fast enough, then- then- then I'll lose you, and- and I can't, I can't do that again, I-
Rex: Sui! Breathe!
Sui: ...
Rex: You don't need to prove yourself. You've always been good enough for us.
Rex: Whatever that- that Sovereign said to you, to make you think everything's that's happened to us is your fault? It's not true!
Rex: Sui. Sui. Mora's death is not your fault!! We can blame the crown, blame the Sovereigns- hell, blame me for leaving him there!!!
Rex: But it wasn't your responsibility to protect him. To protect us. We're a team - a family, and... and I don't want to see you burn yourself to ash like Syndra did.
Sui: ...
Zeph: R...Rex is r- right, Sui. We can... f- fi- fight together, sh...shore up each o- oth... each other's w...weaknesses.
Sui: ...okay.
Zeph: ...b- but we should pr...probably get going, Sui, b- before more backup sh...shows up.
Rex: Sigh. Zeph's right. You guys hurry to the Leaves, while we have the chance. Player and I will prepare for your return.
Sui and Zeph head to the elevator.
Rex: ...ugh.
Let's meet the Canopy.
Rex: Y... yeah. You're right, we should go too. Come on, let's meet at the Canopy's cave.
The dialogue ends here.
You were kind of hard on her.
Rex: A little. But... I don't know how else to get through to her.
Rex: It's so... frustrating! Seeing her taking on all of Syndra's worst traits! I- I know what to look out for, this time, but...
Rex: ...but I still don't know what to do.
Rex: Ha. Maybe I should apply my own advice to myself...
Rex: We should get moving too. Come on, let's meet at the Canopy's cave.
The dialogue ends here.

stages.title: Stage 5
stages.task: Travel to the Mistwoods and find the Canopy in their new hideout at [-1459, 31, -549].
hints: Talking to Rex at the elevator again:
Rex: Well? Let's go.
Upon approaching the destination:
Canopy Fox: Halt! Intruders!
Rex walks up to the guards.
Canopy Fox: Quick, call Captain Cileon-
Captain Rurie walks out of the hideout.
Rurie: Oh, good grief. Look more closely, foxes - these are familiar faces! Or rather, familiar face, I should say - welcome back to the Canopy, Player! And who might this be?
Rex: ...you're Captain Rurie, right? Sui told us about you.
Rurie: Did she! Then that must mean you are one of the dear captured friends - no no, don't tell me, I can figure it out... Rex, I assume?
Rurie: Hm... now, I would bring you in, but then Fuhue might have my head for not following her many numerous protocols... and we certainly can't have that...
Fuhue: Ugh, just let them in, Rurie. We've been breaking initiation protocols left and right already, I can't be bothered enforcing them anymore.
Rurie: Well, would you look at that! Lucky you! Come on in, come on in. Our numbers have grown since last you were here, Player - many more friendly faces hanging about!
Rurie and Rex enter the hideout. The members of the Steel Feather are inside.
Yuman: Player, Rex!! Man, it's good to see you guys!!
Rex: Yuman?! What're you doing here? I thought they had you locked up in-
Yuman: In Deraj Prison, yup. Everything they say about it is true- and, and more! They get you workin' in the mines, if you're not... eh, y'know. Disappeared.
Yuman: Lucky us, these Canopy guys showed up and broke us out! There were explosions, and growing plants, and crashing waves, and- and-
Yuman: And then the feathery birds showed up outta nowhere, like- nothing there, then poof, cloud of smoke, and there they are- and they got us outta there!
Rex: I'm sorry... Rurie. You all... successfully broke into Gravity's Monolith?! And got people out?!
Rurie: Ah, it wasn't so tough once we had the plans of their inner workings! Floorplans, guard rotations... the works.
Rurie: That Warden's a deadly foe, but he sticks to an incredibly firm schedule - out like a light once it turns 9 PM! Of course, the prison goes into lockdown, but we've got our ways around it.
Cileon: Special guard access. Useful.
Rurie: Right you are Cileon, right you are... well, we'll have time to discuss the details later! I must return to my owls, there's much left to do!
Rurie exits.
Yuman: ...
Yuman: Is, uh... is Zeph alright? I overheard a couple of things about what you two went through, so...
Rex: What? You worried about him?
Yuman: Huh? Pfft, nah, 'course not.
Yuman: ...but maybe a little, yeah.
Rex: He's alright. He and Sui will be here later, so you can ask him about it yourself.
Yuman: Oh! Oh, ha, uh, alright- sure, that sounds good, yep.
Yuman: I'm gonna... get back to my bro up there. Talk to ya more later!
Yuman heads toward Yusanu in the hideout.
Rex: ...
Rex: I should talk to the Canopy's leader, get started on some planning. Come by when you're done talking with everyone, okay?
Rex heads toward Azael in the hideout.
There are several NPCs that can be interacted with inside the hideout.
Talking to either Canopy Fox at the hideout entrance:
Canopy Fox: Player. Welcome to the Canopy.
Canopy Fox: Your friend has entered the hideout already, please make yourself at home.
Talking to Captain Cileon:
Cileon: Hm.
What're you doing?
Cileon: Foxes. Guard.
Cileon: Is important.
Talking to Quill and Yulie:
Quill: Ah, Player. I'm glad to see you are well.
Quill: These have been... a difficult few weeks. For all of us, I gather. We have... been informed of our losses.
Yulie: I still can't believe we let her talk us into... into all of that!
Quill: Yulie, let's not speak ill of the dead. We cannot change the past. We can only move forward.
Quill: ...I, too, regret not standing my ground. For her sake, if nothing else.
Quill: Sigh... her grief and rage consumed her, in the end, and I did little to stop it. I- ahh- my back...
Yulie: Quill, you need to rest. Sit down for a while, please.
Quill: No, no... I'm fine, Yulie. We have work to do, after all.
What's wrong?
Yulie: Well, the guards at the prison didn't really care much about who was physically fit to work or not. They just... work you 'tll you're dead, I guess!
Quill: Harsh treatment, certainly... but I suppose it is no different than the Roughworks, at its core. Only... less obscured.
Yulie: ...
Yulie: Player, Yusanu told us that he only made it through because of you and Sui. So... thank you. For protecting my little brother when I couldn't.
Quill: Yes... thanks to yours and Sui's magic, I hear...
Where's everyone else?
Yulie: From the Steel Feather? The Canopy has quarters built deeper in these caverns. Anyone uninterested in fighting is staying there, for the time being.
Quill: ...those we could find, at least. There are many we are still missing, unfortunately. I pray they are still alive.
Quill: Perhaps when this is all over, we will be able to locate the rest... I can only hope so.
Yusanu: ...so, look, if we try to charge these in this specific order-
Fuhue: No, wait. Your sequence is charging Thunder twice in a row here, when it should only do it once. Too much of a charge, and-
Yusanu: -and it'll destabilize, right. Thanks for double checking my work, Fuhue.
What are you doing?
Yusanu: ...oh, Player??? I- I completely didn't... notice you were here...
Yuman: Yeesh. You've gotta fix your lack of awareness, bro. Anyone could sneak up on you while you're hyper focused in on something!
Yusanu: Ugh, yeah, yeah, you keep telling me- if you're not going to be helpful, stop hovering!
Yuman: Nah. I wanna see the cool stuff happen when you get it working! Don't want to miss the fireworks or any-
Fuhue: To answer your question, Player, Yusanu believes he has a working theory on the Resonance Weaver's functionality.
Yusanu: Yeah, but a working theory doesn't mean a whole lot if I can't get results...
Yusanu: Look, these five glyphs - they correspond almost exactly to the ones the Canopy's talismans use. Fire, Water, Earth, Air, Thunder.
Yusanu: They can be charged to activate them - a simple burst on its own, maybe, but if chained together... you get something more complex.
Yusanu: Resonance... resonance, resonance, resonance... Soosu was always saying there was something she could not see with her blessing. Intangible, not of the elements...
Yusanu: Maybe... if we could find it, we could use the Weaver to... to visualize it. Bind it in place, so we can see it...
Yuman: ...yeah, none of that made any sense to me. Explain it with easier words?
Yusanu: Okay, sure, just for you. Invisible thing in the air. With device, we make it visible.
Yuman: Oh! Why didn't ya start with that!
Yusanu: Ugh... you're insufferable.
Fuhue: Ahem. Will we try the updated chain?
Yusanu: Right, right... got distracted. Thanks, Yuman.
Yusanu: Here we go...
An oscillating tendril appears out of the Resonance Weaver.
Yuman: Huh?!
Fuhue: What is that?
Yusanu: I... I don't know, but... I think it's working! Fuhue, we did it!
Yusanu: Maybe if I touch it, something will...
DON'T!
Yusanu: Wh- wha?! What's wrong?!
I think I know what it is.
You tell them about the Corruption you've seen in Wynn. About what it does to the land and the people.
You... don't tell them why you think it's here. About the Queen. It'd be best to tell everyone at the same time.
Yusanu: ...
Fuhue: And what, exactly, is this doing here? A blight that permeates the air... concerning. I'll have to speak to Master Azael.
Yuman: Well, uh... now that it is here, can we do anything with it? Like... charge the glyphs to manipulate it?
Yusanu: M... maybe. I'll have to do some thinking. But for now, it'd probably be best to... get rid of it. If I hit all five at once, it should...
Yusanu disables the Resonance Weaver.
Yusanu: ...there. Gods. Why did the Queen need this thing in the first place...?
I'll tell you later.
Yusanu: ...yeah, sure, why not. Later. I guess I've got to clean up here anyway.
Yusanu: Seeing as... is that Rex over there? Oh, good. Well, seeing as she's plotting with Azael, I should get ready for that.
Yusanu: Yuman, could you help me out? Since you've been annoying me all day.
Yuman: Ughhhhhhh.... fine. See ya, Player.
Interacting with Yusanu and Yuman again:
Yusanu: ...
Yuman: ...I missed you, man.
Yusanu: Yeah. Yeah, me too.
Arnol only appears in the cave hideout at [-1488, 35, -523] if The Strong Survive has been completed.
Arnol: I've been looking forward to seeing you again, Player. That is your real name, right?
Arnol: It feels like it's been ages since we last spoke. As you can probably guess, a lot has changed for me since then.
How did you get here?
Arnol: After we took out Commander Ferreo, there was nowhere for me to go, but I knew I needed to leave the Highlands and head somewhere I wouldn't be recognized.

Arnol: I couldn't risk taking the train, so sneaking into the Mistwoods at night was my only option. I had no idea what could be waiting for me there, but I had to go quickly, before they would start looking for me.
Arnol: I took the easternmost exit out of the Highlands, and by some miracle, snuck through to the Mistwoods after quietly taking out a guard.
Arnol: From there, I blindly stumbled across the region, terrified of what would find me. I was eventually knocked out by a Canopy scout, who took me into their hideout to be questioned.
Arnol: I told them the truth, about who I was, where I came from, and what I had done... They didn't believe me until I described you, and what you had done for me.
Arnol: Even after we split ways, you were still there to look out for me!
Arnol: Of course, they didn't trust me immediately, I still had to prove myself. I've learned more here than I would have ever had at Fort Tericen.

Arnol: And now, I can call myself a resistance member, same as you. I've thought a lot about my goals since we were recruits. I want Fruma to be rid of corruption, like what we saw with Commander Ferreo.
Arnol: The resistance is the best chance we have at achieving this goal, I'm sure you've realised this too. I am ready to risk my life fighting for a better future for Fruma!
The dialogue ends here.
I'm glad you're ok.
Arnol: I could be saying the same thing, but the people here have told me that you can handle yourself just fine.
Arnol: I must admit, my time with the resistance has been very difficult. But I can finally say I am fighting for a cause I truly believe in.
Arnol: Deep down in my heart, I've always known I could never live up to the expectations my family had for me. Here, I no longer have to worry about that.
Arnol: I was so alone, Player, I truly can't thank you enough for being there for me...
The dialogue ends here.
I'm sorry for lying to you.
Arnol: You have nothing to be sorry for, I completely understand why you couldn't tell me the truth.
Arnol: What matters the most is that you helped me escape Fort Tericen when you found out that I was in danger.
The dialogue ends here.
Rex and Azael are found at the top of the hideout at [-1455, 39, -535].
Talking to Rex and Azael:
Rex: ...and if we route through the tunnels - we have a couple options for city sectors...
Azael: Yes, I see. It would be worth your while to compare notes with Captain Fuhue, she can help narrow it down.
Azael: ...ah, Player. Young Rex and I were just speaking on our options moving forward. Would you like to join us for this discussion?
Sure! (Selecting this option progresses the quest)
Not yet.
Rex: Well... go, then! Go talk to people, you have time.
The dialogue ends without progressing the quest.
After choosing the Sure! dialogue option:
Rex: Alright! So, Player, here's the deal. If we want to take out the crown, we'll need to hit it at its root - the Queen, the Citadel, and her Royal Palace.
Rex: We're not getting through the front gates, obviously... they're too defended. But we don't need to take the gates - we can come in from below.
Azael: The caverns and catacombs beneath the Citadel are quite expansive. Captain Rurie has-
Rurie jumps down from the nearby tunnel and walks over to Azael.
Rurie: Ah, was that my name I just overheard! We're speaking about the tunnels, are we? If you're hoping to traverse them, I'm the man for the job!

Rurie: It's quite an extensive network, really... the owls and I have spent years mapping each and every inch of it - and we still haven't seen it all! It's very interesting - and that's not to mention-
Fuhue walks up from below and stands next to Rurie.
Fuhue: Get to the point already, Rurie. They want to reach the Citadel through the tunnels. Is that possible?
Yulie and Quill walk up from below and join the group.
Rurie: Hmph. Possible, it certainly is... though results may vary. Looking for something in particular?
Fuhue: Something easy to take, and easily defensible. University is out of the question... too large. The barracks are out of the question... maybe the Industrial Zone? Someone get me a map-
Yusanu and Yuman walk up from below and join the group.
Quill: If I- ahh- if I may interrupt... I believe the Market Square should fit the criteria you are looking for.
Quill: It is closed off, and only lightly guarded in comparison to the rest of the Citadel... or, at least, it was in my time.
Fuhue: Hm... it could work. Rurie?
Rurie: The Market Square, you say? Yes... yes, I believe it could work! The path is long and winding, but should be plenty large enough to fit a strike team.
Sui and Zeph enter the hideout. Cileon walks to the middle of the hideout.
Rex: Good! Captain Rurie, would you be able to map out that route so we can-
Sui, Zeph, and Kaio walk up to the middle with Cileon.
Cileon: Attention! Visitors.
Sui: Oh... everyone's, um, here.
Yuman jumps down to the middle.
Yuman: Zeph!!!
Zeph: Y...Yuman?! Y- you- you're here? Y...you're okay?
Yuman: 'Course I am, princess! What, were you worried?
Sui: Are you done? Weren't we here to plan our next moves?
Sui walks to the upper area with the main group.
Yuman: ...yeesh. Cold. But I guess-
Yuman, Zeph, and Kaio all walk up to the main group.
Sui: So we're attacking the Citadel through the tunnels?
Azael: Indeed, we are. It seems we have decided on the Market Square? We will take control of the sector to serve as a launching point for future operations.
Sui: If that's the only thing we attack, won't the crown immediately realize what we're doing?
Rex: Hm... yeah, I guess you're right. We'll want to stage a few more attacks elsewhere, divert their attention...
Sui: We could launch an attack at the gates?
Zeph: Wh- wh- what?! Sui, y...you can't just th- throw yourself at-
Sui: Just enough to draw their attention! N-not to try and break through, obviously. We kill a few soldiers, then retreat.
Sui: If... if we can make them think we're trying the gates, then they won't see the group coming through the tunnels.
Rurie: Clever, indeed... I suppose we could spare some of our best fighters for such a task. Cileon, perhaps you might be interested?
Cileon: ...yes.
Rurie: Wonderful! Then I suppose it's settled? One team to the gates, one team through the tunnels- and, naturally, a team to handle communication-
Kaio: Ahem- a moment of your time? Now, admittedly, I may be a tad outta my depth here- but y'all are talkin' a whole lot 'bout fighting?
Kaio: And it seems to me you're disregarding somethin' quite vital. The crown sure ain't lacking in strength... it can always train up new folks to replace the lost. S'done it time n' time again.
Kaio: But where the crown really lives and dies is the public opinion. Y'know, the whole... ehm, "ordeal" at the Roughworks Festival - it's caused a real stir in the people.
Kaio: Sovereigns turnin', public exe-... sigh. Public executions. The people ain't happy. Wouldn't take much to... push 'em over the edge.
Kaio: Now, the crown's got the tools to deal with violence. What it don't got is the tools to deal with civil unrest, 'least not quickly. So it might do well to give that a go as well.
Rex: That... makes sense. Though, I'm not sure we have the means for something like that...
Sui: We could ask the Blossom of Blades.
Rex: What?! Ugh, no, they're useless. It was a miracle you got anything out of them the first time, Sui! Trying again is just gonna be a waste of effort.
Sui: No, it won't. Because it'll work. Player and I, we can talk to them, we can... we can work something out.
Rex: ...fine. If you want to try, fine. But when it doesn't work - which it won't - remember that I told you so.
Yulie: Okay. So you've got two distractions. But you're forgetting the most important problem - there is a GOD to worry about. If she catches on, you're done for.
Zeph: Y...yeah... We- we need a way t...to make sure she d- does- doesn't show up...
You suddenly remember. Tasim told you the Queen wanted to speak to you. Maybe you could get an audience...?
She wanted to meet with me.
Everyone: What?!
I could get an audience.
Rex: ...and... distract her that way...
Azael: A move with great risk, certainly. But one that solves our remaining problems if successful.
Zeph: Player, a...are you s- sure about this?
Yes.
Rurie: Well, then it's settled! To divert the crown's attention - a strike team at the gates, unrest from the gossip group, and Player turning themself in!
Quill: There are still several days to go before the Highlands Festival... perhaps it could be wise to detail our- aah- our plans further in that time?
Azael: Indeed. Though, before we dismiss this strategy meeting... Yusanu, you have been hard at work on that stolen device, yes?
Yusanu: Yeah. I... think I know how it works, but it's... hard to operate - it's very abstract, needing to figure out which glyphs to activate to get an intended result-
Yusanu: But. One thing we managed to do was... reveal some invisible force in the air. Player said it was... dangerous. And it's, uh... kind of everywhere.
Yusanu: I don't know why the Queen needed this device. But Player said they might have an idea, and that they'd tell everyone here.
Tell them what you know.
You tell them about the War of the Realms. Of Light and Dark and War.
You tell them about Corruption. About how it has affected Wynn, and how the recruits Fruma sends help keep it at bay.
You tell them about the Queen. About what she is, what she was. That killing her won't be as easy as-
Rex: So what?
What?
Rex: I said, so what? We already knew we were facing up against a god. We already knew that wasn't gonna be easy!!
Zeph: Y...yeah... It's a l- li... a little scary, h- hearing about... a- all that... but we can w...worry about it later, r- ri- right?
Sui: Doesn't really matter what she is. She's still going to die.
Fuhue: It's good information to have. It'll help us formulate the specifics of our plans better. Master Azael, could I have a word with you?
Azael: Ah, yes, certainly. Very well, everyone is dismissed. Get some rest, while you still can - these next few days will be very busy!
The camera goes black.
Everyone has dispersed into various groups.. you can talk to them, or go rest right now.

stages.title: Stage 6
stages.task: Rest in the Canopy at [-1490, 37, -525].
hints: Yulie: ...
Yulie: Hey, Player.
Yulie: Sigh. This is all... going a bit over my head.
Yulie: Feels like everyone's forgotten why we tried to stay out of trouble for so long.
Yulie: We're making big plans to... storm the Citadel, take down the Crown, kill- kill an actual, living God!
Yulie: And... I don't know. It's too much. It's too risky. What are we going to do if it all fails?
Yulie: Quill and I, we used to be the ones who considered that. Considered the safety of everyone in the Steel Feather.
Yulie: And- and look, it sucks that Syndra died, it does. But I really wish she would have left us alone. She got Quill feeling guilty again, and...
Yulie: And there's real stuff to feel guilty about. Of course there is. But there's nothing he can really do about it now. So that guilt isn't really serving a purpose anymore.
Yulie: ...whatever. At this point, I just have to keep my bros safe. I can't change anything else, so that's all that matters.
Talking to Yulie again:
Yulie: Good luck, Player.
Yusanu: It's... good to see you again, Sui. I- I'm glad you were able to find Rex and Zeph.
Sui: Yeah... it's good. I'm, um, glad you got your brothers back too.
Sui: ...
Sui: Um... Yusanu. I wanted to-
Yusanu: Hey. It's fine. You don't have to apologize for being upset after... y-yeah. And, it's not like I was exactly being helpful...
Yusanu: So. It's alright. Water- ha- under the bridge, right?
Sui: ...heh. Yeah. Alright.
Rex: ...
Rex: So, Yusanu, you've been... working on that device, right? How's that been?
Yusanu: Slow... but, I think... I think I'm glad I've had it to work on? Because- because everything at the festival would've still... happened, without it.

Inspiration from Ancient Tales (-16045, 20770):
In founding this dojo, I was inspired by many a tale. I was many a time scoffed at by others, for taking stock in the legends of old...
And yet the results speak for themselves. As of the time writing this, being 997 AP, I am 76 years old.
Despite this, I am still in great health! Surely the years are catching up to me, but many I know are far less able by the same age.
By following the old ways, I have prospered and allow others to prosper in kind. By looking to the past, I am preparing myself for the future.
Many forget the power one's body can rise to, thanks to the prevalence of magical practices. Although magical knowledge is itself important, and I am guilty of neglecting it myself.
But the tales and practices of ancient warriors and kings, such as Remikas, or even modern soldiers such as Tisaun Sodeta, have great value.
Here, I will tell of what tales have brought me my wisdom, my power, and my health, and pass that knowledge onto you, dear reader.
...though this is a fascinating read, you're already going through a lot of what is described in the book, and it hasn't brought you tranquility.
Guide to Meditation (-16050, 20770):
To meditate is to remove all distractions, and to peacefully introspect- to be at one with yourself and anchor yourself to the moment, or merely to relax.
It is highly recommended for anyone experiencing stress or a clouded mind. Here will be detailed the basic steps for practicing meditation.
First, find a quiet, comfortable place. Someplace that you feel safe in, and where you will not be interrupted by outside influences.
If you are first beginning, set an hourglass or a clock alarm for a short time. Ten or fifteen minutes will do. Even short sessions can help.
Next, sit down. The traditional position is to sit cross-legged with hands in the lap, but so long as you are comfortable, any position works.
Once you have found a comfortable spot, close your eyes and breathe deeply. Breathe in deeply, hold for a few seconds, breathe out, and hold for the same amount.
Focus on the sensation of your breathing, and on only the sensation of your breathing. If your mind wanders, do not fret- simply return your attention to your breath.
When you feel ready to rise, or when your time ends, slowly open your eyes and notice your environment- the sights and sounds, and the feeling of your body.
Although there are more complex and involved methods of meditation, they are not necessary- Now that you have read this, try it yourself when you have a spare moment.
...this seems promising. Carefully, you settle down, and close your eyes.
...breathe in...
...breathe out...
...breathe in...
...you can't focus. Your mind is wandering too many directions at once. Unfortunate, but it's worth remembering anyways.
Scroll of Martial Stances (-16053, 20769):
When fighting unarmed or with weapons such as knuckles, katars, or gauntlets, one's stance is paramount in fighting an opponent.
The way one is positioned can ground the body, allowing for blows to be taken with less consequence, or allow one to be light enough to evade attack.
All combat of course must be learned through rigorous training- One cannot expect to become an expert simply by reading. Here are a handful of basic stances to practice.
The Forward Stance has legs placed broadly apart, the back leg outstretched fully and body upright. This is a firm stance to steady oneself.
The Back Stance has one foot in front of the other, with the back foot facing to the side and one's weight on the back leg. For evading attacks to the top of the body.
The Cat Stance has weight on the back foot, with legs bent and held close together and front foot resting on the heel. This allows easy preparation for strong front kicks.
The Crane Stance has one leg raised, the foot level with the other knee. Also used in preparation for kicking, as well as dodging a sweeping attack by the enemy.
...while this is fascinating to read about, learning about combat stances seems too active to bring you tranquility.
Ancestry of Magical Arts (-16053, 20764):
Many a venerable mage has made their mark on history. There is a reason their names are repeated- we can learn much from what they have demonstrated.
This, unfortunately, applies for both positive and negative reasons. For instance, a lesson that has become law involves the use of soul-binding magic.
The upturn of necromantic practices ended in 294 AP, with the outlawing of the technique. Defiling the dead and preventing their spirits from moving on...
...was considered a monstrous and unmoral practice. Keeping the spirit trapped, forced to obey orders, in a decaying body wracked with pain, is something that could not be abided by.
Since then, soul-binding is the most strictly punished brand of magic on all of Gavel, above demonic rites and even the necromancy that soul-binding was endemic within.
...this is a very heavy read. Certainly not suitable for finding tranquility.
The Art of Brewing Tea (-16051, 20761):
To brew tea is a simple, meditative process that in itself has deep intricacies. We shall draw upon its heritage now.
Fresh, clean water is required. Bring it to a soft boil in a pot or cauldron, and then mix in herbs and ingredients to taste.
Harvesting ingredients freshly can add extra depth to the tea, although you can make fine tea from any ingredients, so long as they are not rotten.
It is best not to add too much to the tea, for too many conflicting tastes will leave it muddled and foul-tasting. Three ingredients is a fine benchmark.
Common ingredients include sugar, lemongrass, ginger root, chamomile, and lavender. Each has their own purpose for tea.
Sugar helps sweeten the bitterness of some brews, and balances the flavors to be mild. However, too much will leave the brew sickly and tacky.
The unique tang of lemongrass is lauded as a signature for green tea. The mild, lightly minty flavor is a perfect base for which to create a relaxing brew.
Although Ginger Root is bitingly bitter and inevitably overpowers other ingredients, it has potent medical effects which may help invigorate the sick.
Chamomile adds a pleasantly sweet, floral taste to a brew. The delicate flavor helps the body and mind relax- it is oft used as a sleep aid.
Lavender is similarly relaxing, but must be the focus of the brew. It must be steeped for a long while and is severely bitter, which causes it to drown out the other ingredients.
...come to think of it, a cup of tea sounds like it would be quite nice, after all the hard training. Perhaps you should make a cup.
Home Relaxation Ideas (-16043, 20761):
While many people think that relaxation is out of reach with their busy schedules, the truth is there are many things you can do daily to wind down and take that little time.
For instance, caring for houseplants is a simple task. You can grow them from seeds or get them pre-bought, and caring for gardens is an easy way to relax, while also giving you a place to relax.
You can turn any room into a garden simply by getting planter pots, but for those who can't devote enough time to that, you could try caring for a bonsai tree instead.
They just need water, sunlight, and care by using garden shears to carefully cut the limbs of the tree. Shaping it like this is artful in itself, and has spiritual significance as well.
It requires focus in the moment, but not much time at all, meaning you can still simply set aside short time and be done. It also helps clean the air in the house as well!
Another easy way to relax is to set up a stone garden. You don't need a large amount of space to have one- even a small box will do. Fill it with gravel and smooth stones.
Use a small handheld rake to draw lines in the gravel in different patterns, each day. It's as simple as that- don't focus on making specific ones though, just draw whatever your hand draws.
Doing this can help draw focus away from stressful thoughts, and bring you back to the moment, while also being a fun conversation piece that's easy and cheap to set up.
...those are nice thoughts, but unfortunately, there isn't a zen garden set up here, and you don't have a bonsai tree or garden shears handy.
Unlabeled Book (-16035, 20760):
...hm? This isn't actually a book, it's a dossier. Did Miyagi leave this out by accident?
Seems to contain a number of trade agreements, between the Sakura Dojo and the Qira Hive.
It appears that recently, a large shipment of Hive silk has been received. There's no record of emerald payment.
A shipment of cherries and rice has been sent out at the same time- they must trade products directly.
Previous records show trades of metal salvage for cherry wood, and gifted shipments of tea leaves and ingredients.
...there's a letter here, too. The script is very ornate...this is addressed from the Mistress of the Hive herself, only a few months ago.
"I hope this letter finds you well. I once again thank you for the trade. The caravans from Lake Gylia have been scarce recently, and your donations have kept the servants from going hungry."
"Although I would under most circumstances send a small party of my creations to run for supplies, it is a logistical and political nightmare I would just as soon avoid."
"I will provide remuneration for this in due time- certainly, I may spare a sum of emeralds if you wish it. You are trusted enough to write a blank check on this for, so you may name your price."
"Equally I am willing to offer extra salvage metal of top quality, or perhaps further silk or animant stones for your training dummies. Please write back quickly with your request."
"I plan to accompany the next caravan which will bring our recompensation, and I look forward to the visit. We may finally finish our set of Go yet."
"Regards, Mistress Qira"

In the cavern, there will be five different nodes where you can harvest resources. Just outside the room to the right is a well where you can harvest water, in the flower beds by the Wild Cow will be some Lavender, the dead bushes will allow you to harvest Ginger Roots, the field of white flowers lets you get Chamomile, the field of grass by the Wild Sheep lets you get some Lemongrass, and the sugarcanes by the pond will let you harvest Sugar.
Once you have the ingredients necessary to brew tea, go to the cauldron to get the Cup of Tea of Tranquility.

NOTE: Tea that was brewed with all 5 ingredients won't trigger animal's dialogue. In order to progress you have to read the book about teamaking in the library then go to cauldron and start brewing. It will tell you that Lavender and Ginger shouldn't be used, so you will have to drop them before continuing.
With the tea brewed and the scent filling the room, you gently take a few sips.
The heat of the tea and the gently sweet, floral taste warms your throat and body. You feel more relaxed, but...not at peace with nature yet.
...there were some animals wandering the cave. Making a small offering seems like the right way to go, and there's plenty of tea left...
After you have received the tea, give it to the Wild Cow, Sheep, or Pig in the cave.
The cow/sheep/pig raises its head to look at you. Its eyes flare at the sight of the green tea.
You gesture the tea generously towards the cow/sheep/pig, and place it on the ground for it to drink. The cow/sheep/pig nods respectfully towards you.
...watching it drink from the cup as you did, there's a certain kinship you feel, and with that realization comes a feeling of peace.
You can't recall the last time you've felt this relaxed. You know for certain that you have mastered the challenge of tranquility. Time to leave.|finding tranquility}}

stages.title: Stage 1
stages.task: Talk to Arwes in the ruined cathedral.
hints: Arwes: Welcome, weary traveller. To the house of Talor... Or what remains of it.
Arwes: As you can see, times are hard in the forest, especially here in the west.
Arwes: Very few are left in this church. Myself, the good Pastor Nitram, and of course old Golie here.
Arwes: This used to be a thriving religious sanctuary, but all my brothers have turned to darkness.
Arwes: They think that our gods have abandoned us and the decay is our punishment. They now worship demons, of all things.
Arwes: It is heartbreaking to see such good people turned to this sort of depravity. Murder, sacrifice, oppression of the downtrodden...
???: Let me go! I'm so young, you can't throw away my life like this. p-please! SOMEONE HELP ME!
Arwes: Wha?! That sounded like... oh gods no, another sacrifice? Even strong Talos...
Arwes: Please, human. I have heard of many kind acts by you folk, please help save Talos! It sounded like they were dragging him to the north-west crypt...

stages.title: Stage 2
stages.task: Search the ruins to find the cultists.
hints: ???: Please, NO! Don't do this!
???: A Human! Oh, please help! They're going to try to feed me to a hellhound!
» Find Talos in the crypt.
» Kill the hellhound and free Talos.
Talos: That's the kind of strength I would expect from you humans! Thank you so very much! If you could cut me loose here...
Talos: Ah, there we go! These three madmen attacked me while I was sleeping, so I couldn't defend myself. They stole everything I had!
Talos: Hah, now that your little hellhound won't be eating me, you give me back my-
Talos: Wait, there...there's only two others... I'm sure there were three of them here just earlier. Has the third ran off with my things?! Tell me! Now!
???: Yes indeed, foolish treasure hunter. Only one thing... but that is all we will need. It is more than enough. The rest will make but a fine offering to our lord...
Talos: Ugh, they ought to lock you nutters up in that dreadful prison. Well, whatever the case, was Arwes in the church?
Talos: He's probably rather worried about the both of us. You ought to go tell him we're alright. Even barehanded I can fend these loonies off.

stages.title: Stage 3
stages.task: Return to Arwes in the cathedral.
hints: Arwes: Oh, thank goodness you are safe. I never knew my old brothers were so strong to have taken a hardened adventurer like Talos.
Arwes: Now, I wouldn't normally ask someone for this kind of request, but since you have already proven yourself...
Arwes: And I truly have no where else to turn. I must ask you once more for help.
Arwes: A robed figure... I did not see their face, but they brandished a dark artifact. Apparently, stolen from Talos' treasures...
Arwes: They called it the [Eye of Blood]. Such a perverse, twisted aura... I nearly passed out on the spot. Who knows what they could do with it...
Arwes: They probably took it to the town they currently occupy, Lexdale. They have turned it into their own personal playground, with no regard for the people within.
Arwes: I cannot even so much as help them. The dark cult has completely blocked the town off from outsiders... And yet, the people of Cinfras don't even as much as bat an eye...
Arwes: But this is no time for grievances. You must retrieve the [Eye of Blood]. An old friend of mine, Ceyquin, might help you. You will have to sneak into Lexdale, though...

stages.title: Stage 4
stages.task: Talk to Ceyquin in Lexdale.
hints: Ceyquin: What- A...A human? In Lexdale?! How did you get in, do you have a death wish?!
Ceyquin: Uh! I mean... P-praise our new lord, th-the great and terrible Naragath!
Ceyquin: Ugh...you're welcome, I brought us a few more minutes. those cultists have eyes and ears everywhere in my town anymore...
Ceyquin: Ther're trying to summon that Naragath character, whatever it is...some kind of demon, I suppose. They say if we obey them, he'll spare us.
Ceyquin: I want to stop them, but it's hopeless. They've already killed many dissenters just on their own, but I think they really can summon this demon.
Ceyquin: Just look to the north, you see that giant hand? They summoned it. As if the decay wasn't bad enough already, that looks completely different, and even worse!
Ceyquin: You don't believe me? Go inside my house and up to the highest balcony. You'll have a clear view of the pit from up there. Take a good long look at what you're up against!

stages.title: Stage 5
stages.task: Climb to the balcony in Ceyquin's house.
hints: A massive corrupted pit is visible in the distance, to the north-east. A similarly huge dark hand seems to be sprounting from within it. It strains your mind to view...

stages.title: Stage 6
stages.task: Return to Ceyquin.
hints: Ceyquin: N-no, nothing to hide! I wouldn't dream of barboring a dissident in my humble home!
Ceyquin: Phew...if you came out even a second earlier we'd both be dead on the spot! Anyway, do you see what you're up against now?
Ceyquin: I'd quicker try and kill Ozoth barehanded and bloody-knuckled than see the body attached to Naragath's hand there.
Ceyquin: If you really think can you help, you certainly won't be able to from here. The cultists have this town in a stranglehold.
Ceyquin: There is a wizard who sometimes sneaks in food for us...though, if he can't defeat them on his own, I don't know how much he could help you.
Ceyquin: Well...whatever the case, you'll want to go to the hill next to the hand. I think the house near to it is Rismor's.
Ceyquin: You can use the secret exit I've got in my basement to leave. Be quiet when you sneak in there. I'll make sure no one sees you.

stages.title: Stage 7
stages.task: Enter the tunnel under Ceyquin's house.
hints: Ceyquin: W-what? They...they knew about the tunnel?! I have to warn the human- N-no! They already jumped down! Oh no...

stages.title: Stage 8
stages.task: Escape through the cavern and find Rismor in his house.
hints: Stage 1: Left, Up, Right, Down, Left, Up
Stage 2: Up, Left, Up, Left, Down, Left, Down, Left, Down, Right, Up, Right, Up
Stage 3: Left, Up, Right, Up, Right, Down, Left, Down, Right, Up, Right, Down, Left, Up

Rismor: And STAY out of my home, you damn fool cultists! Can't you see that thing will just burn our world if you manage to summon it?!
Rismor: Oh, I wasn't talking to you, human. Those foolhardy cultists just broke into my house. I repelled them, though. So, what brings-
A massive tremor suddenly rocks the hill, and a wave of despair washes over you. This feels somehow familiar...
Rismor: Ugh, no, no, no! They're advancing further with the summoning! This can't have been my scroll, they only just left! How did they get this far so quickly?
Rismor: The...what now? The eye...the [Eye of Blood]?! A corrupted summoning item...this gives us no time at all! I need to figure something out now!
Rismor: Wait...what am I saying, there's a human in my house! You're known for helping those in need, right? Well, there's a lot on your shoulders today.
Rismor: Your heard me shout it earlier, it those idiots summon Naragath he could ravage the entire province! You see the giant hand, we'd be powerless to stop him!
Rismor: I'd send you straight in, but the Pit of Despair here...not only does it emanate hopelessness just of its own accord, but the newfound corruptive energies of the eye will overwhelm your mind.
Rismor: I'd cast a spell of protection on you, but those cultists are smart. They stole my wands and all my spell scrolls too. You'll have to get it back for me.
Rismor: They ran off towards their "Blood Oak", a tree they once used for sacrifices before they took the church crypts. It's just south of here. Pursue them!

stages.title: Stage 9
stages.task: Find the Guardian and the ancient blood oak, south of Rismor's house.

stages.title: Stage 10
stages.task: Kill the Guardian and bring back the Lost Spell Scroll to Rismor.
hints: Rismor: I saw your fight. Did the accolyte there have the scroll?
Rismor: Thank goodness. If they'd run farther we would have certainly run out of time. We should consider ourselves lucky they decided to hold their ground.
Rismor: Not a second to waste, hand the scroll here and I'll read the incantation.
Rismor: Ballreth Illi’dan Coropleth!
A warming comfort suddenly washes over your body. The despair filing the air before seems distant now.
Rismor: Alright, you should be able to enter the pit safely now. Expect to be attacked. Hopefully my agent is still doing fine...
Rismor: His name is Harker. I sent him in a while ago to spy on the Order and sabotage their rituals. He's a fairly powerful magic user in of himself.
Rismor: I'll attempt to contact him via magic to tell him to expect you. I can't guarantee anything, but even if i can't contact him, he should know a human wouldn't be helping the Order.

Harker: I can still use the magic Rismor taught me, so I can help you stop the ritual. The cultists have already begun.

Harker: I am still weak, so you will need to fight the demon on your own. Defeat him and bring me the Eye of Blood. We've made it this far, now let's end this!

Rismor: But, just a few minutes before you came back, it suddenly stopped. It seems to be frozen like that now. It'd be better if it had disappeared, but this is preferable to an apocalypse.
Rismor: The cultists suddenly panicked when the hand petreated of its own accord as it did. Most of them seem to have left Lexdale.

Rismor: For now, I will hide the Eye of Blood and make sure no one touches it ever again. And I will be sure to keep an eye on the remaining cultists.

Rismor: Farewell, adventurer. I do hope we may meet again, under better circumstances.I can only pray that this is the last we will clash with those from the realm of darkness.
