stages.title: Stage 17
stages.task: Talk to Sovereign Majin and the Spymaster at [-956, 159, -1125].
hints: ???: It's been a while since we've met face to face, hasn't it? And you've been busy.
???: So in the end you made the choice to search for your answers... bold, I'll admit. You've caused quite the disruption thus far.
Who are you, really?
???: I am the Second, the Spymaster. You may call me Two.
Sovereign Two: You've quite the set of accomplishments, it turns out. Careless work by our inquisitors, perhaps, that we did not know beforehand... with some exceptions, granted.
Sovereign Two: To think, the Shade was struck blind by your hand! At no small cost, of course... but a shattered soul means little in the wider stage.
Sovereign Two: Had we known, would you have been given greater consideration? Perhaps. Or perhaps not. Each flaw remains as damning as before.
Sovereign Majin: Oh, get to the point, would you? I have more important things to attend to then this frivolous attempt at information gathering.
Sovereign Two: Very well. I shall digress.
Sovereign Two: Of all your accomplishments, of all your history, of each point along your storied trail, there is but one we cannot see. A place we cannot go.
Sovereign Two: You and the Light's Scion entered the Realm of Light. At a time pinpointed to have transpired during your stay within, the spread of Gavel's Decay abruptly ceased.
Sovereign Two: You would later return to your numerous adventures, not a sign of ever having traversed the realms at all. She has not been seen since.
Sovereign Two: I do not expect you to share this information freely. That is why we are here. To make an... exchange, of sorts.
Why do you care?
Sovereign Majin: I should rather like to know the same thing myself! The way I see it, it hardly impacts the wider scope of your schemes.
Sovereign Two: I do like to be meticulous. Each additional defined variable helps with the accuracy of my predictions.
Sovereign Two: Regardless - the request comes directly from Her Majesty. It appears she is just as interested in the answer as I am.
The dialogue branches combine here.
How do you know all this?
Sovereign Majin: My goodness, what a question! How does the Spymaster know these things? What a conundrum - perhaps the title should clue you in?
Sovereign Two: There is little I do not keep track of in this world. Mostly, my inquisitors work to collect information beyond our gates...
Sovereign Two: Though, in special circumstances, I have been known to do so myself. Such as the one we find ourselves in now.
The dialogue branches combine here.
Why is this a blind spot?
Sovereign Two: Entry to their Claims is not such an easy task if uninvited. You've seen the portal that lies at the end of the Expanse, haven't you? Still active, yet... sealed shut.
Sovereign Two: It seems the Shade did not take well to losing its Sight. An act of caution, blocking your access to its domain. The Light is much the same.
The dialogue branches combine here.
Sovereign Majin: Awestruck, are we? I do suppose such is the natural consequence of being in the vicinity of the crown's two strongest Sovereigns!
Sovereign Majin: But I'm afraid we do need you to speak up, so do get over yourself, would you?
The dialogue branches combine here.
Sovereign Two: And so, we return to the exchange. If you tell us what we wish to know, I will offer some valuable information in return. I trust it will be of interest to you.
Sovereign Two: Well, do we have a deal?
We do.
The dialogue branches combine here.
Do I have a choice?
Sovereign Two: You always have a choice. But sometimes, there is a right and a wrong choice to make. The decision is yours.
The dialogue branches combine here.
Sovereign Two: So tell me. What happened in the Realm of Light? What could we not see?
Tell her.
You tell her about entering the portal with Lari. About seeing the realm's connections severed, made smaller.
You tell her about remaking the connections, About the monoliths, deactivated with intent, their light fading.
You tell her about crossing the bridge. About your encounter with the Scourge of Wynn. About his battle with Lari, from start to end.
You tell her about fighting through the nexus. About the battle between Light and Dark ongoing within.
You tell her about Orphion. About the Parasite latched on, eating through his radiance. About the struggle to remove it.
You tell her how you finally killed it. How it fought, and fought, and fought, but could not take you down. How the Light was freed from the Shadows.
Sovereign Two: ...
Sovereign Two: How very interesting. To think, the Shade has enough trust in War's lost Scion to send him to defend its trump card...
Sovereign Majin: I had wondered when he might finally show his ugly face again. Heavens know we'd had enough of him already.
Sovereign Two: And the Dawn is freed from the Dusk's assault... but its Scion is lost to the Dark's Claim... a step forward, and a step back alike.
Sovereign Majin: A step back, perhaps, but it could also be a boon in disguise. She could serve as a potential ally for your... whatever, if you could only locate her.
Sovereign Two: Certainly, she could. This will shift the trajectory of certain shards of possibility... I'll have to dive deeper into the consequences.
Sovereign Two: Regardless, this has been enlightening. Her Majesty will certainly be interested in these developments.
Why does she care about all this?
Sovereign Two: You refer to the War of the Realms, I presume?
Fruma seems so... detached from it.
Sovereign Two: I suppose it must. Beyond the wider scope, why do we care? Wynn's corruption is at a safe distance, and both Light and Dark are far, far away.
Sovereign Two: I can answer your question. But first, a tale.
Sovereign Two creates a cube of light and a cube of dark.
Sovereign Two: Once, there were two twins orbiting one another, each laying claim to their own piece of the void they were given.
A red mirror appears between the cubes.
Sovereign Two: The first was bright, radiant, overwhelming. The other was dark, shadowed, suffocating. Gazing through the abyss, they saw one another - each a mirror image of the other.
Sovereign Two: The twins grew to hate each other. They built forms all their own, denying the truth of their reflections. They tried, and tried, and tried to break their bonds...
Sovereign Two: ...but in the end, they could do naught but orbit - holding influence in their own right, but possessing nothing to exert it on.
A third green cube appears above the other two cubes.
Sovereign Two: Until... they found it. A miraculous world, of magic and life, and all of a sudden, nothing became something.
Beams extend from the light and dark cubes into the green cube.
Sovereign Two: They took. They battled.
The mirror in the middle shatters.
Sovereign Two: And in so doing, they came to shatter the mirror which once held their reflections. A building pressure of light and dark and hate, until finally enough was enough...
A circle of shards start pinning around the mirror.
Sovereign Two: And from those uncountable shattered pieces of their battleground, War came to be.
Sovereign Two: War, Chaos, Hate... call it what you will. It was lesser, holding less control over itself than the twins from which it was birthed.
Sovereign Two: All it knew was the hatred of the twins, directed towards one another, never acknowledging the battlefield they had made. All it knew was the pain of being.
The beams from the light and dark cubes disappear.
Sovereign Two: Until, one day... it all stopped. The twins had lost their connection to their world of influence, and could no longer sustain their endless War.
Sovereign Two: It was in that silence that War could finally sense beyond itself, could feel the world the twins had taken for granted, the beauty they had discarded in their race for victory.
The beams reextend.
Sovereign Two: And so, when the connections emerged once more, it took its chance.
A grotesque hand extends from the broken mirror towards the green cube.
Sovereign Two: It broke through the endless void, forcing its own connection unto the world, following in the twins' example.
Sovereign Two: Finally, it saw the world beyond... sprawling plains, forests, seas. Saw towns, cities, farmlands- war, destruction, tainted by the human desperation to live.
Sovereign Two: And it began to dream of that desperation itself.
The entire diorama disappears.
Sovereign Two: ...are you beginning to understand?
Sovereign Two: Her Majesty is War - was War. But it is no longer hers - instead, she has chosen to lay claim to this world's protection.
Sovereign Two: And in the meanwhile, the twins continue to take and take and take. If left unchecked, they will take until there is nothing left to fight over.
Sovereign Two: ... Will that do for your answer?
Sovereign Majin: You've a streak for the dramatic, don't you... Was that truly all necessary? We could have always laid it out simply- on that note, why even answer at all?
Sovereign Two: I believe the context to be important.
Sovereign Majin: Of course you would... well then, are we finished here?
Might we finally dismiss our little guest and return to important matters.
Sovereign Two: I suppose we are. We may consider this interrogation adjourned.
So I'm free to leave?
Sovereign Majin: Ah ah ah! Not so fast. Certainly, neither of us will deign to stop your escape... but the troops lying in wait will have no such reservations.
Sovereign Majin: Now, see yourself out, would you? You are dismissed.

hints: Follow the blood trail to the next room. The next room has three stone pillars with a mirror copy.

Using the Soul Retainer once again, the Player must switch places with their soul repeatedly to navigate up the parkour. Every time they switch with their soul on the last platform, a new platform will be added. This should be repeated until the first column is reached, then ride a block trail that will make its way to the other column in the room. Standing on the pressure plate launches the Player upwards to the next room.

WARNING: It is highly recommended that you have a low ping when completing this and the next stage. This is because servers with high amounts of lag will cause you to fall through the platforms when switching. If you're doing this part and experience these glitches, then join a different server with less lag or switch hubs depending on your location for lower latency.
Where does all of this lead?

stages.title: Stage 6
hints: In the next room, there are four pressure plates identified with textures: Cobblestone, Sandstone, Wood, and Stone.

In this room, you must stand on one of the four pressure plates at a time to spawn platforms for your soul to jump onto using the Soul Retainer. If you swap and your soul is suspended midair, a platform will appear directly under it regardless of whichever material is picked. The goal is to reach either gateway with your soul.
First, stand on the Sandstone pressure plate.
Then, have your soul stand on the platform 1 block off the ground near the front center of the room.
Switch back and stand on the Wood pressure plate. Jump to the platform 1 block up and away from where you are standing.
Once you reach the platform, switch to the Stone pressure plate and jump to the platform 2 blocks away from yours.
Move back to Wood and jump to the platform that is at the same height as the platform you're standing under.
Finally, move over to Cobblestone and perform a 3 block 1 jump to the next platform. Jump from this platform to the gateway.

▸ Post-Quest
Upon returning to Lutho, the citizen is revealed to have become eyeless.
Lutho Citizen: ...
▸ Tips
This quest has a few 3+1 blocks jumps, so walk speed buffers such as a potion of agility, a weapon/armor piece with walk speed bonus, or archer's escape spell speed boost is highly recommended.

On Stage 6, you are highly susceptible to falling through the platform your soul is standing on when you switch. This is because your soul NPC lingers for a short moment when you switch with it, and it tends to push you down as you're spawning inside of it. To prevent this from happening, hold space right before you switch with your soul while standing on the pressure plate. This will still make the platforms activate, but it will also make you jump when you switch, preventing you from falling through the platform.
On Stage 8, make sure you are not wearing any piece of equipment that provides jump boost, as it prevents you from getting the actual jump boost effect that prevents you from falling to your death.

On Stage 9, part two (with the flame pillars), you can avoid harm by either using movement spells or by simply hiding under the doorway to the next part, where the flames will not be able to reach you.

Tasim: It's been a while, hasn't it? We should catch up! You've probably had lots of adventures, right?
Tasim: But before that... I've just got to find...
What're you looking for?
Tasim: Huh? What am I oh, yeah. I'm trying to find Aledar.
Tasim: He sent me a letter asking me to join him on some... scouting mission. But I haven't been able to find him.
Tasim: It did take me a while to get here... so maybe he's gone somewhere else by now. Aegis did tell me the mission ended up being called off, so...
Tasim: But if he's not here, then I should probably stop trying to catch him on the streets, huh? I'll just leave a message for him at the barracks.

Tasim: We can head to the tavern and catch up! Gods, I've missed the Rusty Recruit's drinks... that barkeeper, he says it's the same as anywhere else, but it really isn't! Nowhere else pours it like he does.
He... doesn't know about Aledar, does he?
Don't.
He just got back. You can't... tell him now. You'll do it later, once he's settled in.
Yeah... Let's catch up.
Tell him.
...he doesn't know. You have to break the news to him.
I need to tell you s
A Ragni Courier will come frantically running through Detlas's western entrance.
Tasim: ???
Ragni Courier: Pardon me, excuse me coming through! Coming through! Ah, you two! Just the folks I was looking for.
Tasim: Huh? Us two specifically?
Ragni Courier: Well, perhaps not specifically. I've got a list of folks to try and track down, and the two of you are on it! Tasim and Player, right?
Ragni Courier: I've got an important missive from Ragni. Direct from the King himself, yep yep!
Tasim: Really? I don't think I've seen him since... what could he possibly want us for?
Ragni Courier: I'm not privy to the details I'm afraid! He's summoning a number of you seasoned visitors to the castle, for some sort of meeting.
Ragni Courier: Anyway, I've got more to try and track down, so I'll give you the written letters and be on my way! Best of luck with whatever it is!
Tasim: Thanks...
The Ragni Courier will then run back the way he came.
Tasim: Hm. That is strange, isn't it? I guess we'll have to call off drinks for later... probably for the best. Maybe I'll be able to catch him before...
Tasim: Oh, uh you go on ahead. I have to stop by the barracks first. I'll meet you in Ragni, then?
Talking to Tasim after this stage:
Tasim: I'll meet you in Ragni. I have to deal with some things at the barracks first.
names: » Tasim is looking to catch up in Detlas

stages.title: Stage 2
stages.task: Attend the meeting with the King in Ragni at [-928, 67, -1630].
hints: Tasim: ...oh, there you are. Didn't you head out before me?
Tasim: I don't know most of the people here, so I'll stick with you for now.
Ragni's King: Ah. Please head to the meeting room. I will join shortly.
Linton: ...and it's all crashing down, right? So I knock the zombie back, grab the kid, and jump for
Mel: Wait, wait wait wait you're tellin' me there was a kid involved? And you still set off the bombs?!
Linton: Yeah! I said that already, right? That was the whole reason I

Mel: I do try to keep my distance.
Lanu: So, you received the summons too? The King has a lot of people here. It's interesting.
Tasim: We did, yes. And it sounded like they had even more people on that list that they were searching for.
Lanu: Oh, apologies, I hadn't noticed you there. You're a friend of Player's, I take it?
Tasim: I am! We arrived in Wynn on the same caravan. I'm Tasim.
Mel: Tasim?! You're Tasim?
Linton: So you're the one Aledar was always talking about! I thought you were off in Gavel?
Tasim: I... was. How do you all know him?
Lanu: I believe we first met on a mission to reclaim Almuj's barracks from a treasonous commander. We've run into each other a few times since.
Mel: Still, it's good to finally get t' meet you! We've heard lots of stories! Including somethin' about not respondin' to letters...?
Tasim: Oh... right. We, uh... sorted that out.
Tasim: But speaking of have any of you seen him recently?
Mel: 'fraid not. I don't think our paths've crossed since... was it the siege at Troms? Must've been.
Linton: I saw him a month ago in Detlas! I asked him what he was working on and if I could help and he just brushed me off. Weird, right?
Lanu: Mmn. No, that sounds like him. I think he had enough of your antics last time.
Linton: What?! I'm capable. C'mon, Mel, tell her I'm capable.
Mel: Linton, y'were just tellin' us about how you caved in a whole temple by
Linton: Okay! Okay, okay okay, let's talk about literally anything else! Tasim, right? What's... uh...
Linton: ...so, your... no, no, give me a moment you were... and... um... oh, right...
Linton: ...d'you like guys?
Tasim: ...
Mel: Linton!! Y'can't just ask someone that!!
Linton: ...uh
Lanu: It was nice meeting you, Tasim. I look forward to working with you during this mission.
Tasim: ...likewise. It's always nice meeting friends of Aledar.
Following interactions:
You don't think you could handle the awkward conversation that would follow that interaction.
Jenprest: Well, look at you! It's been quite a time since we last spoke. Far above the task of cleaning out sewers now, eh?
Jenprest: I've heard some tell of your accomplishments. Fine work, fine work.
Jenprest: And... hm. Aren't you the one who ran off to Gavel without sayin' a word? Didn't expect you to be one o' the ones picked out for this.
Tasim: I... didn't expect it either. I didn't even realize the King still remembered me, truth be told.
Jenprest: Mmn. Well, whatever the reason, you're here now. Don't suppose it matters much the path you took to get here. We need all the folks we can get or so Kymer's been sayin'.
Captain Kymer: Well well! If my eyes don't deceive me! Player and Tasim!
Captain Kymer: I'll say, I didn't quite expect them to track you down! What with your... extended stint off in Gavel.
Tasim: I should say the same about you, captain. Did Llevigar no longer have a use for you once the war ended?

Captain Kymer: Ah... nothing of the sort. You know, I was sent out there initially to serve as more of an envoy from Ragni! If the King needs a diplomatic situation sorted, I'm the one he turns to first.
Captain Kymer: Which... is indeed why I am here now. I was recalled rather abruptly several weeks ago. It seems we've entered a tricky situation with our... neighboring province.
Captain Kymer: But! I shan't say more before the King arrives. He'll tell you all of the problem that hopefully we will be able to resolve.
Tasim: ...I see. We'll leave you to it, then.
Dr. Picard:
Dr. Picard: If we align the manaflow with Water, then nudge it to the side, maybe... ah Reynauld, pass me my notes on... damn, what was it oh, yes, the recovery period! Pass me those ones.
Reynauld: ...You already have them on your left, doctor.
Dr. Picard: Do I now! It seems I do... oh, but this is only the first half where did I leave the rest...
Reynauld: Sigh... If you'd just allow me to organize for you, maybe you wouldn't
Dr. Picard: And ruin my predefined sorting system?! No, Reynauld, I do think it works perfectly well as it is, thank you very much! Now, where could it have
Dr. Picard and Reynauld notice the Player and Tasim.
Dr. Picard: Ah! You two! Good, good, you're here I was worried Reynauld would be the only other one with recovered memories around here!
Tasim: What, you didn't test it on anyone else after we left?
Dr. Picard: Test it on no, of course not! After what I saw? No, no, that would certainly not have been worth the risk. No new test subjects until I am certain it's flawless!
Dr. Picard: I've been using it on myself instead! And, let me tell you the breakthroughs I have made... there is much to be learned.
Tasim: And is that... safe?
Dr. Picard: Pah! "Safety" a meaningless term made only to stifle progress. Have there been side effects certainly! But it has all been worth it.
Dr. Picard: Now, I must return to the pages... I've some equations I need to perfect before the King arrives...
Reynauld:
Reynauld: Hm. I can't say I would have expected you to be here, Tasim.
Tasim: Well... fate has other plans, I guess. How about you? Did you stay in Elkurn?
Reynauld: Mostly. Moved around for a few assignments here and there, but I kept coming back.
Reynauld: ...we haven't spoken in a while. Are you... doing well? How have you been managing the memories?
Tasim: ...
Tasim: As well as I could be expected to, I guess. It was rough for the first few months. Eventually, I got used to it.
Tasim: How about you? I also wouldn't have expected you to show for a mission like this.
Reynauld: Same as you. Helped that Caid and I managed to talk it through. We meet every so often, talk about it. He talks about his sister, how he wants to find her one day.
Tasim: That's... good. Happy for you.
Reynauld: Hm. Nothing stopping you from stopping by, yourself. It might even help you.
Tasim: I'll... consider it. Good to see you again, Reynauld.
Ragni Guard: Another soldier? Allow me to see your summons.
Ragni Guard: ...good. Come on in, Player. The King will be arriving shortly.
Go inside
Ragni Guard: Right this way.
Give me a moment.
Ragni Guard: If you insist. Don't take too long.
The Player is brought to a room with Dr. Picard, Reynauld, Jenprest, Captain Kymer, Tasim, Lanu, Mel, Linton, and the King of Ragni. All of them are gathered at a table.
King of Ragni: Ah... here we are. I thank you all for coming on such short notice. It has been some time since I have seen many of you.
King of Ragni: ...I'll get right to the point. We find ourselves in a very delicate position when it comes to relations with our neighboring province, Fruma.
King of Ragni: We rely heavily on the flow of new recruits sent to us, but we have no means of contacting their province. Only they may reach out to us, and only once they have chosen to do so.
King of Ragni: ...several weeks ago, we received a cloaked visitor through the outskirts. She claimed to be of Fruma, one of their Sovereigns.
King of Ragni: We were extended an invitation, of sorts. Of all the recruits we have ever received, we were to select the greatest, and send them into Fruma for some sort of celebration.
Tasim: Is that who we are? The greatest?
Captain Kymer: The ones that could be reached, at the very least! Perhaps some were greater yet, but we all know the roaming habits of your sort, and tracking them down really can prove
Linton: Ugh, we're not going along with this, are we?
Mel: Linton! You can't just
Linton: What? They're demanding something weird and obviously suspicious, so why should we just accept it?

King of Ragni: I'm afraid we don't have a choice in the matter. As I mentioned, the recruits we receive make all the difference in our province's continued survival. If we were to reject this invitation...
Jenprest: ...who's to say they wouldn't just stop sendin' 'em, eh? Tough.
Dr. Picard: Besides all that, think of the opportunity this presents! A true, freely-given view of what lies beyond those walls! We'd be fools not to accept it, no matter the implied threat!
King of Ragni: Indeed. I regret that I must request this of you... but there is no other choice. You must accept this invitation.
Reynauld: ...even those of us with bad experiences of the province?
King of Ragni: I apologize... but you must. My hands are tied.
Lanu: I take it we are expected to gather as much intelligence on Fruma as we can while we're in there?
Dr. Picard: That's the plan, indeed! I'll explain more once we're there, but I believe we're on a time limit, correct?
King of Ragni: You are correct, doctor. I have been told that a representative will greet you all at the royal gates of Fruma, situated on the western coast.
King of Ragni: I've sent a courier ahead to Nemract to inform the local captains of the destination they are to take you to.
Tasim: Nemract... I know a captain there. Player, want to join me?
Dialogue after the meeting:
Dr. Picard: Finally... a glimpse at the province's inner workings... how long have I been seeking these answers?
Dr. Picard: So many theories... how many will be proven right? How many will be wrong? I cannot wait to find out!
Reynauld: Sigh... I did know this was coming. Why else would the doctor have been summoned? But I hoped I was wrong.
Jenprest: Tough situation, isn't it? Lots o' secrecy on part of the Frumans...
Jenprest: But we'll handle it. Everyone here's plenty capable, after all.
Captain Kymer: Hm... what a situation it is we find ourselves in! Diplomacy is my specialty, of course, but my expertise has not prepared me for... this.
Captain Kymer: Fruma knows what they want, and know they are strong enough that they can afford to let up their position.
Linton: Another top secret mission already? And I'm not even allowed to bring my explosives?
Linton: It's interesting, at least! Way better than that last assignment...
Mel: This mission's a big deal, huh? Lot's o' strong folks recalled for it, at least.
Mel: Makes me a bit nervous, honestly!
Lanu: Fruma... I can't say it's been on my mind much. It's a mystery, yes, but not one with any available answers.
Lanu: Well, until now, I suppose. I'll have to prepare a list of details to look out for...
King of Ragni: And yet again, I must send you all into danger... a different sort, this time around, but danger nonetheless.
King of Ragni: I remember each face which passes through my castle. I rarely see any of them again.
King of Ragni: But this time... I have faith we will meet once more. Go on, young hero. YOur mission lies ahead of you.
Tasim: ...back to Fruma. I've only just come back to Wynn, and now...
Tasim: But it had to happen eventually. And I do want answers. So... in we go.
Tasim: I'll be heading to the Nemract Seaskipper, if you want to tag along.

Seaskipper Captain: ...

Player: It sounds very suspicious. Why the sudden interest? Why now?

hints: The rest must be waiting up ahead...

Tasim: ...

Captain Kymer: Yes, yes, fine. We've not been able to get a word out of any of these soldiers! Do we even have the right time and place?

Before the Gates to Fruma open:
Mel: S'anyone's guess when they'll actually let us in...
After the Gates to Fruma open:
Mel: Oh! The gate!!
A Sovereign's Herald will come out of the gate as the group turns to face him.
Sovereign's Herald: Attention!! Attention, Wynn representatives!!

Sovereign's Herald: I hereby introduce you to The Evermoving Zephyr, the ruler of the Auburn Forest, the latest in the line of one of Fruma's great noble houses! His lordship, Sovereign Zhiraok Nasin!
The Sovereign's Herald moves to the right. The camera cuts to the antechamber, showing guards ready themselves in the presence of the Sovereign. The door opens to reveal Sovereign Zhiraok.
Sovereign Zhiraok: Thank you, Xao. Now!
Sovereign Zhiraok: Soldiers of Wynn! Her Majesty welcomes you to the province, as guests of the crown!
Sovereign Zhiraok: Follow me, and you will be escorted to the royal palace. Let's not keep her waiting you all are of great importance to her.

The group go into the province, starting at Fort Torann. Most members stare in awe, while Tasim looks back and nods at the Player. Tasim: What'd you think?

Meh. I've seen better.

Her Majesty: Your work to battle against the blight beyond our walls has been of great interest. You have certainly made our province proud.
Her Majesty: You must have questions on the nature of your summons. All will be revealed but first, allow me to introduce two of my wonderful Sovereigns.
Sovereign Zhiraok: You heard my name, but let me introduce myself. I am

Her Majesty: Enough of the boring talk! It is time for the welcoming feast!
Her Majesty: We would like to share a taste of what our province has to deliver. Please find your way to the grand dining hall, situated just behind me.

stages.title: Stage 1
hints: Dr. Picard: Success! Success, success, SUCCESS! I'm a genius, the smartest man alive!
Dr. Picard: You there, random bystander! You have witnessed a magical marvel! I have just successfully restored my memories from years ago!
Dr. Picard: You look to be from Fruma, yes? So you know just as well as I that your memories of your life before have vanished. Poof. Gone!
Dr. Picard: But with this device... we can change that! Restore what has been lost! Recover the you get the point.
Dr. Picard: Now, I'm in great need of test subjects... You would do well as one, yes, but I need to be more certain this thing works.
Dr. Picard: Listen here! I have a proposition to make. You'd like your memories back, yes? Bring me enough test subjects, and I can show you what you've lost!
Dr. Picard: Let's see, let's see... We need individuals originally from Fruma. There are a few of those around here.
Dr. Picard: You can start with the would-be sailor, Caid. You'll find him just past Elkurn follow the path until you reach the river.
Dr. Picard: In the meantime, I'll be making adjustments here... It's not perfect just yet. I'm still missing large portions of my memory... Hm? You're still in here? Get going!

Caid: ... Yeah, alright. I'll come with you to get my memory checked out. Just, do me a solid first, alright?
Caid: I'm something of a builder. Figured I'd try my hand at making a ship, and, here it is! Pretty good, right?
Looking good!
Caid: That's what I'm talking about, take that Reynauld! I knew someone would like it!

Caid: You'll have to promise me you won't tell Reynauld but... Some of the more exotic components have been comin' from the guard's quarters. Nothing big! Just some stuff skimmed off the top...
Caid: I only need one more part to finish it off, and well, you see... A shipment just arrived from the blacksmith's... You see where I'm going with this?
Caid: Get me the part from the blacksmith's and I'll come with you to Picard's tower. I could hardly leave my baby alone unfinished like this now, could I?

stages.title: Stage 3

hints: In order to find the treasure you have to go to all three islands and get a map piece from each one.
Looking towards the islands from your starting point in the ocean, there are three islands. One is to the left, one in the middle, and one is to the right.

On the left island, which you can enter at [8705, 11, 6886], you have to climb to the top of the mountain, avoiding a rockfall and doing a bit of parkour part of the way up. At the very top, at [-7866, 131, -3488], there is a red "X" with a button in the middle; press the button to get the map piece.

On the middle island, which you can enter at [8742, 12, 6920], you will be taken to the water next to the island. Do not attempt to climb it, you get the map piece from the watery cave near where you spawn. you have to press buttons to get the map piece. Press the buttons 2, 5, and 6 to solve the riddle. This will open a door that takes you to a small room with a red "X" and a button in the middle; press the button to get the map piece.

On the right island, which you can enter at [8703, 11, 6939], you have to fight multiple waves of mobs. In the first wave, a swarm of mobs will spawn, which occasionally drop Magical Thunder Shards when you kill them. You can use two Shards to spawn each of three minibosses underneath the crystals around the arena. Once you have killed all three, put all of their drops into the hopper that will appear at [-7916, 64, -3806]. This will give you the map piece.

All 3 map pieces seem to fit together...

[+1 Treasure Map]
It looks like the island with the crystals. Maybe there is a way to the tallest part of the island on the side?

When you are teleported to it, turn to the left and follow the path to the top of the island shown on the new map. Boss tips

If this fight is proven to be too difficult , you can try to wait until level 75 and complete Tower of Ascension (Quest) for champion armor first. Champion armor can help for this fight. Otherwise I would personally recommend grabbing Purified Helmet of the Legends,Cloak of Luminosity,Abysso Galoshes and Photon as these are free quest reward gears with amazing stats.

Using spells that have piercing or AOE like arrow bomb and ice snake will help hitting bob while clearing the swords easier. Try destroy the water one as quickly as you can as it heals the boss a solid amount.
In phase 1 , NEVER stay close to the boss. Try stay away from the boss as its arrow storm can quickly shred your health dealing almost lethal damage.
In phase 2 , the boss will occasionally vanish. During this try to keep walking backwards to prevent getting hit by his melee attack.
In phase 4 , an easy way to dodge his charge attack is by moving in a triangle shape.
You can utilize knockback or slowness spells to try get the boss Abit away from you like uproot and ice snakes.

stages.title: Stage 12
stages.task: Kill the Corrupter of Worlds in the cave at [-714, 61, -963] and bring proof of its death to Kelight at [-692, 63, -975].
hints: Once you enter the main cave, passing the second pair of Legend Guards, the following dialogue will play:
You start to feel weaker as you enter the cave...

Continue through the cave. As you do, you will be able to see the Corrupter of Worlds flash by a few times; one of these times is while you are stopped at a barrier, and some Corrupted Soldiers will spawn behind you. Continue either way around the pillar, until you reach a gray leaf wall. Once you do, go through it and jump down, which will trigger the next dialogue:
It feels as though demons are starting to consume your mind... Maybe it wasn't a good idea to enter this place...

Jumping down will also trigger another short appearance of the Corrupter of Worlds, and cause a large horde of Corrupted Soldiers, Warriors, Assassins, Mages, Archers, and normal Corrupteds to spawn in the room. You do not have to kill these to progress, although it can be difficult to get past them without doing so. Either way, the tunnel out of the room leads straight to the boss fight - once you stand on the soul sand at the end, the Corrupter of Worlds will walk up and break the soul sand, knocking you into the boss room.
▸ Tips
If you have trouble with defeating the Corrupter of Worlds, bring a party of people to assist you in killing it, preferably with a mage for Heal Spells.

Bring a Ragni or Detlas teleport scroll with you so you don't have to walk too far to get to Kelight. Make sure you have completed The Passage (and Tunnel Trouble if you use a Detlas scroll), otherwise you will have to use a Troms scroll, which is more expensive.
Try to acquire all the items for making the helmet before doing the quest (except the Light Dust and Sky Vapor, which cannot be acquired beforehand). It will make the quest much faster and easier.

For maximum efficiency for getting the items for Garull, you can get the [Old Touroto Hide] during the Canyon Condor quest, [Aseado Leaf] during Lost Soles, [Maro's Eye Jewel] mid-way through the Zhight Island quest and [Coral of Nelfors] right after Stage 9 as you can easily get to Nemract via the Mysterious Obelisk near Tempo Town (requires Tempo Town Trouble completion) to Nemract, then either take the Seaskipper or Nexus to get to Selchar, which is very close to where you can acquire the Coral of Nelfors.
After all of this, you can either;

Use a Troms teleport scroll (or take the Seaskipper to Nesaak, then go to the Great Bridge (defeating the boss is required if you haven't done it already), through the jungle and then into Troms) to quickly get back and access The Passage), or;
Travel to Ragni either by the tunnel in Detlas (requires Tunnel Trouble completion) or with a teleport scroll, and then to Garull via the Pigman's Ravine.

stages.title: Stage 1
stages.task: Speak to King Burtan.
hints: King Burtan: Hello, traveller. I suppose you have seen the horrific damage inflicted to Thanos.
King Burtan: A fearsome dragon named Ozoth is responsible. She lives atop a mountain named for her, called Ozoth's Spire.
King Burtan: She used to be entirely docile to us dwarves, but ever since she began nesting, she’s become hostile.
King Burtan: Judging by your impressive equipment, you look like you've seen your fair share of large creatures.
King Burtan: I am not asking you to slay Ozoth, that would be nearly impossible. I just need you to feed this enchanted flower to her.
King Burtan: It’s a native Elven species usually diluted down to create sleep medicine.
King Burtan: The pure substance, however, is very potent and it should calm the beast, perhaps enough to make it hibernate until her egg hatches.
King Burtan: We sent in Tharroli to do the job, but I bet he lost his dang flower again. The only issue is, dragons do not like flowers. You will have to force feed it to her.
King Burtan: To reach Ozoth's Spire, go through a cave to the north of the entrance, near the fortress entrance. Follow the flames of Ozoth's breath from there.

stages.title: Stage 2
stages.task: Feed the Enchanted Flower to Ozoth.
hints: It appears you've been swallowed. You should probably bring the flower to Ozoth's stomach, if you can find a way there. Perhaps there's something at the top of the throat.

stages.title: Stage 3
stages.task: Bring the Enchanted Flower to Ozoth’s stomach.
hints: 1st block: top-middle
2nd block: left-center
3rd block: bottom-right
4th block: bottom-left
Puzzle 2:
1. Wooden Shovel
2. Wooden Block
3. Coal
4. Block of Coal
5. Lava Bucket
Tharroli: Great, another person fell down here. No one seems to be able to survive the trip down… except for me.
Tharroli: I was supposed to bring some magic flower to calm down the dragon, but I must've lost mine at some point.
Tharroli: Wait, you brought one? Oh, thank goodness! We still might be able to save my fellow dwarves.
Tharroli: I'll take your flower and just toss it down into the pit. It should calm the dragon. It's a shame that we’re pretty much just another sacrifice though...
Tharroli: There. The flower's gone. Now, I can tell you're thinking about escaping. However, it isn't as simple as that.
Tharroli: First of all, you'd have to make it across this pit, which is nearly impossible. And if you manage to do that, who knows what else is ahead?
Tharroli: Try to escape if you wish, but it’s probably hopeless. I'll think of another way out, you go ahead without me.

stages.title: Stage 4
stages.task: Escape from the inside of Ozoth.
hints: Press the button to open the door
Note - In the parkour over the lava, first head to the right where the button is and go back to the left to where the door is.

stages.title: Stage 5
stages.task: Return to King Burtan to tell him of your success.
hints: King Burtan: Have you fed the flower to Ozoth? You have? Thank you, I cannot believe you were brave enough to approach a dragon. I only curse myself for not honouring my people.
King Burtan: Ozoth was responsible for countless deaths of my men. Not that I can blame her, you should see dwarf women when they rear their young!
King Burtan: I trust the task was no mean feat. You deserve a reward for this triumph.
King Burtan: You have also earned the trust of the dwarves. You will now be allowed into other dwarven cities.
King Burtan: Thank you, kind traveller. May we meet again.

stages.task: Get to the mouse nest by following the cheese trail and get rid of the pest.
hints: To get to the mouse nest, you follow the cheese crumbs to a plant. Climb up the plant and it will launch you up. Continue following the cheese trail to a bookshelf at [2, 36, -7380], and you will have to solve a puzzle. The hint is 'Even just a first letter can tell you a story... Sometimes it can even reveal a color...'. The answer to the puzzle is:
Battalion of History #7: An Ancient Pact: Brown
Gavel's Fine Dining: Green
Occurences of Mysterious *Magic*: Orange
Raging Seas, A Wynn Tale: Red
Pernicious Prankset: A Starter Guide: Pink
Years of No Return: Yellow

The books will then reveal a staircase leading you to the first checkpoint. While the end of the blue carpets might seem like a dead end, climb up the brown mushroom to continue following the cheese trail. Eventually, you will end up at a tunnel where several Razorice live. Continue through the tunnel to the end where you end up at an arena to fight the Razorouse King. Fight him to get the Razorouse King Tail to open the way to the blue mushroom.
You've taken care of the Razorice problem, now you just have to find that blue mushroom Psilo was talking about...
After the above dialogue has played, you will now arrive at the second checkpoint. Continue following the cheese trail to the blue mushroom.

stages.title: Stage 7
stages.task: Give Psilo the good news about the mice.
hints: ▸ Tips
If you see a Regular Zombie, don't fight him, because he will regenerate his health too fast and it isn't meant to fight him in the Quest.

You can skip most of the quest that takes place inside of the mushroom house while small by using movement skills to get straight to the blue mushroom. For example, there is a red, 'bouncy' mushroom with an iron plate on the left somewhat below the blue mushroom at the top. The quest can then be completed by walking into the blue mushroom, without fighting any boss or anything at all really.
When you kill the mini Boss, you must follow the cheese path again.
Be sure to get a Small Mushroom at [-305, 91, -7705] during Stage 3, as it is needed for a later quest.
names: Be sure to get a Small Mushroom at [-305

stages.title: Stage 1
stages.task: Speak to General Elix at [758, 164, -4463] in Kandon-Beda.
hints: General Elix: ... Alright, let's see here... Private! Give me a report!
Private Walder: Sir, our readings are postive! Stablility is at 96%, and shows no sign of dropping.
Private Walder: Readings are positive!
General Elix: Excellent. Keep an eye on everything, and let me know if something comes up. Now, I need to go find...-
General Elix: Hmph. And who exactly are you? This site is off-limits to civilians.
[1] Just an adventurer passing through.
General Elix: Adventurer. Of course. Well, as it stands, we're doing rather dangerous work here. I'll have to ask you to-
[2] What's this device for?
General Elix: ... The stabilizer? We're doing rather dangerous work here, keeping the thing beyond that cliff passive. So, I'll have to ask you to-
The ground will then shake beneath you.
Private Walder: General! Stability is dropping, and fast!
Private Walder: General!
General Elix: What?! Of all times for it to-
General Elix: Urgh... Soldiers, follow protocol! Secure what you can, and leave what you can't! And- you! I haven't forgotten about you. As soon as this all cleans up, we'll-
General Elix: Gah! This damned Colossus! What I wouldn't give to...
General Elix: ... It's over. Walder! Survey the damages to our equipment! Morec! Take count of injuries around the base, make sure everyone's safe!
Private Walder: Yes sir!
Two scientists named ??? will walk up to the stabilizer.
???: General! We came as soon as we could- we were down in the library and the exit co- Oh. Wow.
General Elix: Well, Rhay, you're here now, yes? What do you think, can you fix it? We'll need to get it working before-
One of the scientist's names changes to Rhay.
Rhay: Can I- No, of course I can't fix it! Not on my own, especially since we don't have the proper equipment around here! Ugh, how long has it even been since last time?
???: It has been... three days... give or take. Rhay... you know we can't keep-
Rhay: The stabilizer has been working so far, Ineos! It's some of the finest technology our province has had to offer, and it has been working!
The other scientist's name changes to Ineos.
Ineos: Rhay, you know... as well as I do... that it is getting worse. The Protector is... growing resistant to... your machines. We need... a new plan.
Rhay: Yes, well, as soon as you come up with one, I'll be glad to hear it! But so far, you've barely gotten anything-
Rhay: ...
Ineos: ...
Rhay: ... Sorry. I'm sorry, I didn't mean that. General, to answer your question... The stabilizer itself is damaged, but you should have what's needed to repair it here.
Rhay: The issue is that the controls look like they're fried! And we don't have any replacement parts stored here. We'll have to travel back to Corkus, and...
[1] Is there anything I can do to help?
General Elix: ...Right. You. You're an adventurer, yes? And you appear to be well-equipped. Then you'll be traveling to Corkus with Rhay, and assist with whatever is needed there.
Rhay: Huh?
Rhay: Wait, General-... Right. Alright. In that case... I'll give you time to prepare. We'll take the Hot Air Balloon to travel to Corkus, so I'll meet you there. We don't have any time to waste.
Ineos: And I will... return to the library. I trust... you will succeed... But we must... prepare for the... worst.
Ineos: Alright...
Rhay will then run towards the Hot Air Balloon while Ineos heads towards the library.

stages.title: Stage 2
stages.task: Meet Rhay at the Hot Air Balloon at [770, 162, -4385]
hints: Rhay: Ah, you're here! Well, if you're ready, then we'd best be off. Just hop aboard this balloon, and the captain will take us where we need to go.
Rhay: I can tell you more while we travel, but we need to get going quick. There's no telling how much time we have before-
Rhay: Right, right. Don't mind me, I'm just a little on edge, for... well, obvious reasons. Just hop aboard.
names: » Meet Rhay at the Hot Air Balloon at [7

stages.title: Stage 3
stages.task: Travel to Corkus City via the Hot Air Balloon at [775, 165, -4382]
hints: Rhay: Well, there it is! The Canyon Colossus itself. The source of all our problems here at Kandon-Beda.
Rhay: So! How much do you already know? I know we dragged you into this without telling you much, so... I can fill you in on the details.
[1] I heard the General mention it. So it's the source of those earthquakes?
Rhay: Oh, he did? Right, that makes sense. Well, you're right in that it's the source of the earthquakes, but there's more to it than that.
Rhay: You've seen the Sky Islands, right? Heard of the Fracturing. From what I can tell, what happened to that region a thousand years ago is happening again, here and now.
[1] And the Colossus is what's causing it?
Rhay: Yes, exactly. It's been malfunctioning for a long time now, and it's starting to tear the canyon apart. That's where we come in.
[2] I don't know much about it. Can you tell me about it?
Rhay: Well... To start with, it's an ancient thing. It was built long before even the doguns can remember, and they've lived in this region for thousands of years.
Rhay: According to Ineos, the doguns used to be responsible for keeping it calm, but ever since the dwarves came in and started their war, that knowledge has been lost to time.
Rhay: Which is... a problem! The Colossus has been malfunctioning for hundreds of years, and it's reaching its breaking point. If we don't stop it, it'll tear the canyon apart.
[1] Alright. How do we stop it?
[3] I've seen the kinds of things it does to the canyon.
Rhay: Oh? So you've traveled the canyon, then. Yeah, then you've seen how the canyon twists and changes.
Rhay: It destroys peoples' homes, it traps them deep within the maze-like valleys... And, more recently, it has been tearing a hole into the void.

Rhay: This thing is ancient, and we don't know how it works. The best we can do is try to keep it from reaching its breaking point, and prevent the canyon from meeting the same fate as the Sky Islands.
Rhay: So, Gavel's government contacted us in Corkus some time ago, requesting our help to deal with this threat.
Rhay: Our council agreed, and we got to work designing a machine that could replicate the dogun magic that pacified that Colossus long ago.
Rhay: We've had Ineos' help on that front. He and I have been working here in Kandon-Beda to ensure things are running smoothly. Which... evidently, they are not.
Rhay: ... We'll be fine! We're going to meet up with my husband at Corkus, and he'll know what to do. He always does.
[1] What are we going to do at Corkus?
Rhay: Our people there will be able to get us the parts we need to repair the device. This... this isn't the first it's exploded. I had hoped that this time we would have gotten it stable, but...
Rhay: But, hey! We have it under control. We're always able to repair it quickly enough to keep it running while the Colossus is active.
[2] Your husband?

Rhay: Oh! Yeah. He's the one responsible for the design and production of this device. He's got a talent for designing these sorts of things, without him... well, we'd be in a much worse situation than we are now.
Rhay: I'll be glad to see him again. It's been a while since I last had to travel to Corkus, and... Well, I'm confident he'll know what to do here. He always does.
Rhay: ... Right! Hey, it looks like we're almost there. We'll be able to get this all sorted out, and we'll be back to Kandon-Beda in no time.
names: » Travel to Corkus City via the Hot Air

stages.title: Stage 4
stages.task: Find the contact in the factory at [-1529, 71, -3083]
hints: Rhay: Alright, let's just head on in. My husband should be around here somewhere...
Maxie will then walk out of the factory.
Maxie: Rhay, love! You're back already? Our next routine maitenance isn't for another- Wait, ? What are you doing here?
Rhay: I... You two know each other?
Maxie: Of course we do - they're the one who helped me with all the Factory stuff! How did you two meet?
Rhay will then turn to look at you.
Rhay: They just showed up at Kandon-Beda and agreed to help us with... - Why didn't you bring this up earlier?
[1] Must have slipped my mind.
Rhay: It must have...- right. Well, if anything that makes you even more qualified to help us out, I guess! I can't believe I didn't recognize you...?
Maxie: Okay, right, back to the question - what are you two doing here already? There's another few days or so until our next routine maitenance, isn't there?
[2] Wait, Maxie, you got married? Why wasn't I invited?
Maxie: I did send you an invite! I gave it to... you know, that that one captain who ferries people around! But then you didn't show up to the wedding, so I guess it didn't reach you...
Maxie: Look, you're a hard person to reach! You've been all over the world at this point, including Kandon-Beda of all places- speaking of, why are you two here?
Rhay: !!!
Rhay: Right! Right. Got a little distracted there... Uh, we've run into a problem back at Kandon-Beda. We experienced an undetected seismic event, and the device was heavily damaged.
Rhay: We should be able to finish most of the repairs with what materials we have there, but we're missing a Magmaflux Capacitor for the control panel.
Nodise will then walk up behind Maxie.
Maxie: ... Oh. That's going to be a problem. We haven't had an opportunity to make more parts yet - it hasn't been long enough since our last maitenance. So... I'm not sure what we-
Nodise: I overheard the conversation from over there- good to see you Rhay, by the way- But. We may not have any capacitors left up here, but I know where you can get one.
Nodise: We repurposed this factory for our needs, but it was built here to process resources from the mines below.

Nodise: Though it was discontinued, it's still very likely that there are still miner mechs down there- and some of the more powerful models made use of very similar circuits to the capacitors we use today.

Maxie: ... You're right! If they're still down there, we should be able to scrap one of the bots and reuse its circuits. , we can send you down into the mines to find what we need, while we prepare up here!
[1] Alright, I can do that.
Rhay: Alright... Good luck down there! Find the bot, destroy it, and bring the capacitor back up! Just step on the platform in the middle of the factory when you're ready.
[2] I need to prepare first.
Maxie: Okay. That's fine, just make it quick! You know we can't waste any time here.
names: » Find the contact in the factory at [-1

stages.title: Stage 5
stages.task: Retrieve the part from the cave at [-1529, 69, -3104]
hints: Maxie: Door opening in 3...
Maxie: 2...
Maxie: 1...
[!] Central bore tunnel opening! Exercise extreme caution around the deep drop.
The door below you will open, sending you to the cave with the mechs. As you make your way through the cave, it will start to shake.
Mining Robots: INTRUDER DETECTED. HOSTILE ENGAGEMENT AUTHORISED.
The Mining Robots will then spawn, and you must kill 4 to proceed.
Mining Robots: DEPLOYING SECONDARY ANTI-INTRUDER MEASURES.
Another wave will spawn, requiring you to kill 8 more.
Mining Robots: DIVERTING ALL AVAILABLE UNITS TO HALT INTRUDER.
A final wave of 12 mining robots will spawn. Kill them all to get to the boss.
The Mother Drill: THIS IS A RESTRICTED AREA. REQUESTING AUTHORISATION FOR USE OF LETHAL FORCE AGAINST INTRUDER.
The Mother Drill: AUTHORISATION GRANTED.
The ground will then shake as the Mother Drill comes out of the ground.

The Mother Drill's fight is fairly simple, as it has a custom spell, Drill, which will teleport the Mother Drill to a certain spot in the arena. The spot is telegraphed by several dirt particles coming out of it. Once the boss is as 65,000 HP, it will call for backup.
The Mother Drill: DIVERTING MINER MECHS TO HALT INTRUDER.
You will then have to kill 12 of the mining mechs that were fought prior to the boss fight. Once all 12 have been killed, you can then go back to fighting the Mother Drill.
[+1 Magmaflux Capacitor]
names: » Retrieve the part from the cave at [-1

stages.title: Stage 6
stages.task: Return to the hot air balloon at [-1526, 71, -3067] with the Magmaflux Capacitor.
hints: Rhay: Amazing work! I'll get us back to Kandon-Beda with that capacitor as quick as possible.
Maxie: Good to see you again, . Good luck with the colossus. And Rhay... come home as soon as you can.
Maxie: Fly safe, both of you.
names: » Return to the hot air balloon at [-152

stages.title: Stage 7
stages.task: Return to General Elix with the Corkian Stabiliser
hints: Rhay: Well... that went better than expected, really. I still can't believe you didn't tell me you already knew Maxie.
Rhay will then walk to General Elix and Ineos.
Rhay: Oh, wow. It looks like they've managed to fix up the machine pretty well, all things considered. Just this part left to get it running again...
General Elix: Hmph. Rhay, there you are. Seeing as you've returned, I gather everything went smoothly at Corkus?
Rhay: Smoothly enough, General! We have what we need to repair the control panel. We'll be able to get the stabilizer running again!
General Elix: Well?! What are you waiting for? Finish the repairs, we can't afford to lose any time with this damned Colossus looming over us.
Rhay: Yes, sir! Alright. , just slot the capacitor in right... there. I'll make sure it runs smoothly.
Right-click the machine to insert to Magmaflux Capacitor.
[-1 Magmaflux Capacitor]
The machine will start up.
General Elix: There we are. Now, let's get this thing running again! Walder, keep an eye on stability! And... Rhay. You're confident this will work?
Rhay: I-I'm sure. This is our last chance. We have to hold out hope that the stabilizer will hold.
The ground will then shake.
Rhay: Alright, alright... It's now or never... Hold, stabilizer, hold!
The ground will keep on shaking as fire comes off of the stabilizer, before eventually exploding.
Rhay: ... Oh. That's... that's it, then. It's over. We failed.
Ineos: I... am sorry, Rhay. I had... hoped it would work. In truth... I do not have... a plan... either.
Ineos: The Elders... would have known... what to do... But they are... long gone. Nothing but... ruins remain.
[1] The Elders?
Ineos: The Elders... They were... the greatest... of doguns. As old... as the oldest stones... and wise... as the earth itself...
Ineos: They were capable... of magic... beyond what any... of us could achieve. They alone... could calm our... Protector.
[1] What happened to the Elders?
Ineos: They were... sealed away. Frozen in... the deepest... of ice. When the dwarves... slew Garaheth... the Elders... fell with him.
Ineos: Such atrocities... The war... My people... But it is not... to dwell on, now. There are... more important... things at hand.
[1] But the war is over. The dwarves and doguns have made peace.
Ineos: I... I did not... know of this. My people... are free? How long... has it been... since I have seen... my home?
Ineos: You... Adventurer. We must... speak to my people. Our chieftain... will know... how we may free... the Elders.
General Elix: If there is a chance... We have to take it. Ineos, , take the balloon. We'll do whatever we can here. Now, go! There's no time to waste!

stages.title: Stage 8
stages.task: Meet Ineos and Rhay at the Hot Air Balloon at [770, 162, -4385].
hints: Rhay and Ineos will be by the Hot Air Balloon. Once you get in, you will fly over Ahmsord before landing in the Dogun Settlement in the Molten Heights.
Ineos: I have never... seen the Heights... from above. I wonder... if their glow... holds the same strength... it does from below...
Ineos: I only hope... the Elders... are not gone... for good. We greatly need... their wisdom.
Ineos: Ah... I believe us... to be landing...
names: » Meet Ineos and Rhay at the Hot Air Bal

stages.title: Stage 9
stages.task: Travel to Molten Heights with Ineos via the Hot Air Balloon at [770, 162, -4385]
hints: Korzim and two other Doguns will appear alongside him.
Korzim: ... Hello. What a... strange sight... to see you landing... at our village... in such a contraption...
Korzim turns to face Ineos.
Korzim: And... is that... Ineos? We thought... the dwarves... had turned you into rubble...
Ineos: I escaped... It is a long... story, Korzim. We do not... have time. Where is... your father?
Korzim: He is... below. They are... freeing the frozen... in New Taloka. Why do you... wish to speak... with him?
Ineos: The Protector... is angered. We must find... the Elders. They will know... how to calm it.
Korzim: The... Protector... I understand. I will... bring you two... to him. Sidio... Raetin... I leave you two... in charge.
The Dogun on the left has its name changed to Sidio, while the one on the right is changed to Raetin.
Korzim: Now, let us... travel. Through flame... and through stone...
Korzim will then create a portal that you can walk through to fast-travel to New Taloka.
names: » Travel to Molten Heights with Ineos vi

stages.title: Stage 10
stages.task: Speak to Rodoroc's King and the Dogun Chieftain at New Taloka at [1456, 16, -5151]
hints: Korzim: We are... here. Taloka was... one of the first to fall... in the war. We have been... working with the dwarves... to restore it.
Korzim and Ineos will then walk to a group having King Draani, Chieftain Paku, a regular Dogun named Edac, and a Dwarven Technician trying to unfreeze a Dogun.
King Draani: Are we all ready?
Edac: Ready...
Dwarven Technician: Ready!
King Draani: Very well. Begin on three. One... Two... Three!
Dwarven Technician: Beginning reheating cycle! Stand back from the subject.
The Dwarven Technician will then run some machinery to unfreeze a Dogun.
Unsealed Dogun: ... Where... am... I? How long... has it... been...?
The Unsealed Dogun turns its attention towards the technician.
Unsealed Dogun: ...Dwarf... You... you froze me... I will... I will...!
Chieftain Paku and Edac run around to stop the Unsealed Dogun from attacking the technician.
Chieftain Paku: Calm yourself... Delg. Our war... has ended. We are... freed. You have been... freed.
The Unsealed Dogun's name changes to Delg.
Dogun Delg: ... Freedom? Hundreds... of years... of war... And we are... free?
Chieftain Paku: Yes. We are free... to roam our home... once more. Edac... Escort Delg... and help him re-adjust... to the heights.
Delg will then walk away with Edac.
King Draani: Ah, ! It's good to see you again. We haven't seen you around here since... since the end of it.
Chieftain Paku: Yes. We have been... hard at work... these past weeks. Taloka will soon... stand once more. And many... of our sealed bretheren... have been returned to life.
King Draani: Ah, but we can talk more about that later. Tell me, what brings you here today? Is there something you need from us?
[1] The Canyon Colossus is tearing apart the canyon, and we need your help.
Ineos will then walk up to Draani.
Ineos: The situtation... is dire. The Great Protector... has been left alone... for far too long. We need... the wisdom... of our Elders. Do you know... where they are sealed?

King Draani: The Elders?! Yes, we know where they are sealed. However, retrieving them is no simple task. It would take us years to break past the defenses, and we have countless other doguns to release first.
Chieftain Paku: The Protector?!
Chieftain Paku: Ineos... I want our Elders free... as much as you do. But our Protector... has stood firm... for hundreds of years. It can stand... for another-
Another earthquake will happen, affecting all NPCs in the area.
Chieftain Paku: No... Has it truly... fallen this far..?
King Draani: ... That was your Protector? How powerful is it, if it can reach this far?
Korzim: If the Protector... could shake even the Heights... It could destroy... half of this province.
Chieftain Paku: Draani... the Elders must be freed. They alone... would know how to calm it.
King Draani: Yes... I understand. Very well. , I will take you to the Elders' vault. I hold the keys to open the way forward. Paku, gather your people. See if anyone has alternative solutions.
Chieftain Paku: We will... search for one. I cannot... promise that one exists.
King Draani: , let us go. It sounds as if we have very little time to waste.
King Draani: I will make preparations, and meet you at the Vault of Ice.
names: » Speak to Rodoroc's King and the Dogun

stages.title: Stage 11
stages.task: Enter the Dogun Vault within the lower Freezing Heights at [1512, 34, -5468]
hints: King Draani: ... Ahem. This is the entrance, then. One of our most closely guarded secrets... I was hoping not to have to confront this reminder for a while yet...
King Draani: But it seems we don't have much choice now. I have the keys, let's go inside.
Draani will then open the Vault of Ice.
names: » Enter the Dogun Vault within the lower

stages.title: Stage 12
stages.task: Unlock the Dogun Vault to find the Elders.
hints: King Draani: Rather cold in here, isn't it? A vault carved into a drake's True Ice... I suppose my ancestors hoped to seal these doguns in here forever. I'll be glad to disappoint them.
King Draani: Quickly, then, let us proceed to the primary door. I pray the Elders will be responsive to our situation with the Colossus.
Draani will then walk towards the Dogun Elders' vault.
King Draani: In any case... Let me see if I can open this second gate. It should be as simple as...
Draani will attempt to use magic to open the vault, but it fails as the door is unresponsive.
King Draani: Hm. That... didn't work. This magic is old, and I have never took the time to learn it properly... Alright. We have alternatives.
Draani will then walk to a parkour course to the right of the door.
King Draani: If my memory serves correctly, there should be a manual override on the other side of this chasm.
King Draani: The issue is that treacherous pool of lava on the way... and I don't think my knees are up to the task of jumping over it all.
King Draani: I would usually never do this, but these are desperate times. Here, take my Trusty Grappling Hook. It should help you get over to the switch.
King Draani: It has limitations, though. It will only be able to latch onto those blue rocks on the walls - and I'll be taking it back once you're finished, thank you very much!
[+1 Trusty Grappling Hook]

While on the parkour course, you will use the Trusty Grappling Hook to latch onto the blue rocks, and arrows will point your way. Sometimes, some rocks will be under an overhang, and can only be grappled once you are under the rock. After the first checkpoint, your path will diverge, and you can grab onto a ladder or go underneath the orange platforms. The upper path has you perform some tricky maneuvers, such as jumping down and grappling onto a blue rock while falling, while the lower path will have easier maneuvers at the start, once you get to a section, jump to a platform, and then King Draani will say the following:
King Draani: Hey, ! Looks like you're doing good so far, but if you get stuck remember you can jump and then grapple mid-air, that might help on some of those trickier platforms!

Following this, the maneuvers will be far more complex, being going under an overhang, and grappling onto a rock while in the air. Once you reach the end, there will be a machine and a button that will open the vault door.
King Draani: Looks like that unlocked it, ! Get yourself back over here and I'll open the door.
You use the grappling hook to swing back to the King in a dazzling feat of trapeze consisting of mid-air flips and acrobatic flourishes.
King Draani: There we are! Excellent work. You used that hook like a true expert! Ah, reminds me of the time-...
King Draani: ...Ahem. Excellent work, indeed. With the override activated, I should be able to do the rest of the work to open the gate.
King Draani: First, though, I'll be having that grappling hook back! Think of what could happen if you had free reign of that all over.
Draani will take the Trusty Grappling Hook from you, and then walk to the vault door. A cutscene will play as it opens, and once it does, Draani will walk inside.
King Draani: And so... I believe we have gone as far as we can.
[1] What do you mean?
King Draani: This is True Ice, . It has scarred this part of the Heights for centuries, ever since it was created by an ice dragon in my ancestors' conquest.
King Draani: It cannot be melted or burned through any means. It is why this location was chosen for their tomb. I'm afraid there is nothing more we can do.
[1] When were the elders first imprisoned here?
King Draani: At the end of the war, I imagine.
King Draani: As the final dogun settlements fell, and as Garaheth was slain for the first time, my ancestors must have sealed them deep in this ice.
King Draani: The... actions of the Dwarves after winning the war are well documented. I would not be surprised if our accounts describe this imprisonment as a great victory.
[2] Who put them here?
King Draani: The Dwarves, of course. Who else?
King Draani: I believe it was General Algard of the Dwarven army to order the Elders' imprisonments.
King Draani: He was lauded as a hero, naturally. Now... we must reap the consequences of such a decision.
[3] Tell me more about True Ice.
King Draani: True Ice is a material that cannot be melted or burned through by any means. Not even dogun magic has been able to make a dent.
King Draani: ... I imagine why this location was chosen to hold the elders. A prison from which they would never be able to escape.
King Draani: It is known for it to form naturally under extreme conditions... But the ice here is nowhere near natural.
King Draani: It was formed by an Ice Drake's Breath partway through the war- and, well, as you can see, it has remained here ever since.
King Draani: Just another remnant of our past mistakes, I suppose...
King Draani: Ahem. In any case- as I said, True Ice is impossible to break through, even with the most scorching flames.
[1] If an Ice Drake formed this ice... perhaps a fire dragon could melt it?
King Draani: I... I suppose that a dragon's breath might be able to melt it. That logic does make sense.
King Draani: We have little knowledge of what dragons were like, though. As they went extinct, that information became... useless. And so, it was lost.
King Draani: If anyone would know more about dragons, it would be the doguns.
King Draani: But none of that matters. All the dragons are gone, after all. We still have no options.
[1] What happened to all the dragons?
King Draani: Why, they died out. As Gavellian civilizations grew in size, the ferocity and size of a dragon was simply too much of a threat.
King Draani: Some were hunted. Some died of starvation. Eggs were taken from nests and shattered over boulders for the birds to feed on.
King Draani: Now all that are left are dragonlings - echoes of their once-great ancestors, with barely enough flames to singe your armor.
[2] Not all of the dragons are gone. I helped relocate one near Thanos.
King Draani: You- what? Near Thanos?
King Draani: A living dragon... You've done quite a lot, haven't you? Stopped a war, moved a dragon...
King Draani: Well... if there is a living dragon at Thanos... Then we still have hope! , we must ask for its help.
King Draani: Let us return to the others. I asked them to wait outside of Rodoroc... perhaps they'll be able to confirm that a dragon's breath would do the job.
[3] The Doguns would know about dragons?
King Draani: Indeed. The fire dragons that sided with them during the war. I'm sure you've come across the skeleton just outside Freezing Heights?
King Draani: Yes, well... the Dwarves needed a counter to the sheer power of a fire dragon in battle, and so they resorted to enslaving dragons and drakes of other elements.
King Draani: Like the Ice Drake that created this vault, and encased the Elders in the truest of ice.
[4] Read any good books recently?
King Draani: ... Well, there was this excellent novel of about one of those creatures from the Shiar, who had to travel to the Heights with this ring he had inherited-
King Draani: But I confess, these questions seem almost irrelevant. We have a more pressing issue at hand, .
[2] Could we shatter it somehow, with a weapon or spell?
King Draani: This ice is harder than obsidian itself. The crystals which form the material are bonded by ancient magic.
King Draani: Shattering it with such tools isn't an option. Perhaps there is a weapon that could break through, somewhere deep in our armory- after all, this vault had to be carved somehow...
King Draani: However, given the circumstances, I don't think we have the time to search for it. Even if we started now, our armory is enormous. It would take weeks to find what we need.
[3] Would lava from the Heights work?
King Draani: The lava of the Heights is nothing more than molten rock. Just a remnant of the shaping of these caverns.
King Draani: It's not nearly hot enough to melt True Ice. If it could, the Freezing Heights would have faded long ago.
[4] What's your favorite color?
King Draani: My... uhm... green is nice, I suppose? Though perhaps not very Dwarven...
King Draani: Red, then. Or orange! ...Although my bedsheets are the most wonderful shade of navy blue...
[4] What did you have for breakfast today?
King Draani: Breakfast... I had some eggs, I suppose. Though, I had no idea that breakfast would be my last, did I..?
King Draani: Hm... Had I known, maybe I would have chosen differently. Maybe I would have-... nevermind.
After you have told Draani a solution to the problem, he will then run towards the exit of the Vault.

hints: King Draani: ... so this is the situation we find ourselves in. Paku, what do you think? Would such a plan work?
Chieftain Paku: Hm... You may be correct... Draani. The magic in... a dragon's breath... was very potent. And to think... mighty Ozoth had survived... all these years...
Ineos: If Ozoth is alive... we must seek her help. If the doguns ask... for her aid, she will... give it.
King Draani: Well, that's as good a plan as any. , you'll travel to seek this dragon's counsel, along with... Ineos, was it? Good luck.
Ineos: You should... take the Trading Tunnel... . I will put the coordinates... in your Quest Book.

stages.title: Stage 15
stages.task: Travel to Ozoth's Spire at [206, 97, -5179] in an attempt to speak with her.
hints: You need to get to the path up to Ozoth's Spire. There should be signposts outside of Thanos...
Follow the arrow posts up to Ozoth's Spire, and when you reach the top, Ineos will be waiting for you.
Ineos: Ah... it is... good to... see you. We must... proceed to Ozoth... with all haste.
Ineos will follow you to talk with Ozoth.
Ineos: Ozoth the Dragon... Endless Kindler... we have come... to ask for your aid.
Ozoth: ...
Ineos: We are searching... for a way... to melt the truest... of ice. The fate... of Gavel... hangs in the balance.
Ineos: Doguns... and Dragons... our fates have been entwined... for centuries. We call on you now... Endless Kindler... to save this province.
Ozoth: ...
Ineos: I... see. ... Ozoth tells me... that an Everflame... will free the Elders.
[1] Where can we find one?
Ineos: ... well...
Ineos: The Endless Kindler... is willing to part... with hers. You must... retrieve it... from her stomach.
Ozoth: ...
Ineos: I would advise you... not to think... too much about this. When... you are ready... enter Ozoth's mouth and retrieve... the flame.
Ozoth's mouth will then open for you to enter her body.

stages.title: Stage 16
stages.task: Descend into Ozoth's belly to retrieve an Everflame.
hints: The first section of Ozoth's Stomach involves you having to grind 10 Muscle Tissues, which are dropped from Fiery Arteries and Starving Survivors. The Fiery Arteries can regenerate while the Starving Survivors don't.
After 10 Muscle Tissues are gathered, the next section is parkour to the Everflame. This parkour is fairly simple, and has no unique mechanics. Falling in the lava sends you back to the start.
At the end, you will find the Everflame. However, when you start to pick it up, several mobs will ambush you.
It looks like Ozoth's body is trying to prevent you from getting the Everflame!
At the end of the scuffle, you will get the Everflame and can leave Ozoth's stomach.
[+1 Everflame]

stages.title: Stage 17
stages.task: Travel to Rodoroc at [1233, 9, -5200] with an Everflame.
hints: Ineos: ! Have you retrieved... the Eternal Flame?
Ineos: Excellent. Endless Kindler... thank you... for your sacrifice. I will ensure... that your flame... is returned to you.
Ozoth: ...
Ineos: Ozoth apologises... if it was a bit hot... in there.
Ineos: Now, ... I was never the best... at the ancient magic... but I hope I have enough skill... to take us the short route back...
Ineos will then create a portal back to Rodoroc.
King Draani: You have returned! Is there news from Thanos? Did the dragon offer aid?
Ineos: She did... Ozoth has made a great sacrifice... for this province... but we have an Eternal Flame... to melt the ice.
Chieftain Paku: Well done... both of you. I will ensure... that the doguns thank her... properly. The dwarves would do well... to do the same.
King Draani: Yes, yes, but there's no time to worry about that now. Quick, let's get back to the-
Chieftain Paku: Be wary... of the Elders... Draani. It is unlikely they will react well... after their imprisonment. It is vital... you explain the situation... to them.
Chieftain Paku: I would join you... both... but the ice is inhospitable... to my kind. I wish the both of you... the best of luck.
King Draani: ...right. Yes. Well, there's no getting around it. Come, . We must unfreeze the elders and get them to listen to us. Bring the flame, I will meet you at the Vault.

stages.title: Stage 18
stages.task: Return to the Dogun Vault at [1512, 34, -5468] to free the Dogun Elders.
hints: King Draani: Well then, what are we waiting for! Let's free these elders, shall we?
King Draani: Just bring the Everflame to each of the cells, and melt through that True Ice.
Right-click on each of the Dogun Elders' cells to free them. A cutscene will play of them being freed.
King Draani: Excellent! We've done it! Now we just need to explain the situation-...
Elder Astal: We are freed.
King Draani: ...Ah. I suppose I did not... think this through. Ehm. Elders, I must apo-
The three elders walk towards Draani.
Elder Astal: Dwarf... Hm. The crimes... of your ancestors... must be repaid.
Elder Desint: However. We have... heard you speak. We have... learned of... the Protector's state.
Elder Iscor: We will... settle your debt... later. This situation... is a more pressing... concern. The Protector... must be calmed.
Elder Astal: ...Yes. You. Human. That was... dragonfire... was it not?
[1] It was.
Elder Astal: Then allow me... to borrow it. Its strength... will allow us... to restore ours. Now... Who now holds... the title... of Chieftain?
King Draani: A-ah! Paku is now the Dogun Chieftain. He would be at... At Taloka.
Elder Astal: Very well... We shall travel... through flame... and through stone...
The Dogun Elders will then use magic to warp you to Ineos and Chieftain Paku.
Chieftain Paku: ...The Elders... after all this time... to see you, again... in the flesh...
Elder Desint: Greetings, Paku. We have much... to discuss. But first... we must travel... to the Protector.
Elder Astal: Join us... Ineos and Paku. There is... very little time... to waste.
Elder Astal: Now, let us travel... (The following part of the line is High Gavellian) Through flame... and through stone...
The Elders will then teleport you and the crew to Korzim.
Chieftain Paku: Korzim... my son... join us. The Elders must see... to the Protector.
Korzim: Iscor... Astal... Desint... it has been... too long. I will come.
Korzim walks to the circle, before Astal warps everyone to Kandon-Beda.
Elder Astal: Earth and flame... fire and stone... transport us through your form! (In High Gavellian)
Rhay: -have to trust that they'll return!

General Elix: There's no time! I can feel the damned ground cracking beneath my feet, we have to turn to the final option. We've had demoltion mages on standby the past few days, our only choice is to-
Ineos: Rhay. Elix. My Elders... have been freed. They are here... to help... the Protector.
General Elix and Rhay turn to face you.
Elder Iscor: Join us... brave ones. You will see... that your efforts to save this Province... have not been in vain.
Rhay and General Elix will then join the circle, as Astal warps you a final time to the Canyon Colossus.
Elder Astal: Flames of the earth... take us to the Great Protector... to make our plea! (In High Gavellian)
