stages.title: Stage 19
stages.task: Travel to the Canyon Colossus at [611, 52, -4448] to attempt to calm it.
hints: Elder Astal: Great Protector... It is furious.
Elder Astal: Hmph. Foolish dwarves... This is what has come...of your needless war... You are fortunate...to have freed us now...
The Elders prepare to get ready for the ritual.
Elder Astal: Desint... Iscor... I will prepare... the ritual. Defend me... as I do so.
Astal will prepare the ritual as the other NPCs speak.
Elder Desint: Human. We will pull the Protector... away from the brink. That is all we can do now. All the power... we can muster.
Elder Iscor: You must enter... these sacred grounds. Battle through it to the end... Knock some sense... into it.
Ineos: Adventurer... We are counting...on you. We will try to...support you however we can.
Rhay: We'll do the best we can out here! I have some ideas already...
General Elix: Rhay, this isn't the time. Human. We have your back. You can do this.
Korzim: You have faced...worse odds before...have you not? You will face them...again.
The Elders take their places as the ritual begins.
Elder Astal: It is done. Desint... Iscor... Take your postions. We must... hold it back.
Elder Astal: Great Protector, lord of stone, hear our burning call. Your fury clouds your vision, your anger burns and twists our home. (In High Gavellian)
Elder Astal: We, the doguns, who now hold the final flame of a fallen god... We will hold you back. We will keep this land intact! (In High Gavellian)
Elder Astal: We will... hold it from here... human. Now... go! We will not... be able to hold it... for long...
Elder Astal: This crystal...will let you harness...our flame. Use it...to break through...its defenses.
Chieftain Paku will then walk up to you.
Chieftain Paku: ... Before you go. I will offer you... these powerful relics. Our people... have held them for... longer than I have lived. They may... help you on your quest.
King Draani: I cannot give you something as unique as what Paku has offered, but I can still lend you a sum from our treasury. Use it as you must, so long as you can calm that thing. Good luck.

hints: In the mineshafts, there will be a section where you control a minecart. stages.title: Stage 8
stages.task: Fight the Canary.
hints: During the Canary's fight, you will be unable to use spells.
In the first phase, several pellets will glide across the arena, and getting hit by one deals damage. After about 20 seconds, it will move on to the second phase.

In phase 2, the Canary will start to attack you by sending pellets towards you, as well as gliding on the ground. To defeat the second phase, you must destroy all 8 Bizarre Monoliths. If you fall off of the arena, you will be bounced back onto it while the Canary says a line. As you damage the Bizarre Monoliths, the Canary will say several things:
Each of the spells the Canary has are as follows:
Bizarre Fire: The Canary fires a pellet at you.
Bizarre Burst: The Canary fires 5 pellets at once at you.
Bizarre Strike: The Canary will mark an area on the arena that will deal damage to whoever is in it.
Glide: The Canary will glide across the ground, similar to the pellets in phase 1.

hints: Syndra: Player, it's good to see you. Have you been well?

What's up with Sui?
Syndra: It... isn't something you need to worry about. Not yet, at least.
Syndra: Magic... or, rather, curses have a tendency to be associated with bad memories.
Syndra: It's not my place to tell you why. Sui can share more if she wants to, later.
I thought you wouldn't force anyone?
Syndra: Sui is... the exception.
Syndra: I have my reasons for it. I believe it would be better for her to hear this now, rather than later.
Syndra: It's not my place to tell you why. Sui can share more if she wants to, later.

Rex: Here we are! So, could we get started already? Some of us actually have responsibilities.
Syndra: Seeing as everyone is here, yes, Rex, we may. Player, let us start with the basics.
Magic is... in everything.
Mora: Ah, yes, such as the cursed... the stories do tell of the original evil lurking within us. It would follow that it exists in all things.
Syndra: Indeed. So Player, how do you wield your magic?

Mora: Similar to the blessed implements of the crown's commanders, yes? I remember hearing of this from the military recruiters.
Rex: Don't those usually only have one specific blessing attached to them? I don't remember them being as... uh, flexible, I guess.
Syndra: You'd be correct, Rex, though the same principle applies. A blessed weapon is referred to as a "focus" by the crown. They allow the wielder to more easily access the blessing placed within.
Magic usually drains energy when I cast spells.
Syndra: Ah, I do have experience with this. We call it mana. Once one receives a blessing, it takes time to learn how to draw from your own source of mana.
Syndra: This is where foci come into play they are crafted or forged from mana-dense materials, and so provide a more easily accessible source to power one's blessing.
Most people in Wynn could use magic.
Rex: And, so... what? You think any of us could just... do it? That's hard to believe.
If given the right tools and training.
Mora: Ha! If it were truly the case, would there not be many, many more cursed ones running around? I concur with Rex, it seems outlandish.
Zeph: I d- d- don't know... Player doesn't seem like they're l- ly- like they're lying. What- wh- what if it is true?
Syndra: It would explain certain aspects of the crown's response to cursed ones...

Mora: Yes, precisely! My sister is correct. Any... "magic" not sourced from the crown is innately tainted, from my understanding.
Rex: Yeah, curses, blessings whatever. So, what, you think all of us could just... use "magic"? What would that even look like?
Casting magic requires belief, concentration and skill.
Rex: Ha. Right, sure. "Belief." So if I think hard enough, I can just start calling down lightning strikes?
Rex: Ugh. This was a waste of time.
Mora: Now, now, Rex. Don't be so hasty in writing it off entirely. You have seen with your own eyes what Player can do!
Zeph: Belief... I- I- I can do that.
Rex: Oh, come on Zeph, really? You can't seriously
Syndra: We're getting off track. Player, what else is there?
Magic comes in different forms for different people.
Zeph: So... s- so you don't even know what your m- ma- magic will look like?
Syndra: Correct. There are aptitude tests which the crown uses before giving out blessings, but those only provide an idea of the general typing.
Syndra: As an example I learned that I have an affinity for the fire element, but I didn't know what form that would take until I actually received my blessing.

Sui: ...

Syndra: Well, thank you for your time, Player. I think we'll call it there. You're all dismissed.

Syndra: Zeph, even if Player's information is true, it doesn't mean it's immediately applicable.

Syndra: Better than nothing, I suppose.
Syndra: It's hard to enjoy yourself with your experiences with the crown weighing you down, isn't it? I know the feeling.
Syndra: Mmn. I'd suggest to take what you can get. Happy moments like this can be fleeting, in my experience.
Syndra: If there's even the smallest spark of joy... take hold of it before it's gone. Cherish it while you still can. Try not to grow old and jaded like I have, would you?
Not really.
Syndra: Ha! It's alright. Neither have I.
Syndra: Every year... every single year, the crown hosts these festivals. Starting here, and moving around in a ring around the province.
Syndra: The festival's a holiday, a day of rest, of celebration. What a gift it is, not needing to work for a time! How generous.
Syndra: I can't stand it here... Every year, I convince myself I can bear it. The reminder it brings, of memories long passed. Every year, I'm proven wrong.
Syndra: ...Ah. It's time. The main event is about to begin.
What's the main event?
Syndra: Why, Her Majesty's annual speech, of course! It wouldn't be a Festival of the Crown if she didn't make an appearance, would it?
It's not the orchestra?
Syndra: Ha! No, no. Of course not. It wouldn't be a Festival of the Crown without a speech from Her Majesty herself, would it?
Syndra: Now... observe. Behold our enemy, take note of how she presents herself, what she says, what she doesn't say.
A cutscene begins as the Queen of Fruma walks onto the stage, as "Presence" begins to play. Sovereign Zhiraok flanks her. The Espren Orchestra move to the side and bow in her presence.
Her Majesty: Ah... beloved people of the Auburn Forest! What a joy, what an honor it is to stand amongst you once again.
Her Majesty: Some will claim the stunning Highlands to be our most beautiful region, with its vibrant blossoming trees and grand historic castles...
Her Majesty: But I've always held a special regard for this place. The leaves and their warm shades, blowing in the soft breeze... all the woes of the world would be worth this sight.
Her Majesty: If I were able, perhaps I could stay here year-round! Ah, but alas... work in the Citadel keeps us all occupied!
Her Majesty: We have many plans for the coming year. Increased imports from the other regions, easier access to travel for all, and additional openings in military positions!
Her Majesty: More will be revealed soon. Now, some words from your beloved Sovereign.
The Queen steps to the side and lets Sovereign Zhiraok take the microphone.
Sovereign Zhiraok: ...ah. The one thing I miscalculated. The mic height. Oh well Testing, testing, one two three...
Sovereign Zhiraok: Welcome one and all! I'm your Sovereign, Zhiraok. It's an honor to be here before you all again today.
Sovereign Zhiraok: Two decades of work in the Auburn Forest. Twenty years. It feels like I've been here for so much longer this place, these people, really have become my home.
Sovereign Zhiraok: My duty is not just to serve the Crown, but also to serve you. To make your lives better, to raise this region we live in to new heights.
Sovereign Zhiraok: Whether that's by increasing production of Liff Leaves to share our resources and knowledge the province over, which we owe to your hard work...
Sovereign Zhiraok: ...or through sharpening our infrastructure to exponentiate your quality of life, in thanks for what you do!

Sovereign Zhiraok: I'd be here all day listing the improvements over the last year, but I'll summarize Multiple major road improvements, countless new job opportunities, multiplying guard patrols to keep you safe...
Sovereign Zhiraok: The place we came from twenty years ago is unrecognizable now. My vow is that twenty years ahead, I can say the same thing for how much more we, together, improve our home.
Sovereign Zhiraok: 'til the day we sum up to the grandeur of Aelumia Citadel Thank you all! Enjoy the festivities!
Zhiraok lets the Queen take the microphone back.
Her Majesty: What fine work Sovereign Zhiraok has done for our province! Truly, there could have been no better choice to fill that role!
Her Majesty: The Auburn Forest flourishes under his governance, and I could not be more pleased by the progress he has made.
Her Majesty: One final message before we conclude. These past few years, we have seen fewer and fewer reports of the cursed a sign of our strength as a people.
Her Majesty: And it is all thanks to you! Your diligent reporting of suspicious activity makes all the difference in keeping our province safe.
Her Majesty: We must stand strong, together! We will not allow this evil its victory, we will not let our province fall like so many others have beyond our walls!
Her Majesty: With that, let the celebrations begin!
The Queen casts a spell to set off multiple fireworks as the cutscene ends.
Syndra: Hm... The standard, then.
Syndra: Did anything stand out to you?
How she talks about Auburn. It's... different.
Syndra: Indeed, it is. It's quite puzzling, isn't it? It's a sort of reverence she never displays elsewhere.
Syndra: And if there's one thing I'm certain she's being truthful about, it's this. Which only makes it all the stranger.
Zhiraok's speech.
Syndra: Yes, yes... improvements. Life has improved since he ascended to that position. I'll give him that. He's invested in Auburn.
Syndra: But he is still working under the crown. Don't forget that. For every improvement he has made, there's another he has left ignored.
They didn't mention Torann.
Syndra: No, I suppose they wouldn't. Better to leave the public unaware of such failures.
Syndra: But rest assured that internally, they have not forgotten. They will keep searching for you.
The cursed.
Syndra: Yes... the cursed. The crown needs to keep the people afraid. If there's another enemy out there that the crown supposedly protects them from...
Syndra: There's a reason they want people to believe the outside world is destroyed. Any contact could break the illusion.
Syndra: They'll be closing out the festival soon... so, our work here is done. We should be leaving before the crowd thins enough for us to be spotted.
Syndra: I've scheduled a meeting for tomorrow I'd like for you to attend. It'll be about our next steps, now that the crown has moved on. I'll see you there.
The camera then pans to a cutscene showing an event that occured sometime before. The mysterious Sovereign from Queen's Recruit is speaking with Sovereign Zhiraok.
Previously...
???: Sovereign, a word?
Sovereign Zhiraok: I think I've had just about enough of people sneaking into my office. Care to knock next time?
???: Mmn. It's more interesting this way. I have news from the capital your request for additional troops has been granted. Reassignments should come through by the end of the week.
Sovereign Zhiraok: Well, that'll solve some problems. But that's not the whole message, is it? What obtuse remark has he got for me this time?
???: Merely a reminder to... "get your act together," as it were.
Sovereign Zhiraok: Get my act toge That floundering fractal's developed less in his quadrant in a hundred-fifty years than I've done in two, in the last ten!
Sovereign Zhiraok: I Ugh, focus, Z... He's not even here, don't let him get under your skin...
Sovereign Zhiraok: I'll get off that tangent. If that was all you had to say, it'd be a waste of your time. What do you need to say that a courier can't send in a letter?
???: The intruder. Does your administration believe it can get the situation under control?
Sovereign Zhiraok: There it is. Listen, I've got their number, alright? There's no way in or out of the district where they won't be detected. We'll track them down.

Sovereign Zhiraok: Though unlike some people, my ego isn't so massive I can't recognize when an ally can be of use. Your types have an expertise here, so if you could spare a set or two of eyes it'd be much appreciated.
???: I'll see what I can do. There happens to be an ongoing operation in the area already, we can discuss redirecting the agent once it's concluded.
???: One last thing the identity of the intruder has been made clear to you already, yes?
Sovereign Zhiraok: Mhm. Like I said, I've got their number.
???: Then you will understand Her Majesty's order not to speak of this ordeal to our newest. Ascension is a difficult process, and it would be... unwise to add additional distractions to it.
Sovereign Zhiraok: Wouldn't want to distract a hard worker like him, right. But if that's everything, Spymaster? My to-do list is getting more added by the minute.

The order you move the blocks doesn't matter
Push Block b to the left (if you face to the closed door)
Push block a to the left, and then forwards
Push block a forwards -> right.
Push block b left -> forwards -> right.
Push block c left -> forwards -> right.
Push block a (or the block closest to the right edge) backwards -> left -> backwards
Push block a backwards -> right -> forwards -> left -> forwards -> left.
Push block b left -> backwards -> right -> backwards -> right -> forward -> left.
Push block c backwards -> left.

hints: The Fable
Chapter I
Over 1000 years ago, before the great dismantling of the Ahms region, a mighty beast roamed the land.
It was not only a beast of immense power, but also great wisdom. Many would come from far and wide to seek its counsel.
However, after a cataclysmic event, the region shattered, and left the beast lost all hope in villager kind.
For it was the desire of riches that shock the land, and the beast could not tolerate it any longer.
The beast departed the fractured region, leaving the people with all the riches in the world, but no land to enjoy it with.
He departed this land leaving only this advice: Should the greed of this land be in reprimand, seek me out. The seeds of enlightenment should be sewn at the canyon ridge.
Although the location of the "Ridge" has been supposedly found, no such seed has ever grown there.
Leading us to believe that the Ahms region has always been fractured, and that this is just a tale passed down to explain what cannot be explained.
Should you ever want to waste your seeds, the location is [630,147,-4590]
End Of Chapter I.

stages.title: Stage 2
stages.task: Bring [1 Twain Journal] to Twendle
hints: Enter the house, walk into the dining room on the right and then to the servant's area right by the table. Press the wooden button on the wall at [123, 75, -367] to open the iron trapdoor at [128, 74, -358]. Quickly jump down the hole opened under the trapdoor to reach the cellar.

In the cellar, place items on 2 wooden pressure plates behind the barrels, at [129, 63, -345] and [115, 63, -376], to access the secret room through the doorway at [105, 63, -360]. Inside the secret room, there is a sign saying "Pay tribute to the eyes of the beast, it shall guide you".
Exit the secret room and return to the entrance of the mansion.
For the next part of the puzzle, you will first need to get a Ghostly Cap. To do this you must find three ghosts in the mansion (prepare for jumpscares with each one):
The first is on the third floor, across from the stairs you go up to get to this floor, at [120, 84, -392].
The second is at the end of the hall on the third floor, in the last room, at [118, 84, -332].

The third is in the front left "garden" area of the mansion, at [97, 77, -378]. To get there, you have to go up the main stairs and then walk down the hall to the left, and go through the door behind the stairs that lead to the third floor.

Once you have all three items, take them to the cauldron room on the third floor and drop the three items in the hopper in the middle of the room, at [128, 86, -358]. A skeleton will then appear and drop an unidentified Ghostly Cap.
Identify the Ghostly Cap right outside the mansion to wear it for the next section.

In the dining room, the carpets near the fireplace resemble the face of a wither skeleton, with the two eyes marked by dark red particles. As the sign from earlier suggests, insert emeralds (by right-clicking) into both eyes to open the secret room behind the fireplace.

Once in the secret room, walk to the back and into the painting at [112, 75, -295]. The sign says "Give the riches you hold to the man whos house he once owned, and it will open a grave that does not belong".

As the sign suggests, click with an emerald on the soul sand at the grave in the room. Then, quickly run out of the mansion and turn to the left to the small graveyard in front of the mansion (not the large one in the back). The quartz grave (the one that does not belong) at [66, 71, -314] should be open. You must be wearing the ghostly helmet at this point in order to enter the small graveyard.
Jump into the hole at the quartz grave and follow the cave down.

At the end of the cave you will reach a room labelled "The Prison Of Souls". A sign near the exit of the room states "The obsessions of the souls are the keys to freedom. -Mael". You must find the code to exit the room based on the number of decorative block items in each cell.
Cell 1 "Retenal" has 5 glowstone lamps, cell 2 "Gitsag" has 7 leaves, cell 3 "Nnebrian" has 3 ender chests, and cell 4 "Kal-el" has 2 emerald ores. Put in order, the code is thus 5732.
Once you enter the code, a door opens and you can fight the Phantom Twain to obtain the journal. Step on the quartz block in the back to leave the cave.
▸ Tips
If you are doing the quest with someone else, you will likely have to spawn each Ghostly boss twice so each of you can get a Ghostly Cap.
The boss isn't too difficult if you come prepared, but it can sometimes catch you off guard with its vanish and pull spells, so be careful.
If you've already completed this quest previously as another character, then you skip gathering the ingredients to get the Ghostly Cap by simply reusing your old one.

▸ Magical Materials

Magical Materials
Chapter 1 - A Primer
Artifice is, to simplify, the art of creating magical materials. This book will teach you about various magical materials and methods of crafting your own artifacts.
Magical artifacts are nearly as common as pebbles on the roadside, even moreso in Gavel. Often referred to as Relics, these items were made independently of each other...
...but tend to follow a similar structure. Magic can only be focused in certain ways, after all. Many reliquary items are outdated by today's standards, though theorists are baffled by...
...the presence of such relics in Wynn. Magically-gifted individuals were not present for hundreds of years after the deaths of the Twains.
Some surmise that other entities than humans are responsible for their creation, which is supported by the presence of large amounts of artifacts in the Time Valley and Almuj regions.
A good place to start with crafting is in the humble necklace, and for that you would need string and magical materials. Even the string is relevant to the magical crafting process, however.
Derived from processed crops, ones such as Barely, Rye, or native Wynnic crops are less effective than Gavellian crops such as Hemp.
In particular, the feathery structure of Sorghum, also known as Avo leaf, is very conducive towards the channeling of magical energy.
An exception to this rule is with the recently dubbed "Decay Root" derived from Gavellian plants sapped of their magical energy. Decay Root absorbs magic and can leave sources completely drained.
Chapter 2 - Magical Foci
Most magic items require a "focus" in order to draw out and direct their magical energies. Many items are usable as foci, but certain items have been found to be far more effective than others.
Jewels and precious stones are easy to channel magic through, and thus are often used in conjunction as basic foci. Certain gems have inclination towards specific elements...
...most often indicated by the color of the gem, but all are applicable for general purposes.
A less common type of focus is found in the form of Runes. They are a magical unknown, for all intents and purposes, with each specific rune seeming to have a different magical inclination.
Only five types of Runes have ever been found, and after a disastrous attempt at combining Runic power, horrifically powerful Rune Guardians have begun to appear in Gavel to guard them.
Due to this, the remaining stockpile of Runes continues to dwindle as they are used and sold between their holders, or hoarded by the wealthy.
Chapter 3 - Quartz
Quartz is a versatile magical material useful in nearly any magical item in some fashion.
Due to its natural ability to passively absorb magical energy, it is a phenominally [sic] applicable material for magical batteries or storage.
Magical marvels such as the electromagic generator in Llevigar are powered primarily by quartz and related materials.
However, it has its limits. While it is effective at storing energy, it can only store a finite amount.
Overloading quartz with magical energy can cause it to create magical discharge, which can overcharge nearby quartz as well, causing violent chain reactions.
Chapter 4 - Stabilizers
Magical stabilizers do as they state, stabilize magical energy. Though materials such as quartz and runes are useful, misuse can result in disaster for the user.
Thus, stabilizers are a necessity for creating safe-to-use magical items. In the past, these manifested as massive chains of quartz batteries or wasteful use of metals such as gold or silver.
Recently however, a material called Lodestone was discovered. It actively stabilizes influxes of magical energy far more efficiently than jewels or precious metals.
However, it has the side effect of leaching excess magic into the environment into a raw form. It is theorized that the presence of Lodestone in Gavel has...
...contributed heavily to the diverse flora and fauna of the region; the magic energy influenced evolution in ways that areas like Wynn have not seen.
Chapter 5 - Elemental Powders
Powders, while simple in actual structure, are often misunderstood except by enchanters and artificers.

Being made of specific blends of various items with magical ties to elements, certain powders are easier to create than others. Magical plants are easier to grind down than magical minerals, for instance.
After each item is ground to dust, enchanters purify the blend to remove extraneous aspects, leaving only the pure elemental powder in its wake.
Items more heavily attuned to a specific element will create a stronger blend of powder, but even items with the slightest connection to an element can conceivably be used to create a powder.
To apply powders to items in a refined way, one must either incorporate the mix into the base construction of an item, or utilize the energies within for an enchantment.
Merely sprinkling powders over other things will not generate any magical effects, although some artists are known to use powders to make brilliant colors of paint, strangely.
Chapter 6 - Cosmic Unknowns
Cosmic Magic is being studied presently by magical experts. There are few conclusive truths of cosmic energies, one such being that it is only found in things fallen from the sky.
The meteors and comets that have fallen are difficult to study, as not only does each color or type of fallen meteor appear to have different magical effects on its environment...
...but many types of meteor have been found to induce a creeping insanity in those exposed to it for extended periods. Three initial cosmic researchers fell prey to this effect.

Small samples and meteor shards appear generally safe, but are to be treated with the utmost care and caution. Gavellian law outlaws non-registered usage of cosmic materials.|Magical Materials library|60|Spoiler alert: The hidden text contains the text from the}}

Mora: ... Oh, Rex... what happened?
Rex: You know what happened, Mora. I- I messed up. Again.
Yuman: Huh? What do you mean, agai-
Mora: Ah, Yuman, would you mind taking Yusanu along with you to go tell the others we'll be a little late to the meeting? I believe there will be some additional news today.
Yuman: Uh... sure, I guess. Yus, can you tell me what's up while we walk?
Yusanu: ...yeah, sure, Yuman.
Yuman and Yusanu exit the forge.
Mora: ...well, how bad it it?
Rex: It's... bad. We stole something important from the Sovereign's workshop. It's... a long story. Yusanu should tell his part of it. But...
Mora: I see. I apologize, Rex, I should have been more attentive.
Rex: No! No, it's not your fault, I should have- I should have known I was being impulsive, I... I wasn't thinking straight.
What are we talking about?
Mora: Ah. Of course, you don't know. I should have informed you the last time this happened...
Mora: Rex has these... ah, "moods," sometimes, wherein she gets... overly excitable and impulsive. Many a time have they led her into trouble.
Rex: Ugh, I should know better by now! Especially here, especially now, when...
Mora: Well, what is done is done, and nevertheless, we must press on. Let's join the others for the meeting. Syndra has something important to tell us.
Rex and Mora head into the meeting room.
names: » Return to the Steel Feather through Yu

stages.title: Stage 18
stages.task: Attend the meeting in the Steel Feather at [-2085, 6, -695].
hints: All of the resistance members are around the table.
Syndra: There you are! Mora, Rex, what's going-
Quill: Syndra, I believe that can wait. We've, ah, held up dinner long enough, I believe. If everyone is here, we should begin. First- Yusanu, what was it you had to tell us?
Yusanu looks at everyone around the room.
Yusanu: ...sigh. Before I begin, I need to make it clear- I was doing what I thought was best for the Steel Feather.
Yuman: Yeah, man, good start... really instills confidence.
Yusanu: Yuman, please... let me get through this. Don't interrupt.
Yusanu: So. So, so,so... The... the reason the crown has left us alone down here is because I have been working with Sovereign Soosu.
Everyone jumps in shock, except for Syndra and Quill.
Yulie: You WHAT?!
Rex: Hey! Let him speak.
Yusanu: The reason we've been able to stay under the radar for so long is because of this, Yulie.
Yusanu: The reason we can live here, leave our home, make use of the city's electricity... it's because of my collaboration.
Yusanu: She said she saw potential in me. Told me that if I helped her in her workshops, then... then you all would be safe down here.
Yusanu: I didn't tell anybody because I knew you wouldn't get it. You'd think it was stupid, and risky, and a bad idea. Working with... with someone responsible for our problems.
Yusanu: And I knew it was risky. I did. But I thought that if I were to mess up, only I would be punished. You all would be safe.
Quill: ...now. I understand emotions are running high right now. I would ask everyone to take a step back, think through it logically, and remain c-
Yulie: Are you insane, Yusanu?! Of all the secrets you could have been keeping-
Yuman: Hey, bro, leave him alone.
Yulie: No, I don't think I will! Is that what the alarms were about? How long has this been going on? What was running through your head when you decided-
Yuman: As if you haven't been doing the same thing this whole time! Trying to put all the weight on your own shoulders, not getting help from anyone else!!
Yuman: So- so, y'know, I'm a little mad. He should have talked to us about it! But... he's telling us now. He's asking for help now.
Yulie: ...
Rex: Unfortunately, it gets worse.
Yulie: How?!
Yusanu: After yesterday's run-in with the soldiers... Soosu is demanding I hand over whoever's responsible. I... I can't do that.
Yusanu: Rex and Player caught me talking to her today. That's why... that's why I'm telling you.
Rex: ...yeah. I convinced him to stop working with her, and to tell you all about it.
Rex: We also... stole an important gadget she and Yusanu were working on. Something the Queen was very invested in.
Yusanu: I don't know what it is or what it does. I don't know what it's for. All I know is that the Queen needs it finished. It's all she's had Soosu working on for... months.
Yusanu: I'll try to figure out what it is in my spare time. Maybe it'll help us! I... hope it will.
Yusanu: Yulie, Yuman... I owe you a better apology. I can talk to you in private later, but... right now, we should continue with the meeting.
Yulie punches Yusanu out of his chair.
Yusanu: Ow... yeah, I deserved that.
Syndra: ...that was certainly a lot. Fortunately, angering the Sovereign may not ultimately matter. If all goes according to plan... the crown will fall at the end of the festival.
Syndra: My goal, as always, has been to find a way to destroy the crown's influence and to free our province. I believe this upcoming festival is an opportunity to do just that.
Syndra gets up on the middle of the table.
Syndra: During the Crown Festival, Her Majesty will die.
Mora: Wha- now?
Sui: What are you-
Quill: ...
Zeph: W-wh-wh-WHAT?!
Yusanu: First the Sovereign, and now-?
Rex: Right after we?!
Yuman: What the hell, man?!
Quill: Settle down, everyone, settle down! Please, allow Syndra to continue.
Syndra: It will not be easy. But if we strike when her guard is down, and catch her by surprise, I believe it is possible.
Syndra: I'll be splitting you all into several groups, and will assign tasks that must be completed before the festival.
Syndra: The decision Quill and I have come to is that I alone will be going for the kill. That way, if anything goes wrong... no one else faces the consequences.
Syndra: I'll go over the details tomorrow. I think... we've had enough excitement today. Please, hold your complaints until then, as well.
Quill: Ahem. Yes, indeed. I suppose we should be getting to dinner, as well.
Quill: Yuman... this may be unfair of me to ask, but would you be willing to play us a song tonight? We will not have many days left together.
Yuman: Yeah... yeah, man, of course. I can do that.
Quill: Then let us enjoy the remainder of our company!
The camera fades to black, then fades in with everyone gone from the meeting room.
names: » Attend the meeting in the Steel Feathe

stages.title: Stage 19
stages.task: Watch Yuman's performance at [-2100, 6, -715].
hints: All of the regular members of the Steel Feather, the Leaves in the Wind, and Jiro are in front of the stage. Interacting with anyone will cause the cutscene to begin
Yuman jumps onto the stage with his guitar.
Yuman: Hey, everyone! Man, uh... small crowd today, huh?
Yuman: Oh, man, is that Jiro I see? Hey, man! I didn't, uh... expect to see ya.
Jiro: Huh? Why not?
Yuman: Uh, just, you didn't seem super happy with me after... after yesterday. With the- soldier thing.
Jiro: ... Oh! Yeah. No worries. Water under the bridge.
Yuman: If... if you say so! Don't think you've heard this one before, so tell me how you like it!
Yuman: But first... Yus. Yusanu. Look, I... I'm not one to hold grudges. So I don't need any more apologies from you! I get it.
Yuman: I just... want you to trust us more, 'kay? You and Yulie both, haha! 'Cause... I want to help!
Yuman: I had a think, and yeah. It sucks you didn't tell us. But your deal with Soosu- it saved us! Gave us a home, gave us a future!
Yuman: So... this song's dedicated to you. Hope you like it.
Yusanu begins to play the song. Shortly after, the camera fades to black and perspective shifts to Soosu in her workshop.
Sovereign Soosu: No... no no no no no, where is it, where IS IT?! I can't... I need to find it, I-
The Queen enters the room.
Her Majesty: Not a good look, Sovereign.
Soosu turns around.
Sovereign Soosu: EEP! Y- your Majesty, I- I- I wasn't expecting you until... tomorrow. Wh- what're you doing here?
The Queen is facing away from Soosu, looking at some stuff on a shelf.
Her Majesty: My schedule freed up, so I decided to check in early. Is something wrong, Sovereign?
Sovereign Soosu: Um... I-
Her Majesty: Don't bother. How incompetent must you be, to have lost it from your own workshop?!
Sovereign Soosu: I- I- I don't understand how, my golems haven't been disturbed! They didn't detect anything!
Her Majesty: Perhaps if you focused more on efficiency instead of playing around with your toys, this could have been prevented.
The Queen turns to face Soosu.
Sovereign Soosu: I'll- I'll fix this, I promise! I promise I promise I promise, I can fix it! I can... I can restart! I still have all the research notes, and I-
Her Majesty: Enough. I have been lenient with your performance maintaining your district, because I had faith there would be results.
Her Majesty: Restarting the Resonance Weaver project... it cannot be done. That artifact I entrusted you with... that magic is a lost art. It cannot be replicated.
Sovereign Soosu: N- no, I have the notes, I- I know how it works, I can do it, just- just give me a chance! I can fix this!
Her Majesty: I must prepare for the festival. I will expect your presence there, as usual. Please... clean yourself up before that.
The Queen walks away from the shelf.
Her Majesty: Sovereign.
The Queen turns to face Soosu again.
Sovereign Soosu: Y- yes?
Her Majesty: Consider our agreement null. You have failed me. You will continue your service as Sovereign indefinitely... with your blessing intact.
The Queen turns around and leaves the workshop.
Sovereign Soosu: ...what? No- no, no no no, you- you can't, you can't, you can't!!!!
Soosu raises her hands.
Sovereign Soosu: AHHHHHHHHHH!!!!!!!!
Soosu claps and destroys the interior of the room, then sits down. The camera fades to black and the perspective returns to the player.

Tell me about being a recruit.
Secretary: Recruits are separated by their divisions, their uniform colours reflect this.
Secretary: Those with red uniforms are from Auburn, cyan uniforms are from the Industrial district, white uniforms are in the Wings division...
Secretary: Green uniforms are in the Mistwoods division, they are recruits selected from other regions based on a test that decides if they are suited for the dangerous conditions in the Mistwoods...
Secretary: Since you are in the Highlands division, your group leader is Recruiter Effal.
Tell me about Fort Tericen.
Secretary: Fort Tericen is the largest and most prestigious military training camp in Fruma, headed by the equally prestigious Commander Ferreo.
Secretary: Many of the most famous soldiers of Fruma have originated from here, you should be proud to be a part of our program!
Tell me about the Fruman military.
Secretary: Most recruits already know this before coming to Fort Tericen... I suppose there is no shame in asking if you don't know.
Secretary: The Fruman military is composed of nine divisions, being seven regional divisions, the Constable division, and the Wings division.

Secretary: Yes, you heard that right, seven regional divisions not six. The seventh being the Xima division which recruits soldiers directly from the Auburn division, which is why most people lump them together.

Secretary: The Constable division has an authority level higher than all the regional divisions, and the Wings division has authority over both of them. Be careful not to step on their toes when you become a soldier!

Secretary: Within each division is a ranking system used to separate leadership roles. In ascending order of authority; there are soldiers, captains, commanders, and finally a single general that manages the commanders.
Secretary: The Wings division has some additional positions within it, like the Gendarmes. They're a group of Wings soldiers that only operate within Aelumia.
What will happen after I complete my training here?
Secretary: Don't worry, this question is more common than you'd think.
Secretary: In about a month, if everything goes to plan, you and the rest of the recruits will attend a ceremony and officially become Fruman soldiers!
Secretary: From there, you'll work in a group with other Highlands soldiers. If you are able to impress your superiors, you can be promoted to captain or even commander!
Secretary: Another thing that can happen if you demonstrate exception abilities is promotion to the Constable division or maybe even the Wings division!
Secretary: There truly is fame and glory waiting ahead of you. If you are able to prove yourself.
No, I don't have any questions.
Secretary: Alright, good luck on your training!
Talking to the Military Guard in the entry room:
Military Guard: Speak with the secretary if you're lost.
Talking to the Military Guard or trying to walk through the door on the south side of the next room:
Military Guard: You may not enter yet, talk to the commander and then enter the stage room across from us.
Talking to the Military Guard or trying to walk through the door on the west side of the next room:
Military Guard: You may not enter yet, talk to Commander Ferreo.
Talking to the Military Guard or trying to walk through the door on the north side of the next room:
Military Guard: I can't let you enter until you talk to Commander Ferreo.
Talking to Commander Ferreo and the Military Recruiter:
Commander Ferreo: You have you brought me Effal, this is not Perin.
Effal begins to sweat.
Recruiter Effal: You will have to excuse me Commander, but I did not deem Perin as fit to be a recruit.
Recruiter Effal: The boy had done no training, he would not have lasted a day here!
Recruiter Effal: I told him this myself, and while I was reprimanding him... Erm...
Recruiter Effal: ... Had overheard our conversation and begged that I take them instead.
Recruiter Effal: Seeing that they looked more suitable than Perin, and hearing their reasoning as to why they should be a recruit, I decided to adhere to their request.
Commander Ferreo: So you deliberately acted against the directions given to you?
Recruiter Effal: Well... Yes... I-I truly apologize for violating the orders given to me...
Commander Ferreo: Do not go against what you are told to do again.
Commander Ferreo: Nevertheless, if what you say about Perin is true, perhaps it is for the best that he does not become a recruit.
Commander Ferreo: Welcome to Fort Tericen, recruit. Enter the room to the right so that we may begin the opening speech.
Recruiter Effal: Thank you Commander! Now, let me lead you to the stage!

stages.title: Stage 5
stages.task: Listen to the speech from Sovereign Majin.
hints: Talking to the Secretary:
Secretary: Shouldn't you be listening to a speech right now?
Talking to the Military Guard or trying to walk through the door on the south side of the room:
Military Guard: You may not enter yet, enter the stage room across from us.
Talking to the Military Guard or trying to walk through the door on the west side of the room:
Military Guard: You may only enter after Sovereign Majin's speech.
Talking to the Military Guard on the north side of the room:
Military Guard: There's no time for chit-chat, the speech is about to start!
Shortly after the player enters the stage room, Commander Ferreo joins Sovereign Majin on the stage.
Commander Ferreo: The speech may now begin.
Sovereign Majin: Welcome recruits, to the start of your training in becoming a Fruman soldier.
Sovereign Majin: You have all been carefully chosen by a group of experienced recruiters.
Majin walks to the right side of the stage.
Sovereign Majin: They have closely reviewed your performances in physical tests of strength and agility since you were children, and have decided that you belong here.
Sovereign Majin: Do not prove to me that they were wrong.
Sovereign Majin: Use the opportunities given to you to show us that you deserve to be amongst your superiors.
Sovereign Majin: Your instructors will expect the best from you, so you must show them the best. Those who refuse or are unable to do this have no place here.
Sovereign Majin: Your role will be the most important in Fruma. Ensuring the safety of the population is no small task, trust me.
Majin walks back to the center of the stage.
Sovereign Majin: So, like I have, each of you must prove yourself worthy of being called a soldier of Fruma.
Sovereign Majin: Let my words serve as motivation for you during your training.
All of the recruits give applause. Majin departs from the stage.
Robin: Wow...
Saldin: Amazing!
Wilton: What an incredible speech!
Everyone stops clapping.
Commander Ferreo: We are thankful to Sovereign Majin for taking time out of his responsibilities to deliver the opening speech.
Commander Ferreo: Now we will be bringing you to your first training session of the day, I hope you all are ready.
Commander Ferreo: Each of you will be separated into groups depending on your division. For each challenge, your group will be paired with another group.
Commander Ferreo: The leaders of each region grouping will be the recruiter who originally sent you the invitation letter.
Commander Ferreo: They will be the ones leading you to where you're supposed to be for the first couple of days here, following an assigned schedule.
Commander Ferreo: You are expected to be at your designated area, on time and ready.
Commander Ferreo: However, if for whatever reason you get lost, go to the secretary at the main lobby desk and she will tell you where to go.
Commander Ferreo: Now, go convene with your recruiters in the main room to your left, then they will take you to your first training session.
Ferreo and the recruits leave the stage room. Arnol walks over to the player.
Arnol: That was a pretty good speech, I was a bit nervous, but now I am ready to start the training!
Arnol: I'm Arnol, I come from the nobel Highlands Tasa family, Fruma has done so much for us, so I am ready to help her.
Arnol: I'm glad that you're from the Highlands. That means we're in the same group!
Arnol: How about you and I stick together during our training?
Arnol: My family tells me that recruits often end up very... competitive...
Arnol: So I think we can both benefit from sticking together, and watching each others' backs.
Arnol: Anyways, we should head to our group's leader, I think his name is Effal?
Arnol walks out of the stage room.

stages.title: Stage 6
stages.task: Talk to Recruiter Effal then head to the challenge room at [-10247, 112, 5288].

200x150px|thumb|The Roughworks group.

Talking to the Secretary:
Secretary: Hey there recruit! Need help with anything?
Where should I be right now?

Secretary: From there, head into the challenge room your team leader told you about.

(For the secretary's other dialogue options, see § Stage 4.)
Talking to the Military Guard on the north side of the room:
Military Guard: Good luck with your training, recruit. But I'll warn you, Commander Ferreo is no pushover.
Talking to Recruiter Alena:
Recruiter Alena: Do you need help with something recruit? Your team leader is Recruiter Effal, go see him for instructions.

Robyn: Definitely not going to happen. After hearing that speech from Sovereign Majin, I feel like I could take on the entire resistance!

Verdi: Are you nervous like me? We're about to start the training and I still don't feel ready.

Talking to Arnol:

Talking to Priscilla:

Talking to Dogi:

Talking to Wilton:
Wilton: Excuse me, Ezero sir, is it true the soldiers around here call Commander Ferreo 'The Iron Commander'?
Recruiter Ezero: I believe he used to go by that nickname in his younger years, he was quite the fearsome leader.
Recruiter Ezero: You should be careful not to get on his bad side... The last guy that did got exiled to Wynn...

Recruiter Ezero: Heh, I'm just messing with oyu kid, you don't have to worry about him, he's softened up a lot over the years.
Talking to Recruiter Riva:

Recruiter Riva: Shouldn't be too hard to do, I'd think.

Katze: I'm ready! Let's show everyone we're the best!

Trying to enter the cafeteria or the room to the west:

After walking through the Shield Challenge door:
Military Instructor: Welcome recruits to the shield challenge.
Military Instructor: Defense is one of the most important aspects of combat. You should not expect yourself to be able to dodge every incoming attack.
Military Instructor: A shield can be an incredibly useful tool for a soldier, but holding them up constantly can often interfere with your mobility.
Military Instructor: Knowing when to hold up your shield to defend yourself against incoming arrows or attackers, is thus, a vital skill to learn.
Military Instructor: Your training today will revolve around holding up a shield against arrows that are being fired from turrets.
Military Instructor: The turrets will give an indication of when they are about to fire, however, the shields provided to you have many weights embedded into them.
Military Instructor: Most of you will only be able to hold your shield up for a second or two at a time, so you must do so wisely.
Military Instructor: I have set up a turret here that you can use to practice getting used to handling the weighted shield.
Military Instructor: Simply stand where I am now, then click the button behind me. Face the turret and hold up your shield when, or just before, it fires an arrow.
Military Instructor: Good luck recruits, I will be judging you from an overlook point. If you haven't already, take a shield from the shield rack next to Recruiter Effal.
Military Instructor: When you're ready to start the challenge, enter the large door behind me.
The instructor and most of the recruits head into the challenge area.

+1 [Heavy Shield

Military Instructor: It's your turn , stand on that plate to start the test.

I had trouble with it at first, but was able to succeed in the end.
Arnol: Good job ! I am glad that you managed to finish. We should talk more about it later.
The dialogue branches combine here.
How were you unable to block any of the arrows?
Arnol: Well, maybe you just had more strength training than me. The shield was just too heavy to hold up, I don't know what else to say.
The dialogue branches combine here.
Arnol: We should go to our next challenge now, let's hope Effal doesn't erupt at us for being late.
Arnol walks into the Endurance Training room:

You should not leave this area yet.

Military Instructor: The terrain you battle on will never be optimal, so you must be able to adapt to it to ensure your success.

Military Instructor: If you fall, you will have to go back to the start and continue from there.
Military Instructor: We have installed jump pads on the platforms to help ease you into making riskier leaps.
Military Instructor: To use the jump pads, simply stand on them and jump. The mechanism will detect the sudden weight loss and boost you.
Military Instructor: I've installed a jump pad in this room to the right of me if any of you want to practice before starting the course.
Military Instructor: Soon you'll all hopefully be able to complete a course similar to this one but without the crutch.
Military Instructor: You may enter the large door behind me to begin. Oh, and your performance will be judged on how quickly you reach the exit.
The instructor and most of the recruits head into the challenge room:

Arnol: I'm going to take my time on the jumps. After what happened in the first challenge, there's no point in rushing through.
Arnol: Alright, I think I'm ready, let's sit together in the cafeteria after this.
Arnol heads into the challenge room:
Talking to Recruiter Effal:

Recruiter Strumon: The rest is up to you, think carefully about how you want to approach this.
Talking to Adder:

Walk through the door on the west side of the room to enter the challenge.
Military Instructor: You're up , good luck!
If the nickname the Player uses is "Leap" or "Cursed", then the endurance challenge will have smaller platforms and more difficult jumps.

After entering the challenge room, the Mistwoods division recruiter and recruits enter behind the player.
Commander Ferreo: Your final challenge today will be singular combat against another recruit.
Commander Ferreo: When up against the enemy, you may find yourself in a similar situation. You must be prepared for when this happens.
Commander Ferreo: This test serves as a way to further gauge your skills, as well as an opportunity to show off the strategies you have developed in melee.

Lynn: From the moment I saw him here, I knew he wouldn't be able to last a day.
Lynn: But, if it turns out that he didn't leave, I wouldn't stick with him, if I were you.
Lynn: You don't want his weakness to rub off on you.

Commander Ferreo: If you are unable to realize this potential fully, or become more trouble than you're worth, I won't hesitate to have you kicked out.

Kerry: It's just something to keep us engaged, to make sure everyone is doing their best in the training I think.
Talking to Kyren or Dogi:
Kyren: You lied to me... Don't ever think about talking to me again until you get at least 3rd place in the rankings!
Dogi: I'm sorry! I was just too embarrassed to tell you the truth!
Dogi: I-I can make up for this! Please! I don't want to be alone here!
Talking to Katze:
Katze: Are you here to humiliate me further? Go ahead, laugh, I don't care!
Katze: I'll make you and everyone else who mocked me east their words!
Katze: I'll become stronger, stronger than all of you! I-I just need more time.
Talking to Petur:
Petur: ...?
Talking to Arnol:
Arnol: I want to apologize to you . Earlier today, when I told you my reason for wanting to become a soldier, I lied.

Arnol: He pulled some strings, and here I am, becoming a soldier in order to bring more respect to house Tasa.

Arnol: If word went around that a member of house Tasa was forced to clean the guard barracks as a punishment...
Arnol: Well... Everything my father has done for me could be wasted, and I would be an even bigger failure than before...
Arnol: That's all I wanted to tell you. I hope you can understand why I lied to you, I just didn't know if I could trust you with this, but now I do.

Reading Diary Note 1:
Today I will start my training to become a recruit at Fort Tericen. It's hard to believe after all this time, my dreams are finally coming true!
Soon, recruiter Rosei will come to my house and escort me to the barracks. I am shaking with excitement and nervousness even while writing this.
I hope I can appear presentable when I meet Commander Ferreo.
There is a strange message at the bottom of the page.
Reading Diary Note 2:
My first day at Tericen went amazingly well! I didn't stutter when introducing myself to the Commander, did great in the training exercises, and was able to befriend a fellow Highlands recruit!
Her name is Darea, and we ate lunch together. I spent most of that time talking to her about Commander Ferreo. She seemed somewhat freaked out with how much I knew about him.
Tomorrow we will have dueling and shield training. The instructor for dueling training will be Commander Ferreo himself!
Oh dear Queen... Please give me the courage to ask him how he managed to reach that level...
Reading Diary Note 3:

I still couldn't do it... I can't just ask him a question like that outright, I need to show that I am "worthy" first. I've done well in the challenges but I still can't make it into the top three on the ranking.
Those Wings recruits are just too good, compared to the rest of us. It sometimes scares me how strong they are. If I want any chance of reaching that level, I need to start taking risks.
With that credit behind me, I may finally get the courage to ask Commander Ferreo about his biggest secret.
How a vagabond was able to become one of the most famed military commanders, and even receive an incredibly powerful blessing.
There is a strange message at the bottom of the page.
Reading Diary Note 6:
Tomorrow I graduate from Fort Tericen and become a soldier. The days seem so similar to me, I've been forgetting to write these diary entries.
In the past I may have been considered for promotion to captain, now, all of that has slipped away. My rankings have been steadily decreasing over the days, becoming lower than ever before.
I spend most of my time thinking about what could have been, it feels like I am detached from reality.
Yet, even still, the thought manages to appear in my head. Was Commander Ferreo right?
There is a strange message at the bottom of the page.
Reading the Discarded Letter:
Dear Sovereign Majin, it has been a while since I last wrote to you, or spoken to you, face to face. Coincidentally, I am writing this letter about the last conversation we had.

I has asked you about potentially becoming a field Commander again. You were hesitant to grant my request, given my age, but would reconsider it if I showed my value as head of the recruitment program.
I have heard troubling rumours coming from outside the Highlands, namely of the growing strength of a hidden resistance group in the Mistwoods.
As a Wings commander, it is my duty to defend Fruma with my life. I believe I can be of far greater use out there rather than in-
The letter ends there.

Head into the door to the west to enter the challenge. Day 2's version of the challenge is slightly harder, since there are many platforms that do not have jump pads, and the required jumps are more difficult.

hints: Recruiter Effal's dialogue changes depending on the player's performance.
If you did well:
Recruiter Effal: Not a bad time you had there. Keep this up and you might end up making me no longer regret letting you in here.
Recruiter Effal: Up next is shield training, you're still not out of the woods yet. We are expecting big things from you.
If you did poorly:
Recruiter Effal: Well... That was a disappointment. You've been given many second chances and this is what you do to give thanks>
Recruiter Effal: If your mediocrity persists, I'll have no choice but to let you go, for both of our sake's. Now follow me to the next training room.

Talking to Arnol:
Arnol: Hey , I think the challenge went well. I managed to complete it at least, although I can't say for certain if I made a good time.
Arnol: I couldn't help but feel off about what the instructor said when I started the course... "Good luck Arnol... Not that it would matter...".
Arnol: What is that supposed to mean? I thought instructors were supposed to encourage us, helping us to do better in the training.
Arnol: I'm beginning to think that this training program is more about shaming us rather than preparing us to become soldiers. I wonder if the other recruits are starting to believe this as well...
Enter the Shield Challenge room. The Highlands and Industrial District groups are present.
Military Instructor: Welcome recruits to day two of your training in the shield challenge.
Military Instructor: I'll keep the summary short since I'm sure most of you remember the gist of the test from yesterday.
Military Instructor: This time, instead of three turrets shooting at you, the number has been upped to five.
Military Instructor: On top of that, the three central turrets have been elevated. You'll have to aim your shield higher to block arrows coming from them.
Military Instructor: I've also adjusted the turret timings a little. Two turrets are now able to fire at you in quick succession, you must be ready to block the arrows from both of them.
The instructor looks at Arnol.
Military Instructor: I noticed that some of you struggled with lifting the shield on the first day...
Military Instructor: Perhaps those people would like some sort of crutch to help them perform better, but I must say that no such thing will be granted.
Military Instructor: I believe that failure can be an excellent teacher. Some of you may still need to learn that failure should elicit a change from yourself.
Military Instructor: For those recruits, until this lesson is fully learned, continued failure will be far more valuable than success.
Military Instructor: With that being said, I wish all of you lulck on the challenge! Pick up a shield on the rack next to Recruiter Ezero if you haven't.
Military Instructor: Then, once you're ready, enter the large door behind me to start the test. Oh, and the training turret is still here if you need it.
The instructor and most of the recruits enter the challenge area.

Talking to Arnol:
Arnol: That wretch... Looking directly at me while he talks about failure...
Arnol: I'll make him eat those words... Maybe not today, but eventually... I'm done with letting people walk all over me!
Arnol: Thank you for being here to listen to me, , I don't know where I'd be right now without you...
Arnol: After this, we'll meet in the cafeteria, and discuss what you saw last night with Adder.
Talking to Lynn:
Lynn: Heh... It seems like the instructor had a specific person here in mind when he talked about failures!
Lynn: When will Arnol realize he can't keep playing pretend soldier?
Talking to Wilton:
Wilton: Not this again... I think I can already guess how this will go for me...

Knock on the door.

Type and send an answer in chat.

Leave
Niren: You found all of my diary entries, well done.
Niren: It's been so long since I've hid them, I was beginning to forget about them ever existing.
Niren: Don't expect a medal or anything, I can answer some questions that you may have about them though.
Why are you here?
Niren: It was Commander Ferreo's final insult. That's the reason I am here, as a guard in Fort Tericen.
Niren: After I graduated from the recruit program, my average rankings were seen as too low to join a field Captain or Commander's service.
Niren: So Ferreo himself stepped up and took me in, stationing me here to waste away. I think it's some form of punishment...
Why did you hide your diary entries around the barracks?
Niren: I'm not sure to be quite honest. Maybe I was hoping for a sly recruit like yourself to find them, and not make the same mistakes I did.
Niren: It may have just been out of boredom though. I can't remember what thoughts were going through my head back when I hid them, after I became a soldier.
Niren: Deep down... Maybe I wanted Commander Ferreo to find those notes. I wonder what he would have though after reading them...
Did you ever end up discovering Commander Ferreo's secret?

Niren: I had a feeling you'd ask me that. And surprisingly, yes, I did discover the truth about Commander Ferreo's success. There is no secret. He did it all through a fierce determination to become greater.
Niren: When Commander Ferreo was young, he had nothing, he was a vagabond in Hyloch. Not living, just, surviving.
Niren: Sometimes the Fruman Military would come to visit, and everyone in the town gathered together to see them. Ferreo saw how everyone loved and praised them for their valiance.
Niren: He desperately wanted to be praised and loved like that too. So he made it his goal to reach that position, overcoming the countless obstacles in his way.
Niren: Through sheer strength and expertise, he quickly became a Wings Commander, breaking military records in the process.
Niren: There were rumours that he would push further and attempt to become a Sovereign, even though all the positions were full at the time...
Niren: He had finally reached the level of fame and admiration that he had set out for. But I imagine the potential for even greater heights tormented him.
Niren: Not many know this, but just before he was given his current position, Commander Ferreo had a meeting with Sovereign Majin and The Queen.
Niren: We can only speculate at what the discussed, but quickly after said meeting, Majin appointed Commander Ferreo as head of Fort Tericen. My guess is that he was punished for his ambition...
I should be heading back to bed now.
Niren: Good luck on your training recruit. I recommend you take it more seriously than I did.

Niren: Sorry, but I still can't let you enter.
Reading Diary Note 4:
Finally, I've done it! I've managed to rank first in training! The Commander has surely noticed my gradual ascent in strength.

In the back of my mind I'm still unsure about going through with it... But I've put too much effort into this, I can't abandon everything now! I will speak to Commander Ferreo tomorrow, after dueling training.
I'm certain, whatever his answer is, it will have an immense impact on me.

I am crushed... After defeating my opponent in the dueling training. I mustered my courage and asked Commander Ferreo how he went from being at the bottom of the totem pole, to reaching the top of it.
He paused for a second before asking what my business was knowing that.
I fumbled up a response, saying that I've seen him as an inspiration for all of my life, and have always wondered how he managed to claw his way up to the top.
He told me that those who set out to achieve a goal out of envy will never be able to reach it.
No matter how hard I tried, I would never be able to become a commander, nor receive the accolades that he has. Although he may be right... That wasn't what I wanted to hear...
I feel like such an idiot.
There is a strange message at the bottom of the page.

Lunge: Telegraphed by a grunt and angry and blue particles, Adder will lunge forward and charge with his estoc. This attack deals damage twice, once at the start and once at the peak of the lunge. Perfect blocking the last hit will stun him.

Swipe Chain: Telegraphed by angry and green particles, Adder will continuously swipe his estoc in front of him while running towards the Player for several seconds. Perfect blocking the last hit will stun him.

▸ Tips
Arrows fired from turrets that are farther away from you take longer to hit you.
Start blocking when the first arrow is already in the air, so that your shield is still up by the time the last arrow hits you. The timing is tough, but doable.
Increasing your FOV allows you to see all turrets at once on the second day.
Arrows may be easier to track with hitboxes on (F3+B).
The jump pads launch you farther if your eyes are looking perfectly horizontal. Conversely, looking up or down allows you to control how far you are launched.
Some jumps require you to jump into a platform's wall to stop your horizontal momentum, using the jump pad's vertical boost to reach the platform.
Holding your sprint button and forward in the air allows you to gain extra distance. This is especially useful when trying to jump from the ropes to a platform.
If you miss your jump, but land in a part of the room that doesn't send you back to the start, it may be possible to reach a previous platform and continue from there.
Watch Adder carefully for the particle telegraphs before his attacks.

If you are close to Adder when he does his Lunge attack, the last hit can miss you. If you are far away from Adder when he does his Lunge attack, the first hit can miss you. Keep this in mind and adjust your perfect block timing.

Adder may occasionally miss you during his Swipe Chain attack. If you click or keep holding block when he misses you, your block will go on cooldown, even if your timing was perfect, leaving you open to later hits. To prevent this from happening, you can use one of a few strategies:
Walk into him during his swipes, reducing the chance that one of his swipes will miss.
Trap yourself in a corner, guaranteeing that all hits will connect.
Walk backwards and jump right before he hits you, he should knock you back far enough that if your block goes on cooldown, the cooldown expires by the time he reaches you again.

Holding block allows you to block one of Adder's attacks without stunning him, but a non-perfect block causes your block to go on cooldown, leaving you unable to block the next hit of Lunge or Swipe Chain. To block these hits, perfect block the first hit.

If you are in an open space, Adder's Sidestep will send him a good distance away from you, allowing you to recover from block cooldown. If you are in an enclosed space, Adder will land closer to you and can hit you before your block cooldown recovers.
If you named yourself "Cursed", you can skip the duel and still obtain the Iron Medallion, though you will miss out on the Warped Emblem.

stages.title: Stage 19
stages.task: Meet up with Yusanu and Captain Rurie at [-1151, 62, -758].
hints: Talking to Sui again:
Sui: ...
Leaving through Gikyo's office door teleports you outside of Fort Hegea.
After talking to Rurie and Yusanu, Sui walks out of the fort, but doesn't look at them.
Rurie: Hello, dear friends! I see you have returned to us safe and sound!
Yusanu: We found everything we were looking for, and- and more!! Plans, Sui, plans!! Of Deraj prison!!
Rurie: It would seem our dear Changeling Sovereign worked closely with the prison's warden... for what purpose remains unclear, though I imagine something changeling-adjacent?
Yusanu: Sui, with- with these plans, we could... we could stand a chance of breaking everyone out! We could- we could get them all back!
Sui turns to look at Yusanu.
Sui: ...
Yusanu: ...
Yusanu: Sui... where... where are they...?
Sui looks at the ground.
Sui: ...
Yusanu walks up to Sui.
Yusanu: Sui...?
Sui looks back up.
Sui: They're gone, Yusanu! Mora's- Mora's dead.
Yusanu jumps back.
Sui: The Sovereign, they... they killed him.
Yusanu: ...what? What- what about the others...?
Sui: Just... gone. Taken to the Highlands. But, Mora is- he's-
Sui: So. So, I- I'm glad you have hope! For... for getting your people back! Good for you!!
Rurie: Emotions are... certainly running high right now, aren't they! Why don't we, ah, regroup with the rest of the Canopy, and... take some time?
Sui: Take. Some Time? No. No, I'm done taking time. I'm done crying, I'm done worrying! I'm so... so... angry! At the Crown, at myself, at- at Mora!!!!
Sui: At all of you for treating me like I can't handle anything myself!!!
Yusanu: S-Sui, please, I- I understand, but-
Sui: DO YOU?! Do you understand?! Because it SOUNDS like everything's all just fine for you! Your brothers are still alive! You even have a plan to get them back!!
Sui: Rex and Zeph, they... they need me. Need us! And... and I'm not letting anyone else get hurt, or- or- or d-die, not if I can stop it!!
Sui: The Crown... the Sovereigns... the Queen... they'll pay. They'll pay for everything they've done to me, and my- m-my... my family...
Sui: ...
Rurie: And how exactly do you expect to be able to take vengeance in your current state, Sui? I beg of you, please rest before doing something so extreme!
Sui: Every minute I waste is another chance for something to go wrong!!! "Fading with each and every passing moment..."
Sui: If- if only we were there sooner, then- th-then... so- so, no. No, I can't rest! I will be getting my family back!
Yusanu: Sui, we... we can't just storm off into a new district without a plan! The Canopy, they- they can help us! And Soosu's device, I'm so close to a breakthrough, I just need-
Sui: Then stay behind, Yusanu. I... I don't need you, anyway.
Yusanu looks down.
Yusanu: ...what?
Sui: I said, I don't NEED you, Yusanu! What have you even done this whole time we've been in the Mistwoods?! Taken as hostage, tinkering with- with- with that STUPID device!
Sui: YOU haven't had to do any of the work! YOU didn't have to- to run random tasks without explanation! YOU didn't have to- to f-fight and k- k- kill a Sovereign! You... you...
Yusanu: ...
Sui: ...sorry.
Yusanu: Is... is there nothing I can say to convince you not to go?
Sui: ...
Yusanu: Fine. I... I can't follow you, Sui, I can't. I'm going to stay with the Canopy... I'm going to save everyone from Deraj... and I'm going to keep working.
Rurie: ...well, this doesn't have to be goodbye for good, does it? We shall go our separate paths, for a time, then link back together further down the line!
Sui: Yeah... sure. Why not.
Rurie: Hm. If you're set on this path, you'll surely be dealing with the Highlands Sovereign. Ah, Majin of House Thalas... what a delightfully horrible man he is.
You have experience?
Rurie: Experience? Ha! Hahahaha! Yes, I suppose you could say that! Goodness. Experience.
Rurie: A word of warning... he's an easy man to underestimate. All confidence, bluster, so insufferable you could hardly believe there's anything beneath it all!
Rurie: But his self-proclaimed "number one" position amongst the Sovereigns isn't just for show! His confidence, his demeanour... all of it is earned. As much as one may wish otherwise!
Rurie: And there's nothing he loves more than to exert his influence over those beneath him. Which would be, ah... everybody?
Sui: ... If he has my family, then... it doesn't matter. I won't let him get in my way.
Rurie: Ooh, frightening. Well, I've said my piece. The rest shall be up to you!
Rurie: If you ever have need of us again, we'll have set up camp in the cave we first met. You remember the one, yes? Where I-
Yusanu: Sui, I... I'm sorry for Mora. I hope you can... I hope you can save the others. I really do. Please... don't get yourself killed.
Sui: ...I- I'm not planning on it. Bye, Yusanu.

Talking to Barkeep Romu at [-1767, 20, -1261]:
Barkeep Romu: Oho, now that's some dress I've not seen in many a moon! You're one of those Highlands folk, aren't ya? Quite some luxury ya must've lived with.
Barkeep Romu: 's a bit more humble down here in the shadow of the dam. Surprised someone like you would take the trip, but it ain't a complaint. Getting about to see the world is a fine endeavor!

Barkeep Romu: Unfortunately, the bar here's dry. Sure, I got alcohol, but you drink that, and you'll be passing more water than ya took in. Dries you right out, and right now we haven't got any water to spare. Dangerous, y'know?
Barkeep Romu: The dam opens up every month or so to let out some water for us, but is passes through a noble manor, past the hill, rationed out to the rest of the forest.
Barkeep Romu: It's so little though, nowadays. The children are going thirsty. The muck in the riverbeds is more mud than water- so even if ya boil it out like I do, what you get is foul trifles.

Barkeep Romu: Didn't used to be like this, though. Ain't sure what's changed, but I'm just an old geezer. I've lived my life enough- it's what it's doing to the kids that has me worried. ...say, stranger.
Barkeep Romu: If you're touring about here, you'll probably see the manor soon enough. If ya could get them to spare us some more water a while, I'll give ya a discount! How's about it?
Talking to Barkeep Romu again:
Barkeep Romu: Ain't quite sure how you would go about convincing the nobles to let out more water for us, I admit. If I did, I'd take the trek up the hill myself- even in spite of my creaky ol' back.
Barkeep Romu: Even if it's just getting them to put a word in to the Sovereign. I imagine that come-lately Zhiraok would do something about it all. I swear that man doesn't know what sleep is...
Barkeep Romu: I can appreciate a young'un with some spark in their eyes, but he needs to learn to slow down! What's that saying about the brightest candle burning twice as fast?
Talking to Mother Aris at [-1785, 15, -1253]:
Mother Aris: Oh, my! Who are you? In such fantastical equipment! Certainly not a guard- I've never seen anything like it! Oh me, oh my...
Mother Aris: Unless... Are you, perhaps...I have heard whispers on the wind of a new Sovereign? I have seen our Sovereign dress rather differently, so maybe-
Mother Aris: No? You aren't? Hm! Well, be that as it may, I do wish I could welcome you more hospitably, stranger, but we are in the lean time of the month- the leanest I have seen.
Mother Aris: *cough* Oh dear, excuse me. My throat is simply so dry... My children need the water more than I, but I would darn a dozen robes for but a glass now.
Mother Aris: The dam opens every month or so- I assume you wouldn't know, stranger. The water is rationed to us by the nobles in a manor over the hill.
Mother Aris: This time of year is usually dry, but the amount of water we have received lately has been less and less. I wonder what is happening...
Mother Aris: This kind lumberer has been visiting and passing out bottles, and without him I am certain my children wouldn't have made it. I'm unsure how much longer I can keep my family healthy...
Mother Aris: Oh, if only those nobles could spare more for us... Perhaps I could speak with them- but then, who would watch over my children here?
Mother Aris: So...as much as I would like to welcome you with a meal and a hot cup of tea... I simply can't. I am just so sorry for this, stranger.
Talking to Mother Aris again:
Mother Aris: I beg your pardon for it. I cannot spare the hospitality. Even my gardens I've had to abandon... My great-grandmother's flowers have wilted.
Mother Aris: My son had the idea to press the flowers so they would not be gone forever...But as it is, the risk of losing the rest of my family for the drought... I can't bear it!
Mother Aris: ...it may be rude to ask, but...could you ask the nobles of the manor, perhaps? To spare a drop or two extra? I'd be forever indebted to you...
Talking to Merchant Risch at [-1797, 12, -1230]:
Merchant Risch: Whoa. That is positively outlandish dress. You...couldn't be a crown guard, can you be? That's simply so far out of uniform...so are you from the Highlands, maybe?
Merchant Risch: But then, why would you be here? The Festival...isn't that soon over in Espren? Why come all the way over here? I've hardly anything to trade, even.
Merchant Risch: It's the dry season, you know. End of the month, I'm sure you- ehm, wait. Perhaps, since you live atop the dam, that isn't the case? Oh, what I would do for that luxury!

Merchant Risch: Well, to the point- I've nothing to sell but dry herbs. A sad state for our village, when the apothecary cannot even make medicine, but every bit of water has to go towards necessities.
Merchant Risch: We've been receiving less and less. Some generous folks have been sharing, but that does only so far. A glass here and there cannot revitalize my poor garden.
Merchant Risch: If you want to find something more suited to the luxuries you might be used to, perhaps visit the manor over the hill? They do ration out the water to us, as well.

No

The villagers need more water.

Master Oshman: All potable water in the forest comes through us- it is our responsibility to ensure the rations we are given are spread to where it is most needed.
Master Oshman: With the Crown Festival in Espren being about this time, the water must go there! Additionally, with all the new construction recently, there have been more places to ration out to.

Master Oshman: We, too, have taken a smaller share than normal. The village down there, unfortunately, has been the lowest priority for some months now. I have petitioned the Sovereign for more water...

Master Oshman: Hahaha!! There is wisdom I have known from you for so long! What a magnificient idea! It would not be without risk for you, traveler, but we all stand to gain!

Master Oshman: Hayn! Please bring the stranger to the rose, under which we have hidden the key. And good tidings to you!
